items.statement: Expect UAE subsidiary to gradually commence operations and contribute to long-term growth as situation stabilizes
items.quote: As the digital situation continues to stabilize, we expect to gradually commence operations and are confident that the UAE subsidiary will play an important role in expanding our international footprint and contributing to our long-term growth in the coming years.

items.statement: Target indigenous 3D printer by 2028
items.quote: We are also actively working on the 3D printer project as well, so that we have a totally indigenous 3D printer by 2028.

items.statement: Established wholly owned subsidiary in UAE; commercial operations delayed by geopolitical tensions
items.quote: Another important initiative during the year was establishment of our wholly owned subsidiary in the UAE. This investment represents a significant step in strengthening our presence there and enhancing our ability to serve customers across the region more effectively.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 38.6%, PBT margin 36.0%, PAT margin 26.7%; Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 40.87%
items.quote: The company maintained healthy profitability with an EBITDA margin of 38.6%, a PBT margin of 36.0% and a PAT margin of 26.7%.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 margins improved: EBITDA 40.87%, PBT 38.38%, PAT 28.61%
items.quote: Our focus on operational efficiency resulted in further improvement in margins during the quarter. EBITDA margin improved to 40.87%, PBT margin to 38.38% and PAT margin to 28.61%.

items.statement: Export demand improving as international markets stabilize; domestic growth 9%, export growth 17.58% in FY26
items.quote: As several international markets gradually stabilized during the year, we witnessed improving demand across key export geographies, providing renewed momentum to our overseas business.

items.statement: Disinfectant business commercialized with encouraging initial response; 3D printing resins grew 40.5%, 3D printers grew 162%
items.quote: During this year, we started commercialization of our Disinfectant business. This marks the beginning of new vertical that aligns well with the rising demand for hygiene-driven products in the dental and medical settings.

items.statement: Oradox oral care sales down 2% due to US MoCRA and Dubai export disruptions; expect recovery with new product launches
items.quote: We are down by 2%. That is because we couldn't export to the markets in the US. US started a new portal called the Modernization of Cosmetic Regulations Act. And the Dubai Municipality and after the war, we couldn't export substantial amounts.

items.statement: Traditional capacity utilization 67-68% (implies ~INR125 cr revenue at full capacity); new lines (digital, resin, disinfectant) at 18-20%
items.quote: As far as the capacity utilization is concerned, the traditional capacity, the company is working at a capacity utilization of, say, around 67% to 68% of its total installed capacity. And if the company works with total installed capacity, the total turnover would be around, say, INR125 crores.

items.statement: US business grew 37.58% (Axiodent + private label); aggressively participating in US exhibitions
items.quote: There is a significant sale growth of U.S. market. Last -- in comparison to last year, we have grown the business in U.S. 37.58%, which is included with Axiodent and as well as private labeling.

items.statement: OEM for 3-4 large companies; expect to add 2 more in next 2 years
items.quote: We presently OEM for around 3 or 4 big companies. And in the next 2 years, we expect to OEM for another big couple of companies.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% revenue growth in FY27 based on order book and new segments
items.quote: Our target is to achieve 15% to 20% growth in the next year.

items.statement: Vision 2030 targets INR 1,250 crores turnover by 2030
items.quote: Actually, we have yesterday we have uploaded our vision of 2030 with the INR1250 crores turnover in the by 2030 we have made the vision like for next 4 years.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR 60 crores plus; FY27 capex targeted at INR 50 crores plus for vehicles and growth
items.quote: Capex in the financial year '26 is INR60 crores plus and the financial year '27 we are also targeting INR50 crores plus to have our growth engine

items.statement: Added ~100 vehicles in FY26 (CNG, EV, LNG, regular); targeting similar additions in FY27
items.quote: Around 100 plus vehicles we have added last year and same we are targeting in the next financial year.

items.statement: Entered rail-based liquid logistics; targeting 8-10 trains by 2030, scaling tankers from 180 to 1,800
items.quote: We have entered into the last year and we will grow in a fast manner with the 8-10 trains by 2030.

items.statement: Launched 50:50 JV Carbonlite Logistics with Baidyanath Group for LNG vehicle fleet; operations starting within a month
items.quote: So we have made a separate logistics company for that name is Carbonlite Logistics Private Limited. That is 50% subsidiary of the AVG and 50% subsidiary of the Baidyanath Group.

items.statement: Fuel escalation clauses in most contracts pass through diesel price increases within 1-2 weeks
items.quote: Maximum customers' contracts includes the fuel escalation clause. So the all the contracts are having the rider and the percentage of the diesel consumption is mentioned in the contract.

items.statement: Supply chain management/warehousing segment carries good margins but is highly responsible work
items.quote: Yes, it's a good segment because we are managing the warehouse and business movement, inventory movement etc. So margin is there but it is a highly responsible work

items.statement: Q4 FY26 results delayed due to detailed audit reviews and branch consolidation as business has grown
items.quote: The delay was only due to the procedural and audit related requirement. As our business has grown, the audit process has become more detailed and require additional reviews.

items.statement: EV trucks currently viable up to 400-500 km with mid-route charging infra; operating cost lower than diesel despite higher asset cost
items.quote: So we are putting infra in between middle way so that both way this vehicle will run and can go up to 400-500 kilometer.

items.statement: Targeting growth in FMCG, beverage, liquor, steel, cement, pharma, chemical, industrial, solar power sectors
items.quote: Now we are entering into beverage, liquor industry, steel, cement, pharma, chemical, and industrial plant and solar power industries.

items.statement: Signed strategic long-term agreement with existing US tech leader adding $125M+ annual revenue and $650M+ over 6.5 years
items.quote: this is a net new deal which will add roughly about $125 million plus on an annual basis and overall for the period of the contract it will be roughly about $650 million plus over 6.5 years

items.statement: Large deal accretive to revenue and margin from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: yes, it will be accretive - revenue & margin from Q2 onwards

items.statement: Transaction funded via €1.4B committed bridge financing from Barclays at Euribor + 175-250 bps (4.1%-4.8%)
items.quote: This will be completely funded through a committed bridge financing from Barclays. The interest rate is going to be Euribor plus a margin of 175-250 basis point. At this point of time that translates somewhere in in the range of around 4.1%-4.8%

items.statement: Transaction expected to be Cash EPS and Reported EPS accretive in Year 1 excluding transaction expenses
items.quote: The transaction is expected to be Cash EPS accretive as well as Reported EPS accretive in Year 1 if you remove the transaction expenses that will be incurred in the first year

items.statement: Combined entity margins expected to be maintained or improved despite Nagarro's lower EBITDA margin (13.9% vs Persistent 15.6%)
items.quote: we do not believe that the combined entity will be at any significant lower margins than what Persistent has today. And if you look at our track record, we have brought our margins over the last several years up significantly

items.statement: Nagarro BaFin queries reviewed; management confident issues are procedural with no performance impact
items.quote: we have done the diligence on both, we are confident that those issues are more answering BaFin rather than any issues that have any impact on the company's performance

items.statement: Nagarro grew 5%+ constant currency despite management distraction from take-private attempt; expect return to industry-leading growth
items.quote: they have on a constant currency grown more than 5% even in these environments. And keep in mind, if I may say so, they were distracted for some time when they were taking a transaction to take Nagarro private

items.statement: Transaction expected to close Q4 CY2026 or early Q1 CY2027; AGM approval targeted last week of July 2026
items.quote: based on the current anticipation of various regulatory approvals that are expected, we expect this transaction to close sometime towards the Q4 of Calendar Year 2026 or early Q1 of Calendar Year 2027

items.statement: No QIP planned; may explore private equity participation at asset level for deleveraging
items.quote: We don't intend doing any QIP, just to be clear for everyone. We don't intend diluting our stake at this point in time. We may look at if there is a merit in deleveraging by having a private equity or some other participation at the asset level

items.statement: Nagarro management committed to stay; integration phased over 2 years before squeeze-out under German law
items.quote: We'll run the company with them. We'll, over a period of the next two years, look at where we can do the squeeze out. And we are in no hurry to do the squeeze out

items.statement: Nagarro EBIT margin 10.9% CY25, 12.1% Q1 CY26; expect improvement with Persistent rigor and new CFO
items.quote: the EBIT for CY25 for Nagarro is 10.9%. For Q1 CY26, it is 12.1%. And they recently brought on a CFO. For the longest period of time, they had run the CFO organization, not necessarily in the most regimented ways. We have good reasons to believe that this will improve

items.statement: Combined entity: $2.9B+ revenue, 46,000+ employees, 40+ countries, 2nd largest digital engineering player globally
items.quote: Bringing the group together, we will be 46,000+ team members globally spread across 40+ countries. It will be a 2.9 billion dollar+ powerhouse focused on forward-looking technologies

items.statement: ChtrSocial and production arm (Chtr Studios) have highest margin contribution; Represent offers scalability through exclusive creator additions
items.quote: In terms of margins, yes, ChtrSocial and our production arm essentially has the highest margin contribution and we continue to see this going forward as well. In terms of scalability, we see Represent being a good scalable business because the more exclusive creators we add, the more stronger pipeline of business it pr

items.statement: International expansion will be disciplined and lean, avoiding simultaneous multi-market entry and large cost centers; focus on strategic clients with omnipresence
items.quote: Our approach is always going to be disciplined. Like we are not going to enter multiple markets simultaneously and have a huge cost center and burn. We want to be very strategic and have a very lean approach in the way we function these markets.

items.statement: Net worth strengthened to INR70.06 crores post-IPO; focused on disciplined capital allocation, working capital efficiency, and governance
items.quote: The IPO has significantly strengthened our balance sheet with net worth increasing to INR70.06 crores as of financial year 26. We remain focused on disciplined capital allocation, improving working capital efficiency, and maintaining strong governance standards as we scale our business.

items.statement: Revenue mix diversified in FY26: Represent 39.27%, Brand Solutions 36.18%, ChtrSocial 24.55%; domestic 82%, international 18%
items.quote: During financial year '26, Chatterbox Represent contributed 39.27% of revenue, Brand Solutions contributed 36.18% of revenue, ChtrSocial contributed 24.55% of revenue. This balanced revenue mix reduced concentration risk and demonstrated the increasing maturity of our platform model. Geographically, domestic business c

items.statement: Core services order bookings grew 34% YoY to INR 734 crores in FY26, representing a 25% CAGR since FY22
items.quote: Order bookings have grown from INR 299 crores in 2021-2022 to INR 734 crores in 2025-2026, representing a CAGR of approximately 25%.

items.statement: Other OEM segment order bookings grew from INR 162 crores to INR 320 crores
items.quote: We are also seeing strong progress in the other oOEM segment, which is very unique for your company, where order growth has increased from INR 162 crores to around INR 320 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA turned positive to INR 277 crores in FY26 from a loss of INR 251 crores in FY23
items.quote: Our EBITDA, which was once reflected a loss of INR 251 crores in FY 2023, has crossed into positive territory, reaching INR 277 crores in FY 2026.

items.statement: Net worth grew over eight-fold from INR 57 crores in March 2024 to INR 483 crores by March 2026
items.quote: We have seen our Net Worth grow more than eight-fold in just two years, climbing from INR 57 crores in March 2024 to INR 483 crores by March 2026.

items.statement: Liquidity position improved from a deficit of INR 66 crores in 2023 to INR 880 crores by March 2026
items.quote: Similarly, our liquidity position has shifted from a deficit of INR 66 crores in 2023 to a robust INR 880 crores by March 2026, an eighteen -fold improvement in our cash position.

items.statement: Bank guarantee exposure reduced by INR 1,364 crores over two years
items.quote: We have shed INR1,364 crores in bank guarantee exposure over two years, untethering our capital from historical burdens.

items.statement: ICRA credit rating upgraded to BBB+ with stable outlook as of June 2026
items.quote: We have also seen an improvement in our long-term ICRA credit rating to BBB+ with a stable outlook as of June 2026.

items.statement: Proposed demerger of Durgapur business to JSW Energy; shareholders get 10 JSW Energy shares for every 139 GEPIL shares, with no dilution of GEPIL stake
items.quote: For every 139 fully paid equity shares of GE Power India Limited, shareholders will receive 10 fully paid-up equity shares of JSW Energy.

items.statement: Durgapur facility incurred average annual loss of INR 27 crores during 2023-2025 due to underutilization
items.quote: During the last two years, from 2023 to 2025, there has been significant underutilization of its capacity, and this has resulted in an average loss of approximately INR 27 crores per year being booked in GEPIL.

items.statement: Five-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy secures reserved capacity at pre-agreed schedules and pricing
items.quote: A five-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy has been put in place to secure reserved capacity at a pre-agreed schedules and pricing.

items.statement: Full supply chain independence targeted to be achieved very soon to protect order execution and service delivery
items.quote: Concurrent efforts to establish an independent supply chain are progressing very well, with full supply chain independence targeted to be achieved very soon.

items.statement: Updated FY27 semaglutide pen sales guidance to 6-7 million pens due to 3-month supply disruption
items.quote: So the range is between 6 to 7 million for fiscal '27.

items.statement: Previous guidance assumed sales in July-October; now unlikely to supply during those months
items.quote: Before that, we assumed that we will sell during July, August, September, and October, and now, unlikely that we'll do that.

items.statement: Demand remains strong and outstrips supply; no change in demand outlook
items.quote: Nothing has changed. Unfortunately, if we had 15 million, we could supply that also. So, there is no shortage of demand.

items.statement: Validation batch failure due to impurity from API degradation; requires process tweak and re-validation
items.quote: It's the impurity that comes from the API that degraded in the formulation. So you detect it when you do the testing to release the batch.

items.statement: Root cause analysis expected in days to 1-2 weeks; validation and testing to take until end of September
items.quote: I'm assuming that it will take us from days to a week or two to find exactly what we need to correct. And then we need to start to make those batches and to release them.

items.statement: Commercial supply to OneSource expected to resume in October; 6-7M pens assumes supply from November
items.quote: Assuming success, we can resume commercial supply in October to OneSource and then move from there. The 6 to 7 million pens that I mentioned is assuming supply of commercial quantities to the market from November onwards.

items.statement: No equipment change needed; process parameter tweaks expected to control impurity
items.quote: To the best of my understanding, no, it will not require that. It's required to tweak the parameters to control that impurity.

items.statement: No regulatory filing changes or agency notifications required; no product recall as batch never shipped
items.quote: There is no need to inform any agencies. There is no change of specs or change of regulatory filing.

items.statement: Small-scale API production continues but halted for validation; not material quantities
items.quote: There is some small scale that is underway. This will continue to be produced, but it's not much quantities.

items.statement: Canadian market supply impacted for next couple of months due to scale-up validation failure
items.quote: The impact on the Canadian market will be because we will not be able to supply in the next couple of months, so there will be future impact of that.

items.statement: Alloy wheel capacity to reach ~6.2 million by FY27 with ~1.2 million addition
items.quote: Expected ~1.2 million capacity addition in Alloy Wheels aiming to ramp up the total capacity up to ~6.2 million for FY27

items.statement: Net capex of INR 196 crores incurred through FY26 for aluminium wheels and knuckles capacity expansion
items.quote: Net Capex of INR 196 Crs. was incurred through FY26 towards incremental capacity expansion, largely focused on aluminium wheels and aluminium knuckles.

items.statement: Aluminium knuckles capacity scaling from 5 lakh to 11 lakh units by FY27 with 2 leading OEMs
items.quote: Currently, we are working with 2 leading OEM's and as we keep increasing our capacity we would increase our customer base

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 40 bps to 10.7% in Q1 FY27 driven by favourable product mix and cost optimization
items.quote: EBITDA rose 33.0% YoY, with margin expanding by 40 bps to 10.7%. The margin improvement reflects a favourable product mix, cost optimization initiatives, and a rising share of premium products in the portfolio.

items.statement: Exports faced tariff-related disruptions but showing recovery from June 2026
items.quote: exports began showing signs of recovery in June as tariff-related disruptions normalized — a potential tailwind for coming quarters.

items.statement: FY27 interest cost ~INR 250-260 crore, depreciation ~INR 425-450 crore (pro-rata for 500 MW commissioning)
items.quote: '26, '27, is a projected figure. I cannot give you the exact numbers, but roughly interest would be around 250 to 260 crores and depreciation would be around 425 to 450 crores. This is a rough I am telling you.

items.statement: 750 MW lignite thermal plant capex ~INR 6,000-7,000 crore, phased over 2027-2033
items.quote: Around INR6,500 crores to INR7,000 crores would be required for thermal capex capacity of 750, it would be around --yes, we are expecting INR6,000 crores capex towards the thermal of 750.

items.statement: 500 MW Khavda solar: phased commissioning post-monsoon, first 200 MW then 200+100 MW in next months
items.quote: Basically, we are at a very advanced stage of commissioning in stage manner and we are just waiting for the power evacuation facility being getting ready by CTUIL. I think post-monsoon they will be ready, so we may be able to commission the first phase of 200 megawatt and followed by another 200, 100 megawatts in next

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin ~40%+ expected as solar share increases
items.quote: EBITDA, I have already given the calculation. You can work further out, it would be the full capacity of 600 capex, INR600 commissioning, '26, '27, EBITDA would be around INR950 crores --INR940 crores roughly over. So you can work out the percentage.

items.statement: Khavda solar tariff INR 2.73/unit fixed under PPA with GUVNL for 25 years
items.quote: See, basically revenue is 2. 73 per unit. This basically you have to calculate separately, that is CUF multiplied by 24 hours multiplied by 12 months by capacity, you will get the million units and then you have to multiply by the revenue, you will get the revenue.

items.statement: No evacuation issue for 600 MW Khavda; full allocation since Nov 2025. 500 MW awaiting CTUIL evacuation readiness post-monsoon
items.quote: We have been given the full allocation in November 2025 and we are evacuating the full load from the 600 MW Khavda. That is why our CUF is 33%. So as such, we don't foresee any issue from GIPCL per se and there is any evacuation issue.

items.statement: Quarterly earnings calls to continue regularly; presentations to be provided
items.quote: Yes, Yes. We will definitely, we have understood your requirement and we will definitely come to you on regular basis so that you will get the regular updates as may be required.

items.statement: Retained FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of 1% to 4% and EBIT margin guidance of 17.5% to 18.5%
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are retaining our guidance of 1% to 4% and margin guidance of 17.5% to 18.5% for FY27. The guidance is organic growth guidance and does not include acquisitions including Jaspersoft.

items.statement: Q1 net new TCV bookings of $2.4 billion, highest ever Q1 bookings, excluding mega deal signed in early July
items.quote: Our net new TCV booking for the quarter was $2.4 billion, highest ever Q1 bookings. This excludes the recent mega deal that we announced, which was signed in early July and not in Q1.

items.statement: Q1 EBIT margin at 16.9%, up 39 bps QoQ and 56 bps YoY; adjusted for restructuring, margin at 17.5% vs 17.7% prior quarter
items.quote: Our operating margins stood at 16.9%, an improvement of 39 basis points QoQ and an increase of 56 basis points YoY.

items.statement: Strategic investment of up to INR 3,500 crores for AI datacenter business with potential to scale to 50 MW capacity
items.quote: In this regard, we will make a strategic investment of up to INR3,500 crores and with the potential to scale to 50 megawatts of capacity.

items.statement: Advanced AI revenue reached $171 million, growing 10.6% QoQ and 62.1% YoY
items.quote: Advanced AI revenue for the quarter stood at $171 million, marking 10.6% QoQ and 62.1% YoY growth.

items.statement: Pipeline remains healthy with strong sustained growth in AI-native and AI-amplified services; AI-disrupted services continue to be optimized
items.quote: Our pipeline remains healthy. Looking at the broader market trends, we are seeing a clear divergence across different segments of the AI landscape. On one side, we are seeing strong sustained growth both in AI-native and AI-amplified services.

items.statement: Mega deal transition starts in a couple of months, steady state by April 2027, negligible revenue impact in FY27
items.quote: On the mega deal win, the transition is expected to start in a couple of months, and the steady state is expected to be reached only in April of 2027, so which is coming in the next financial year. It will have negligible impact to our revenue in this financial year.

items.statement: AI datacenter investment to be funded via mix of partner arrangements, committed capacity, equity and debt; not at expense of payout policy
items.quote: We are not putting this entire investment in the balance sheet in a single year. We are not funding it at the expense of our stated payout policy. We will provide more details as we progress.

items.statement: Token costs may drop but overall consumption will rise; tiered architecture with SLMs and policy gateway becoming prevalent enterprise model
items.quote: Token costs could drop, but however the overall consumption of tokens will go up, so total cost will also go up. So, you need to build a more economic model, which is where our strategy of building a tiered approach with smaller models within the enterprise.

items.statement: Jaspersoft acquisition completed early July; expected to contribute $10-15 million per quarter in FY27 with seasonality
items.quote: We're still working on it, Vibhor. I think we will possibly give maybe $10 to $15 million per quarter in that range, but there's a seasonality involved, so it's going to be that range, I think.

items.statement: CTG acquisition expected to close later in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We expect that to be closed maybe later part of this quarter, but yes, I think that's also on the card. Hopefully this quarter only, we don't know the exact details, but maybe towards the later part of this quarter, that will also get closed.

items.statement: Medium-term margin band of 18-19% not committed; FY28 guidance to be given next year; current focus on FY27 17.5-18.5% guidance including 40-50 bps restructuring impact
items.quote: As regard maybe the longer term, the medium-term horizon of around FY28, we will, give that guidance at an appropriate time when we give guidance for FY28 next year. At this stage, time I would just like to focus on this year's margin guidance, which is 17.5% to 18.5%.

items.statement: ER&D decline in Tech and Telecom verticals due to discretionary cuts at two large US telcos and high base effect
items.quote: The decline in ER&D was in Tech and Telecom, Media and Entertainment verticals. And we did call out that we had some sharp cuts in discretionary spending in two large US telcos.

items.statement: AI Force deployed across 92 client accounts; 23 industry AI solutions; 1,000+ AI engagements delivered in AI Labs
items.quote: AI Force is now deployed across 92 distinct client accounts, enabling organizations to realize the benefits of AI within existing engagements at scale.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 TCV of $9.5 billion including $800M SKF mega deal and other net-new AI-led deals
items.quote: We delivered a TCV of $9.5 billion , including net new AI-led business transformation deals such as, US$ 800 million mega deal with SKF; 6th mega deal win in the last 5 quarters

items.statement: Operating margin 24% in Q1 FY27, down 130 bps QoQ due to 170 bps wage hike impact, partly offset by 40 bps currency benefit and efficiencies
items.quote: Operating margin for the quarter was 24%, declining 130 bps sequentially. In Q1, we rolled out annual increments for our global workforce, which impacted margins by 170 bps.

items.statement: Target to exit at 25%+ operating margin and strive to achieve it sooner rather than later
items.quote: We want to exit at 25% plus and strive to achieve it sooner rather than later.

items.statement: Annualized AI services revenue reached $2.6 billion, up 13.6% QoQ
items.quote: At the end of Q1 FY27, it stands at $2.6 billion in annualized revenue, which is up 13.6% QoQ.

items.statement: BFSI, Tech Services, Manufacturing, Life Sciences expected to turn around in Q2; Consumer Business recovery tied to geopolitical sentiment
items.quote: BFSI, we are looking good. Manufacturing, we believe will turn around in Q2, life sciences could turn around in Q2, tech services will continue to grow. We are quite optimistic about these.

items.statement: Investing in AI capabilities, talent transformation, partner ecosystems, platforms, domain solutions, and go-to-market capacity
items.quote: We are investing in AI capabilities, talent transformation, partner ecosystems, platforms, domain solutions, and go-to-market capacity.

items.statement: Launched TCS SovereignSecure Cloud for Europe addressing demand for compliance, sovereign, and AI-ready cloud infrastructure
items.quote: We also launched TCS SovereignSecure Cloud TM for Europe , directly addressing rising demand from governments and regulated enterprises for compliance, sovereign, and AI-ready cloud infrastructure.

items.statement: Strong client additions maintained across $10M+, $5M+, and $1M+ revenue bands sequentially
items.quote: We maintained healthy client additions across $10 million+, $5 million+, and $1 million+ revenue bands on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Management aspires to deliver consistent double-digit to low-teens revenue growth over the medium to long term, but refuses to provide quarterly or annual guidance.
items.quote: From a slightly longer term, medium to longer term perspective, our aspiration is to deliver consistent year-on-year double-digit growth, and hence that comment needs to be seen in that light, rather than as to a guidance of what the next quarter growth number would be.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to remain under pressure in Q2 FY27, then sequentially ease in Q3 and Q4. EBITDA margin aspiration is low to mid-20s.
items.period: Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: I think margins at a gross margin level will continue to remain, in a tough zone in quarter two and then they will expect to sequentially ease over quarter three and four.

items.statement: Selective price increases and MLH reductions taken to counter raw material inflation; no further pricing actions planned.
items.quote: We don't have any pricing actions planned in. Operating leverage, we will continue to try and run the company as efficiently as we can.

items.statement: High-cost inventory remains in the system; spot prices for petroleum-linked materials and edible oils expected to cool sequentially over the next few months.
items.quote: We do have high-cost inventory in our system and the spot prices are also expected to cool sequentially over the next few months.

items.statement: ADHO delivered low-teen volume growth on MLH-adjusted basis, led by small packs and sachets across all channels.
items.quote: We have delivered a low teen volume growth on an MLH adjusted basis. Just like previous year and quarter, this growth came back on across of, you know, all the pack groups and all the channels.

items.statement: Rural business grew in line with urban; general trade and organized trade (ex-institutional) both grew in strong 20s.
items.quote: The current quarter saw a continued momentum in our general trade channel, which grew in line with organized trade with both channels delivering growth in strong 20s.

items.statement: Growth portfolio (non-ADHO) grew high single-digit sequentially despite coconut value deflation; Banjara's revamp underway with pilots for disruptive growth.
items.quote: On the growth portfolio, which is a cluster of smaller brands, non-ADHO brands, which we have a high growth aspiration against, performed well in the quarter, with the overall portfolio growing high single-digit sequentially against the previous quarter and improving its run rate.

items.statement: Project Aarohan expanding direct distribution in four new states; delivers 200-300 bps one-time growth delta, with multi-year benefits from outlet additions.
items.quote: Aarohan delivers anywhere around a 200 to 300 basis point delta as a one-time when we are executing because of the change of the mix.

items.statement: Execution risk (consistent market share gains, distribution expansion, consumer acquisition) is the single largest risk to sustaining growth.
items.quote: So us being able to consistently gain share, gain more consumers, you know, take our product and distribute it to more outlets is all execution and hence execution risk will remain the single largest risk.

items.statement: Advertising spend to remain consistent at historical 15-16% of revenue; not an area for cost squeezing.
items.quote: We've been operating on number if you look at our historical averages have been around 15% to 16%. We will we will try and operate in that zone.

items.statement: International business rebounded strongly across key markets (Nepal, Bangladesh, MENA, Rest of World) with double-digit growth and margin improvement.
items.quote: Our key markets of Nepal and Bangladesh demonstrated continued double-digit growth and margin improvement. MENA, which was challenged last year, delivered a very strong growth and rest of world, which witnessed tariff and other related disruptions last year, also rebounded back very strongly.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% AUM CAGR over next 3-4 years driven by 10-12% mark-to-market returns and 1% monthly net sales (INR1,060 cr/month on current base).
items.quote: So basically a 20%, 25% AUM growth, 10%, 12% coming from mark-to-market and 10%, 12% coming from 1% per month of net sale coming from -- if my AUM is INR 1,06,000 crores, internally, we discussed that we need to take a single on every ball. INR1,060 crores will be my implied net sale target for that month.

items.statement: Aims to reach 4% market share in mutual fund Category II (equity-oriented) over 8-10 years, implying INR6 lakh crore AUM if industry grows to INR1.5 lakh crore at 10% CAGR.
items.value: 4% market share; INR6 lakh cr AUM
items.quote: Our desire is to take it to 4%. To take it to 4%, we projected what the Category II of the mutual fund industry would be after 10 years. items.quote: So it's really $250,000 is what the LRS limit is. But depending on like what you're doing, there are different limits may apply.

items.statement: FCNR(B) programme in early stages; leveraging international branches and partners; raising bonds; no specific target or leverage disclosed; expect momentum to pick up over next couple of months
items.quote: We will be raising bonds. We do expect the momentum to pick up as we go along and, of course, we are committed to make this initiative of RBI, a success.

items.statement: Overseas borrowing programme of $2.5 billion approved; timing and split under RBI concessional swap window to evolve over next two months; no specific acquisition financing plans
items.quote: We are looking at various options, and we have taken this enabling approval. So, we will see how it goes. But there is nothing specific to the timing as such.

items.statement: Rural portfolio grew 35.4% YoY; substantial portion is gold loans; bank focuses on customer relationships over product-level targets
items.quote: The overall rural portfolio has grown by 35% year-on-year. And, from our perspective, gold loan is just a product. We are focussed more on the customer.

items.statement: AI investment focused on governance, long-term value creation, and customer journey simplification; no material impact on headcount expected; cost-benefit continuously calibrated
items.quote: Because these are early days in AI. As I did mention, we have calibrated our approach. We look at cost, we look at the risk, and we look at the benefits. Our final objective is to make the journeys of our customers simpler.

items.statement: ECL implementation effective April 1, 2027; no material ongoing impact expected; adequate provisions for transition period
items.quote: ECL is effective from 1st of April next year. Those are the numbers that we will start sharing from a next year basis. At this point of time, we do not see a material impact on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: LCR at 124% in Q1-2027 vs 128% year-ago; surplus SLR not disclosed; NRI deposit share not disclosed but expected to rise with FCNR(B) flows
items.quote: I think the LCR for the quarter, which is really the operative liquidity metric, was at 124%.

items.statement: Loan growth momentum continues to be strong; average loan growth YoY will be somewhat lower than Q1's 19.6% due to base effects but incremental momentum remains strong
items.quote: Average loan growth on a year-on-year basis will be somewhat lower, but as I mentioned earlier, higher loan growth this quarter is reflective of the increase in loan growth in the system and both the banks and the system is off the base of Q1 of last year. So, there could be some base effect, but incremental momentum c

items.statement: NIM expected to remain range-bound assuming no policy rate changes; FCNR(B) mobilization may have some NIM impact over time but is earnings positive
items.quote: Based on current conditions and assuming no policy rate movements, I would say it should be range bound. As we go along, we'll also have to factor in sort of the impact of the FCNR deposit mobilization and the related leverage where there could be some impact on margins, but that is something that will happen over a pe

items.statement: FCNR(B) all-in cost after hedging estimated at 6.30-6.40%, competitive vs wholesale rates; mobilization early days, will play out over 8-10 weeks
items.quote: From a cost effectiveness perspective, 6%. If you look at kind of the all-in cost after hedging the coupon, etc., it will be somewhere maybe 6.30-6.40%, which is, of course, lower than wholesale rates and it will be competitive compared to the wholesale rates.

items.statement: Corporate loan growth driven by bond market shift, working capital utilization, and liquidity buffering; no meaningful increase in fresh capex proposals seen
items.quote: Part of it is a shift from bond markets, part of it is working capital utilization, part of it may be corporates taking on some borrowings and just maintaining some liquidity buffers as they also want to be sort of have greater resilience in this uncertain environment.

items.statement: Agri portfolio remediation and validation process ongoing; no timeline given for provision write-back; ECL transition impact on net worth expected to be absorbed by provisioning buffers
items.quote: We just want to make sure that whatever we have done is correct and signed off and validated before we discuss a write-back of the provision. So, we are in the process and will hopefully work it out over the next few months, but I don't want to give a timeline.

items.statement: Normalized credit cost around 50 bps vs reported 32 bps in Q1; one-off recovery from NARCL-sold asset in quarter
items.quote: From a credit cost perspective, the reported of 32 basis points, and as we always say, a more normalised level, adjusting for chunky recoveries would be around 50 bps, and that is where it stays.

items.statement: Personal loans grew 12.9% YoY and 4% sequentially; credit cards declined 1.9% YoY and 1.7% sequentially due to lower revolver rates
items.quote: PL has picked up quite a bit actually, 12% year-on-year and 4% sequential growth. I think it's after a long time that we are seeing those kinds of numbers. Cards, the revolver rates are lower. So that is impacting the book growth.

items.statement: Retail portfolio stable; no change in savings inflows; unsecured NPA additions improved YoY; business banking granular and secured, comfortable growing despite macro risks
items.quote: No, we have not seen any change actually. In terms of inflows into the savings, etc., they are quite stable. We've not seen any change. And as you can see, the performance of the retail portfolio has only improved.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth for FY27
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting double-digit volume growth this year.

items.statement: INR17,000 crores capex for capacity expansion over next 2-2.5 years to reach 242M tons consolidated capacity
items.quote: Projects under execution for capacity growth are backed by a capex of about INR17,000 crores in the next 2 to 2.5 years.

items.statement: Grey cement capacity to reach 212.7M tons by end FY27 and 235M tons by March 2028
items.quote: We'll take our consolidated capacity beyond 242 million tons with grey cement capacity to reach 212.7 million tons by the end of fiscal '27 and further balance to be completed in the next year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton steady above INR1,200; absorbed fuel cost shock while growing absolute EBITDA 12%
items.quote: Operating EBITDA per ton has been steady above INR1,200 this quarter as well.

items.statement: India Cements EBITDA per ton improved from INR386 (Q2FY26) to INR603 (Q1FY27); target INR1,000 by Q4 FY28
items.quote: EBITDA of INR1,000 per ton for India Cements remains very much in sight with the full benefit of the capex program flowing through the P&L from Q4 fiscal '28.

items.statement: All-India exit prices improved through June; industry expects prices to hold steady through monsoon quarter
items.quote: Industry expects prices to hold broadly steady through the monsoon quarter due to the impact of increase in costs, which, frankly, is a constructive outcome for this time of year.

items.statement: Sequential cost increase of INR130-140 per ton expected in Q2 FY27 from fuel, maintenance and operating deleverage
items.quote: I would expect the cost to go up by INR130 to INR140 per ton, all put together.

items.statement: Demand pipeline rich across infrastructure, housing, urban real estate; East region structural upcycle over 2-4 years
items.quote: East will witness good demand upcycle.

items.statement: Retail share ~65-66% of sales; brand premiumization driving blended realizations; RMC only 3.5% of sales
items.quote: 65% to 66% would be retail. If I marry this data point to India as a whole, as the demography of India, the spending habits of India, if you look at the number of cities, which are more than 1 million population, today, we have 63 cities which will reach to 71 cities by 2030.

items.statement: West Asia conflict creating fuel cost volatility; insurance premiums up 4-5% for ocean routes; industrial diesel up 50% impacting limestone raising cost
items.quote: insurance premiums have gone up to 4% -5% for the ocean route as compared to less than 1%. So that is the kind of differences which the war is creating.

items.statement: All growth capex and cost improvement initiatives funded through internal accruals; net debt/EBITDA 0.87x, target below 1x for FY27
items.quote: We had started the year with a net debt EBITDA of 0.94 and the quarter, we have ended with 0.87x net debt to EBITDA. Our belief is, and we are confident that this year also, we'll end the net debt to EBITDA below 1x.

items.statement: Cables & Wires business on track for Q3 FY27 launch; INR1,800 crores approved, INR888 crores spent/committed
items.quote: We reaffirm commissioning and product launch in Q3 fiscal '27, October - December '26 quarter, precisely as committed to you when we announced this investment.

items.statement: Green power at 1,897 MW (47% of power needs); targeting 2.5-3 GW shortly; India Cements green power to reach 86% by FY28
items.quote: We believe we will reach anywhere between 2.5 to 3 gigawatts very shortly.

items.statement: Industry volume growth estimated at 7-8% for Q1 FY27; UltraTech grew 13.1% domestic grey cement volumes
items.quote: Too early, but anywhere between 7% to 8%. We want to see some more results. But our marketing intel says it should be around 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance 11-12%, advances growth 14-16% for FY27
items.quote: Bank had released guidance about composition of our advances, RAM and corporate, and our guidance to market towards the resources side, 11% to 12% in deposit growth and 14% to 16% in advances growth.

items.statement: NIM guidance 3% and above, ROA 1% and above maintained
items.quote: I have given guidance, NIM will be 3% and above and still we are maintaining. ROA 1% and above, that also we have maintained and remain 1% and above.

items.statement: RAM to Corporate credit ratio guidance 65:35 plus-minus 5%
items.quote: RAM to Corporate Credit ratio stands at 68:32, aligning with our guidance ratio of 65:35 plus-minus 5%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target reduction by 1.5-1.6% in coming year
items.quote: We are sure that in coming year, Bank will reduce cost-to-income ratio by 1.5% to 1.6%.

items.statement: Yield on advances expected to reach 8% by March 2027 from current 7.89%
items.quote: So there, we expect that our yield will improve from 7.89% to anywhere between 8%, we are thinking that as of March '27, we will reach up to 8%.

items.statement: Undisbursed advances approximately ₹5,000 crores
items.quote: Undisbursed advances is approximately ₹5,000 crores.

items.statement: NIM at 3.06% in Q1 FY27, above 3% guidance
items.quote: Net interest margin is above 3%, aligning with our guidance to the market. It is 3.06%.

items.statement: Cost of deposits improved to 4.60%, down 33 bps YoY, term deposits mostly repriced
items.quote: Cost of deposit improved to 4.60% that is 33 basis point improvement registered. So, cost of deposit has stabilized.

items.statement: ECL provisions ₹1,525 crores made out of ₹4,500-5,000 crores total requirement, 80 bps CRAR impact if fully provided
items.quote: Under ECL, we have already made provisions of Stage 1 and Stage 2 for ₹1,525 crores out of approximately total requirement of ₹4,500 crores to ₹5,000 crores.

items.statement: Slippage ratio improved to 0.29% (6 bps better), 0.19% excluding KCC slippages
items.quote: Slippage ratio stood at 0.29% for this quarter and where we can mark an improvement of 6 basis points.

items.statement: No capital raise planned despite Board approval for ₹7,000 crores, CRAR 18.28% sufficient for growth
items.quote: We already have CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% In that way, we are having enough capital, and we don't need capital to support our growth guidance.

name: Nippon Life India Asset Management Ltd

items.statement: Expect overall operating expenses (ex-ESOP and one-offs) to grow 18-20% for next 6-8 quarters due to continued investment in technology and brand
items.quote: We will keep on investing for some time because we think that there is a requirement to do investment on these. So, maybe for six to eight quarters we will keep on investing and see growth in the range of 18% to 20% on overall operating expenses (ex-ESOP and one-offs).

items.statement: Blended yield expected to drop 1-2 basis points YoY due to pricing pressure as equity AUM scales up
items.quote: We continue to think that due to this pricing this thing, yield may drop on equity as the size goes up, which will be 1 to 2 basis on YoY on blended yield.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 yields: equity 54 bps ex-arbitrage (53 bps with), debt 25 bps, liquid 12 bps, ETF 25 bps; overall blended yield flat QoQ at 38 bps
items.quote: Yes, Prayesh, the yields are -- equity is 54 basis ex of arbitrage, debt is 25 basis, liquid is 12 basis, and ETF as a category is 25 basis. Overall, our yield remained constant at 38 basis QoQ.

items.statement: Investing in technology, brand, and digital platform; other expenses up 17% QoQ; will continue for 6-8 quarters
items.quote: We continue to invest on the digital and brand and technology side. So, the other expense increase is mainly due to that, we are investing in the technology, brand activities and on the digital platform.

items.statement: Voluntary restrictions on bullion ETF inflows >INR 25 cr and gold fund >INR 10 lakh remain; may be lifted sooner than later as environment improves
items.quote: And to your question on when we will open it, it will be difficult to give a date or this thing, but looking at the overall environment, good thing is because this was voluntarily done by the company. We continuously keep evaluating and may sooner than later open it.

items.statement: SIF products in state of readiness; will launch differentiated products when approved; JV with DWS for AIF business (40% stake) awaiting regulatory approvals
items.quote: Regarding SIF, as my colleague Saugata mentioned earlier, we're in a state of readiness. Rather than getting into the nitty-gritty of what stage we are at with the product and all, we are overall in a state of readiness. We remain very optimistic on this space.

items.statement: ESOP expense ~INR 13-14 cr in Q1 FY27; expected ~INR 60 cr for full FY27, declining YoY
items.quote: Yes, so the ESOP expense for the quarter is around INR 13-14 crores and over the period it should be in the range of around INR 60 crores odd that is for the year FY27.

items.statement: TER changes fully passed through to distributors via commission alignment; no impact on financials
items.quote: On the pass through of the TER changes which has happened, we have mostly passed on everything to the distributors through the commission alignment and there is no impact per se on the financials.

items.statement: Expects growth acceleration from Q2 FY27 onwards after Q1 moderation due to market volatility
items.quote: I do believe that from these quarters on, we can see an acceleration in growth.

items.statement: Raised INR 468 crore via rights issue in April 2026; deployed INR 227 crore for exchange margin, INR 150 crore for loan repayment, INR 88 crore for general corporate purposes
items.quote: We raised about INR 468 crores in the rights issue as capital in the month of April, which is strengthened the balance sheet and which we're going to use for obviously continued investment in the product and tech talent for improving and taking a product to the next level plus partnerships and plus growth marketing.

items.statement: Focused on meaningful improvements in unit economics to improve margin and overall PAT; aims to achieve operating leverage quickly as a tech platform
items.quote: We're looking to also make meaningful improvements in our unit economics to improve our margin and overall PAT. The idea is to get to a state very quickly where we have operating leverage from it because, at the heart of it, we are a tech platform.

items.statement: Long-term opportunity in Indian capital markets remains robust; retail participation still in early innings with financialization driving growth
items.quote: The long-term opportunity in the Indian market is remains very robust, even though past few months have been volatile or the past year has been a little choppy. But we think Indian capital markets, the journey of retail trade is still in early innings.

items.statement: Average client funding book (MTF + T+5) at INR 422 crore, up 3% QoQ; mutual fund AUM at INR 2,073 crore, up 18% QoQ
items.quote: Our average client funding book, which includes both MTF and the T +5 offering, which is also a related offering, now stands at I mean, for the last quarter stands at now it's much higher, but it stands at INR 422 crore, which was an increase of 3% QoQ.

items.statement: T+5 funding interest rate starts at 0.045% per day; MTF funding limits increased to INR 25 crore
items.quote: We've expanded the T+5 offering, which is essentially where you can hold the stock for five days, to 2,500 eligible scrips, with interest rates starting at 0.045% per day.

items.statement: F&O regulatory changes in October 2024 caused industry-wide moderation; Q1 saw slight dip in F&O ADTO but growth in cash ADTO
items.quote: After the F&O changes came in the month of October '24, there was a moderation across the board. On players which were, you know, who are major source of revenue from F&O, and then a lot of them are diversified.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR 468 crore completed in April 2026; net worth now north of INR 1,100 crore
items.quote: We raised about INR 468 crores in the rights issue as capital in the month of April, which is strengthened the balance sheet.

items.statement: Actively evaluating AI partnerships to accelerate AI journey for internal productivity and customer-facing features; selectively evaluating inorganic opportunities for talent and speed
items.quote: We are also very actively looking at the right partnerships in the AI ecosystem to accelerate our AI journey, both within the company internally for improving productivity unleashing creative forces, but also, more importantly, for our customers.

items.statement: Completely revamped platform in beta testing with encouraging early results; multiple platform upgrades moving to production in next few months
items.quote: There are multiple platform upgrades, complete revamp platform, which is happening. And in our early beta-stage testing, we've seen very, very encouraging results.

items.statement: No near-term plans for third-party distribution beyond mutual funds; focus remains on core platform and adjacent products like MTF and potential LAS
items.quote: In the very near future, no. But, in the mid to long term, we potentially might see if there are synergies to be exploited and to be leveraged, we will do it.

items.statement: Long-term growth target of 18%-20% annually, no formal FY27 guidance given
items.quote: we have been growing at 18%-20% since last 10-15 years and we should be able to maintain our growth rates in long-term growth rates around this level in future also

items.statement: New plant commissioning planned for September 2026 with INR45 crore capex, meaningful revenue from Q4 FY27
items.quote: we are planning to commission the plant in September. So that is the status

items.statement: Order book at INR811 crores as of June 30, 2026, up ~10% YoY but slowed due to high aluminium prices
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, our order book stands at INR811 crores providing strong revenue visibility

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.9% in Q1 FY27 from better mix and cost discipline
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 10.9% reflecting enhanced operational efficiency

items.statement: Variable price contracts pass through raw material changes; fixed price contracts hedge by booking raw material at order time
items.quote: in variable price contract, we have a clause built in for price variation. So, whatever is the increase or decrease in input cost for the cable, we pass it on to our customers

items.statement: Strong demand visibility from power T&D, renewables, industrial sectors and exports; volume growth 5-6% in Q1 due to high base and price volatility
items.quote: 5% to 6% is our volume growth and balance is large part of it is kind of derived by the price growth of aluminium

items.statement: Solar cables ~20% of revenue, expected to grow 25-30% annually for 3-4 years; HV cables 68%, LV 30%, conductor 2% in Q1
items.quote: Our solar cable revenue has been around 20% in Q1 and on the full year basis also I think it should remain in the similar range

items.statement: Customers delaying orders due to high aluminium prices; order cycles shortening, only near-term orders being placed
items.quote: customers are not giving us far-fetched orders now-a-days because nobody wants to lock in the price at such elevated levels

items.statement: Entered US market in Q1 FY27 via distribution model; US contributed ~15% of exports; HV/LV/MV cables licensed
items.quote: this quarter we finally entered into the US market. We started our first supply to the US market

items.statement: Existing capacity utilization at ~85%; new plant targets 80-85% utilization by end FY28
items.quote: our existing capacity we are working on an 85% around capacity utilization levels

items.statement: HTLS conductor and data center cables identified as future growth areas; capex largely fungible with existing machinery
items.quote: both these areas, the HTLS conductors as well as data center cables, both are futuristic investment and we believe that in next three, four years, five years, they should be a good market

items.statement: Debt increased due to 25-30% higher inventory value from rising raw material prices, not volume increase
items.quote: the inventory carrying value has gone up because of the increasing raw material prices. So, though the quantity of inventory is same, but the value of the inventory has gone up by 25%, 30%

items.statement: Building wire entry limited to B2B segment only, avoiding competitive B2C distribution
items.quote: We just want to be into the B2B segment which has been our DNA as a company, and it is just an additional product for us in the similar segment

items.statement: Railway signaling segment temporarily held back due to margin pressure and competition; capacity fungible for other products
items.quote: in the railway signaling segment of our business, we were not able to get our desired margins and there was lot of competition. So, we have temporarily held back that segment

items.statement: Full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 12-15%
items.quote: broadly, the revenue guidance for the full year will remain between 12 and 15 percentage, like we've discussed in the last interactions as well.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin expected to improve over FY26
items.quote: on the EBITDA margins, you should be able to expect better than what we closed last year. I'm talking about the full year in perspective.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 gross margin target maintained at current levels despite cost pressures
items.quote: We aim to maintain the same gross margins till the end of the year.

items.statement: Targeting net retail space addition of ~100,000 sq ft in FY27, with potential for 10,000-15,000 sq ft extra in Q4
items.quote: Looking ahead, we are targeting a net retail space addition of approximately 1,00,000 square feet for this financial year.

items.statement: Added ~30,000 sq ft in Q1 FY27 across 2 Kalamandir stores in Karnataka, total footprint now ~814,000 sq ft across 83 stores
items.quote: We continued our expansion journey, adding approximately 30,000 square feet of retail space during the quarter, taking our total store count to 83.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin held near 42% despite challenging environment; EBITDA margin declined ~1% due to same-store sales degrowth
items.quote: I'm happy to report that gross margins held up well, remaining close to 42% despite the challenging environment

items.statement: Q1 FY27 same-store sales degrowth of 7.5-7.8% driven by Adhik Maas and weak discretionary demand; demand slowly improving post-Adhik Maas
items.quote: The same-store sales saw a degrowth of up to 7.5% during the quarter, reflecting the cautious demand environment I just spoke about.

items.statement: Poor rainfall in core markets (AP, Telangana, Karnataka) may impact agricultural income and demand in Q2-Q3; geopolitical factors and rising fuel/dye costs also cited as risks
items.quote: I personally believe that there will be some impact, but it's tricky to quantify how much exactly it will.

items.statement: Innerwear category in KLM Fashion Mall showing ~20% YoY growth; fashion jewellery rollout started in new Kalamandir stores and KLM
items.quote: With respect to innerwear, I think month-on-month, Y-o-Y, it is showing growth. We are expecting a 20% growth compared to last year in the innerwear category.

items.statement: Rationalizing 1 underperforming KLM Fashion Mall store in Telangana (from 19 to 18 stores); monitoring 1 more store for potential closure
items.quote: As part of our ongoing efforts, we have planned to rationalize 1 KLM Fashion Mall store that has shown sustained degrowth despite dedicated efforts towards revival

items.statement: Planning entry into Maharashtra (Pune) and exploring Kerala in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28
items.quote: in quarter 4 or early quarter 1 of next financial year, in that time is where our entry to the new state will be. We are looking at closing down on final location of one in Pune in Maharashtra.

items.statement: IPO proceeds for warehouse under due diligence; target to complete deal by end of September 2026
items.quote: Hopefully, we should be able to complete the deal by the end of September. And then that particular part of the amount for warehouse will be spent at that point of time.

items.statement: FY27 SSSG target of 2-3% positive growth implied by 15% revenue guidance, assuming no major consumption weakening
items.quote: That will put you around close to SSSG growth number on the positive SSSG and not a negative number.

items.statement: CFO indicates normalized SSSG improvement of 3-4% covers inflation and cost increases; store maturity and new store productivity also drive growth
items.quote: Normally, we consider an improvement of approximately 3% to 4% on SSSG, which will cover the inflation rate plus any kind of increase in cost.

items.statement: Confident of delivering 20%+ year-on-year EBITDA and revenue growth for FY27 despite heavy H1 seat additions
items.quote: we 100% feel very confident that, you know, even as the expansion rolls out and the year rolls out, we will definitely meet the guidance of 20% plus EBITDA growth and sort of earnings sorry, revenue and EBITDA growth of, you know, over 20%.

items.statement: Total contracted capacity ~12 million sq ft (179,000 desks) including signed leases and LOIs of 2.9 million sq ft; 32% capacity growth, 44,000 desks locked in
items.quote: We operate 9.1 million square foot today, add signed leases and LOIs of another 2.9 million, and total contracted capacity is about 12 million square foot, about 179,000 desks. That's a 32% capacity growth and nearly 44,000 desks that are already locked in.

items.statement: Q1 desk sales 12,700 (+28% YoY); April record 7,500 desks; 52% sales to existing members; pricing multiples held steady, no discounting
items.quote: We sold about 12,700 desks this quarter, which is up 28% year-over-year. April was our single biggest sales month with about 7,500 desks, and we did this without discounting, pricing multiples held steadily through the year.

items.statement: Locked-in future revenue INR3,363 crores (+60% YoY) vs locked-in rent obligations +30% YoY; contracted revenue growing 2x contracted cost; 4.7x revenue per rupee of new rent
items.quote: future revenue of our members that our members have already signed up for stands at about INR3,363 crores, which is up 60% from INR2,105 crores last year. Locked-in rent obligations only grew 30% in the same period. So contracted revenue is growing twice as fast as contracted cost. For every rupee of new rent that we c

items.statement: Net debt down 89% YoY to INR31.6 crores; cash INR371 crores; net debt/EBITDA 0.06x; borrowing cost 8.5% (from 10.4%); rating upgraded to A+ from A-
items.quote: Net debt is INR31.6 crores, down 89% from INR297 crores a year ago, against INR371 crores of cash on hand. Net debt to EBITDA is 0.06x, cost of borrowing is down from 10.4% to 8.5%, and our rating moved from an A- to an A+ over the year.

items.statement: Targeting profit growth at or above balance sheet growth over the longer term
items.quote: We do think that in the longer term that the profit growth should be at or above the balance sheet growth. Yes, that's still in our plans and that's how we approach.

items.statement: Targeting retail asset mix of 60% from current 52% to mirror India's consumption GDP share
items.quote: Today we are at a 52% retail mix. At our kind of an experience that we have seen, we were at about 60% or so and we always have thought that India's consumption component of the GDP is at about 60% and that's where we want to be.

items.statement: ECLGS 5.0 disbursements reached INR 14,000 crores by June 30, among highest for participating banks
items.quote: We have already as of 30th of June had a disbursement in that scheme of close to INR14,000 crores under the ECLGS scheme. And I think and I believe that's amongst the highest in terms of the participating banks.

items.statement: Healthy credit demand seen across corporate, MSME, and retail segments; El Nino impact to be monitored in Q3
items.quote: We do see credit demand holding. We do see a lot of resilience which has been there in the economy even post what we have seen in terms of the geopolitical situation. Yes, we have to wait for the full impact of the El Niño and see because that does have a bearing which plays out in the third quarter.

items.statement: Branch productivity at INR 330 crores per branch vs INR 266 crores in FY23; 40% of branches less than 5 years old
items.quote: If you look at the per branch metrics, we are about INR 330 crores per branch currently. And if you go back to the FY'23 time period, we were INR 266 crores per branch.

items.statement: CEO reappointment process underway; GNRC and Board seized of matter; announcement to follow conclusion
items.quote: The GNRC and Board is fully seized of the matter and that is work in progress and as they arrive at a conclusion, we will certainly make the necessary announcements in that regard.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 disbursement target maintained at INR3,000 crore despite IT implementation.
items.quote: So 3,000 crores that we are targeting for Q2 stays, that number stays.

items.statement: Confident NIM will be maintained at 3.81% or higher.
items.quote: So, we are confident that the NIM will be maintained at 3.81% plus and we should not have a problem in that.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 10 basis points maintained for the year.
items.quote: So, basically, we are confident that, you know, we should be able to maintain our credit cost guidance of 10 basis points.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected around 19.5% for current year, targeting 18% in three years.
items.quote: Current year we do envisage that it will be hovering around 19.5% cost-to-income ratio.

items.statement: Plans to implement new LOS/LMS across remaining 245 branches by end of Q2 FY27.
items.quote: So, we plan to, in fact, implement it across our remaining 245 branches in this current quarter only.

items.statement: Increased special rate threshold from INR20 lakh to INR25 lakh to improve yield.
items.quote: So, like now whatever special rates that we are offering, which we are offering for more than INR20 lakhs, we have increased it to more than INR25 lakhs.

items.statement: Incremental bank borrowing costs have risen to 7.25-7.5% from 6.95%.
items.quote: As against 6.95% which at which we were raising in last year from the banks, we are now, you know, the spread they have increased and while they can't increase on the existing loans, it's only for the new loans where the banks have been quoting anywhere between 7.25% to 7.5%.

items.statement: No slowdown in demand across geographies; added 60 APF projects in Q1.
items.quote: In fact, in this quarter, that is Q1, we've added another 60 APF projects also.

items.statement: SENP segment yields are 0.5% higher than salaried; NPA higher at 1.45-1.5% vs 0.6-0.63%.
items.quote: If it's everything else being the same, if it was just a matter of salaried versus self-employed, the differential would be 0.5 percentage point.

items.statement: Rate differential with banks widened to over 1 percentage point, increasing BT out pressure.
items.quote: So this difference, which was 55 basis points has now increased to more than 1 percentage point, which is difficult to convince a customer, 50 to 60 basis points, we can convince the customer, customers also don't mind because the impact on their EMI is not very large.

items.statement: ROA for Q1 FY27 was 2.39%, down from 2.53% last year due to higher opex.
items.quote: I guess, this quarter, we have done 2.39% as the ROA and 18% plus in terms of ROE, at least for the quarter.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY27 expected at 21% due to DTA benefits, stable going forward.
items.quote: Yes, 21% because of some DTA benefits, and this will be stable rate. There are no major surprises coming in the next quarters.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining growth momentum this year, barring Middle East global challenges.
items.quote: So we are confident that the same momentum can be maintained in this year as well, barring the impact that the global challenges in the Middle East that everybody is facing.

items.statement: FY27 capex budget of about INR80 crores for analytical capabilities and select services.
items.quote: We have slated a budget of approximately INR80 crores of capex spend for FY27 to primarily focus on strengthening our analytical capabilities and expanding select service offerings.

items.statement: INR10 crores of FY27 capex remaining for Biologics CRADS; rest INR70 crores routine.
items.quote: I think only a portion of it is remaining for the biologics CRADS that we have set up. So, that is around INR10 crores. The rest INR70 crores is for routine operations for the various business units that we have.

items.statement: Biologics project total budget INR35 crores; INR20 crores spent, may spend about INR10 crores this year.
items.quote: And on the Biologics, the plan is to spend INR35 crores. We have spent around INR20 crores. The plan is to see if there is a need to spend the remainder this year. We think we may spend about INR10 crores out of the total INR35 crores budget that we have put for this project.

items.statement: Margins expected not to decline further as business is expected to grow in coming quarters.
items.quote: We expect that the margins will not go down further, because we are expecting the business to grow in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Positive enquiry trend; upcoming quarters expected to be better.
items.quote: As I mentioned in my opening remarks, the enquiry trend is quite positive quarter-on-quarter. So with that positive enquiry trend, we are quite hopeful that the upcoming quarters will be better.

items.statement: Pharma demand strong with tailwinds in India and globally; food imports/exports impacted by war.
items.quote: Pharma, strong. Food, the import and exports have been impacted because of the war situation, because the cost of import and export has gone up for the businesses.

items.statement: Biologics to contribute significantly to top line and margin from third year onwards, not this year.
items.quote: Coming to your first question on when it will be a significant contributor to the top line and margin, not this year, but hopefully, from the third year onwards, we expect it to be contributing significantly to the top line and margin.

items.statement: First Biologics order secured from a domestic customer; commercialization began in Q1.
items.quote: The commercialization has begun already in Q1. The client is onboarded in Q1.

items.statement: Food business has 50% domestic exposure and 50% import/export samples; Middle East crisis caused some business loss.
items.quote: In our food business, we have 50% exposure to domestic testing and also on the other 50% is exposed to either import samples or export samples of food.

items.statement: No active acquisition or inorganic opportunity on the table currently, though open to evaluating.
items.quote: We are not involved actively in any acquisition or anything of that nature right now. But as we get into it, I'm sure I'll communicate that to the investor group. As of now, there is nothing active there.

items.statement: Infrastructure of about 200,000 sq ft built; approximately 60% occupied, good for next 4-5 years.
items.quote: Infrastructure, see, we have built about 200,000 square feet. In that, I think we have occupied at least 60%, I would say, you know, approximately.

items.statement: INR100 crores capex planned across FY27-28, INR27 crores executed in Q1 FY27, INR60 crores to be capitalized in FY27
items.quote: we are looking to spend around INR100 crores in FY27 and 2028 together. In my opening remarks, I mentioned we've already spent INR27 crores in Q1.

items.statement: Out of INR100 crores capex, INR60 crores to be capitalized in FY27
items.quote: Out of INR100 crores, we would be capitalizing around INR60 crores during FY27.

items.statement: Secured 15,000 tons rubberized bitumen processing order for FY27 execution
items.quote: The company also secured a 15,000 tons of rubberized bitumen processing order for execution in FY27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 22% (exceeding 18-20% guidance), driven by gross margin expansion from efficient raw material costs and value-added product sales
items.quote: Our overall margin at EBITDA level has expanded by about 4%. So a very large contribution of this has come at the gross margin level because our -- and some on account of efficiencies because of scale.

items.statement: Management expects sustainable EBITDA margins of 18-20% despite Q1's 22%, citing front-ended costs from new projects
items.quote: overall margins of 18% to 20% is what we believe can be delivered in a business like ours, and that is what has played out well in Q1.

items.statement: TPO and rCB pyrolysis business expected to contribute 7-10% of FY27 revenue (INR50-60 crores)
items.quote: Approximately about 7% to 10% of total revenue will come from the pyrolysis TPO RCB business.

items.statement: Industrial segment revenue grew 58% YoY, exports up 46% YoY, driven by rising raw material costs and ESG focus in tire industry
items.quote: The Industrial segment achieved a strong 58% Y-o-Y growth in revenue. Exports volume delivered robust 46% Y-o-Y growth despite global economic headwinds, supported by a healthy order pipeline.

items.statement: Consumer segment volumes down 20% due to 3x binder/synthetic grass price increases from West Asia conflict; recovery expected when prices stabilize
items.quote: The significant rise in binder and synthetic grass prices nearly threefold in some of the cases led to delay in track and turfing project execution. This segment will bounce back once these scenarios stabilizes.

items.statement: Credit growth target of 13-14% minimum for FY27, expects to exceed as in past years.
items.quote: See, credit growth, we are intending to grow at around 13% to 14%. And I always say that having said that, this is the minimum we want to grow.

items.statement: ROA expected to reach around 1.46% by end of financial year, NIM driven.
items.quote: So going forward, by end of this year, maybe financial year, maybe we are looking at around 1.46%.

items.statement: NIM expected to stay in 3.3-3.4% range going forward.
items.quote: So we are pretty sure that going forward also, sir, NIM will b e in this range only around 3.3 to 3.4 . In this range, it will move.

items.statement: ROA expected between 1.4% and 1.5% over next two to three quarters.
items.quote: ROA also around -- between 1.4% to 1.5%, we do expect in the foreseeable two to three quarters going forward.

items.statement: Full year credit cost guidance of 0.35% to 0.40%.
items.quote: Credit cost for June quarter is 0.14%. And we expect that for the full year, the credit cost should be around 0.35% to 0.40%.

items.statement: INR 5,000 crore equity raise planned in Q3/Q4 in one or more tranches.
items.quote: We intend to go to the market in maybe more than one tranche in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: ECL provisioning: INR 2,150 crores provided against INR 3,000 crores estimated requirement; no 4-year dispensation planned.
items.quote: Till March, we created a forward-looking provision for ECL only INR 1,700 crores. This is the balance sheet we have added INR 400 crores additional. So against INR 3,000 crores of probable requiremen t, we have provided already INR 2,150 crores to meet this ECL provisioning requirement.

items.statement: Corporate loan pipeline of INR 14,000 crores sanctioned; corporate book to grow 12-13% by year end.
items.quote: The corporate book, I will say that, there is a pipeline of around INR 14,000 crores already sanctioned and in different stages of disbursement. And we expect that the corporate loan book also, by the end of this year will grow by 12% to 13%.

items.statement: ECLGS disbursement of INR 2,600 crores done; INR 1,800 crores expected in next 1-1.5 months.
items.quote: And out of that, we h ave so far disbursed around INR 2,600 crores based on the requirement of the individual borrowers and in terms of ECLGS 5 requirement. So, INR 2,600 crores is already done. INR 1,800 crores is expected to be done over the next one, one and half months.

items.statement: Yield on advances rose due to better pricing; 54% of credit portfolio linked to MCLR, 37% to RLLR.
items.quote: Yield on advances has increased because of a pricing issue, of course. And about 54% of the credit portfolio is linked to MCLR and 37% to RLLR , and because of good quality lending at reasonable pricing, yield on advances has increased.

items.statement: Exited INR 10,000 crore corporate account in April as pricing did not match; no loss-making business.
items.quote: See, for IOB, this 10% decline is because of one bigger account around -- amounting to around INR 10,000 crores, which we -- in the first month of this financial year in the month of April itself, since pricing was not matching, so we came out of that arrangement.

items.statement: Cost of deposits fell due to CASA focus and low reliance on bulk deposits; all term deposit repricing completed.
items.quote: All repricing done, already done, yes. Completed 6 months before.

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agriculture, MSME) is about 80% of portfolio; intends to maintain around that level.
items.quote: Our rally is around 80%. We intend to maintain around that level.

items.statement: Total SMA at 4.05% (INR 13,000 crores); SMA 2 rose INR 500 crores over March but mostly regularized.
items.quote: As regards SMA, SMA 0 is INR5,733 crores. SMA 1 is INR3,068 crores. And SMA 2 is INR4,246 crores. So total SMA is INR13,000 crores, percentage terms, it is 4.05%.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: gross NPA <2.5%, net NPA <0.3%, slippages ratio <0.9%, PCR >96%, cost-to-income 47-48% by year-end
items.quote: Gross NPA our guidance is less than 2.5% and net NPA it is less than 0.3%. And already our net NPA is below 0.3, we are 0.28%. Gross NPA also last year it was 3.78, we have brought it down to 2.78 in the first quarter itself. So we are all parameter wise if you see the guidance which we have given, we are on track.

items.statement: Expect healthy Q-o-Q NIM improvement in coming quarters and achieve FY27 NIM guidance
items.quote: I am confident to witness healthy Q-o-Q improvement in margins in the coming quarters and achieving our guidance for the financial year '26-'27.

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved to 2.64% from 2.61% Q-o-Q; global NIM improved to 2.50% from 2.47%
items.quote: Our domestic NIM, which was 2.61% last quarter, it has gone to 2.64%. And the global NIM was 2.47% in the Q4, which has gone to 2.50%.

items.statement: Cost of deposits improved 34 bps Y-o-Y; avoiding bulk deposits and CDs; shedding low-yielding advances below 7%
items.quote: And bank has also mindful of the higher cost deposits, and that is the reason we are absolutely not there in the bulk deposit market and the CD market. And very cautiously we have kept the deposit growth at 8.5%. And this has contributed in the deposit cost of deposit and 34 basis point improvement has happened in the

items.statement: Core advances ex-IBPC grew 15.4% Y-o-Y; retail ex-IBPC 17.5%, MSME 19.8%, agri 16.4%; strong sanction pipeline
items.quote: Excluding the impact of the IBPC book, core advances recorded a strong 15.4% Y-o-Y growth, underscoring sustained credit demand and healthy business momentum. Our core RAM book has witnessed decent growth with retail book, excluding IBPC, growing at 17.5%. MSME is growing at 19.8% and agri priority sector at 16.4%.

items.statement: Targeting USD2.5 billion FCNR(B) mobilization; USD425 million raised so far; 200 million via leverage
