items.quote: Already USD425 million we have mobilized till yesterday and we are seeing the good traction. Whatever the commitment which we have given and we have set the target for ourselves, that is the USD2.5 billion through the FCNR route, we are going to mobilize that

items.statement: Total recovery guidance INR13,000 crores for FY27; INR4,000 crores expected from technical write-off accounts
items.quote: last year when I had given the guidance, first of all the total recovery guidance we have given for INR13,000 crores total recovery will happen through that route now. Within that INR13,000 crores, INR4,000 crores we are expecting that it will happen through the TWO route now.

items.statement: MSME growth target ~25% for FY27; book behaving well with no stress; mostly CGTMSE covered (75% coverage)
items.quote: We are expecting that we will be touching a growth of around 25% in the MSME segment. And book is behaving very well, absolutely there is no challenge in the stress or in the NPA.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio target INR59,000-60,000 crores by FY27 end from INR31,888 crores currently; 103% Y-o-Y growth
items.quote: So we are expecting that around INR59,000 crores INR60,000 crores our portfolio should be there by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Aims to grow advances and deposits 15-17%, slightly above industry.
items.quote: So now moving forward, we endeavor to grow at a little above what the industry would be growing at and which is what makes us happy is, it could be in the range of may be 15% to 17%.

items.statement: Targets NIM north of 3% over next 2 years.
items.quote: Having said this, our near -term aspiration is to move the NIM towards the 3% plus handle over the next 2 years and the underlying levers are well understood.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 SR portfolio gains guidance of INR 800-1,000 crores.
items.quote: Despite tepid gains from the SR portfolio in Q1, we maintain our guidance of INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores of gains from this portfolio for this financial year '27.

items.statement: Expects core ROA expansion of 15-20 bps in FY27.
items.quote: Our expectation is fiscal '27, we should see a 15 to 20 basis points expansion in the core ROA.

items.statement: Aims to deliver 1% reported ROA for FY27 if external factors play out.
items.quote: And if the resolutions, let's say, the external factors on bond gains and trading with all of those elements also play out, I think we should be able to also deliver the fully reported 1% ROA for fiscal '27.

items.statement: Has sufficient capital for next 3-4 quarters; enabling resolution for capital raise in place.
items.quote: But at the moment, we have sufficient cushion to grow for the next maybe 3 or 4 quarters.

items.statement: Plans to raise capital when CET-1 is in 13% handle, not lower.
items.quote: This time around, clearly, we don't want to drop to those levels. We will raise it, let's say, in the 13% handle.

items.statement: Retail disbursements growing 25-30% incrementally; book growth to reflect in 3-4 quarters.
items.quote: But on the momentum on the fresh business, we are in a very steady state at a good state to be in a good range of 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Maintains 75:25 secured to unsecured mix in retail.
items.quote: So typically, let's say, it's a 75 -25 ratio, we will ensure a 75% secured versus 25% unsecured kind of Retail.

items.statement: ECL transition impact expected not material on core equity.
items.quote: So I think that's really the headline message, but we will come back during the course of this year as we firm up these numbers so that we can give you a better visibility of what impact could play out.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced without attrition, improving pricing power.
items.quote: See, basically, you are also aware that since previous financial year April, we have actually substantially come down on the Cost of Deposits. And that has played out very well for us without actually resulting in any attrition of Deposits, right.

items.statement: Sees strong demand for FCNR deposits, keeping leverage at 9x.
items.quote: As of now, we have decided that we'll keep it to 9% - I mean 9x.

items.statement: Working with SMBC and other banks for FCNR limits.
items.quote: So just to add, we are working with many international banks for the limits to make this facility available, including SMBC.

items.statement: Leveraging SMBC partnership for Indo-Japanese corridor opportunities.
items.quote: And eventually, our endeavor is to get the max that happens in this corridor between these two countries, should happen through our Bank.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth target to be given by end of September; company expects growth but no number yet.
items.quote: We had mentioned in the last con call also that sometime for end of September, we would like to give a full year growth target with respect to our revenue. and we still maintain that.

items.statement: Aims to maintain and sustain operating EBITDA margin of a little over 15% for the full year.
items.quote: Last year, on an operating EBITDA level, we did a little over 15% and that is our aim to be able to maintain and sustain.

items.statement: Commodity inflation expected at 11-12%; about 9-10% price increase already taken, may need another 2%.
items.quote: the final effect, which hopefully should be finally settled in July or latest by August with respect to reflection in our costing would be anywhere between 11%, 12%. And we've already pushed around a 9%, 10% price increase.

items.statement: Full-year capex expected at INR200-250 crores, including land takeover and new defense plant.
items.quote: for the whole year, I think our capex should be somewhere around INR200 crores to INR250 crores, in which the major chunk will go to take over that about INR130 crores, INR140 crores to take over the land

items.statement: Defense order execution to exceed INR200 crores in FY27, possibly 10-15% more.
items.quote: Yes, I think we should be doing more than that. It could be another 10%, 15% more than maybe slightly more.

items.statement: Hydra to new-generation crane mix expected to return to 60-40 this year, stabilizing at 50-50 in 1-3 years.
items.quote: I feel that in this year, the Hydra to NG will again go back to 60 -40, where 60 is Hydra, 40 is NG.

items.statement: Three price hikes taken: 1-1.5% in January, 3-4% in March, 5-6% in June; total about 10%.
items.quote: we pushed 1%, 1.5% in January, then 3%, 4% across the range in March and in June, another 5%, 6%, depending on models and products.

items.statement: Demand strong till May-June, traditionally slows in rains; expects Q2 similar to Q1 and better than last year.
items.quote: Demand had been very strong till May, June. And obviously, traditionally, it slows down a little in the rains.

items.statement: New defense manufacturing facility (Plant 9) capex INR40-50 crores, capacity about INR500 crores turnover, functional by Q3/Q4 FY27.
items.quote: from this facility combined together, where we are investing close to about INR40 crores, INR50 crores, eventually, we should be able to do a turnover of , just a second. Maybe close to about INR500 crores.

items.statement: Tower crane capacity already increased to about 1,000 cranes; expansion timing decision deferred to September.
items.quote: we've actually, in the last 1 year, have been able to increase our capacity to about 1,000 cranes now.

items.statement: Deficient monsoon could cause 5-10% variability in business, evident in Q3 of same year.
items.quote: yes, it can lead to a 5%, 7%, 10% up and down if the monsoons are not full or effectively.

name: Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy Ltd

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 10-15% for FY27 despite high base of FY26
items.quote: We anticipate ordering activity to pick up from this quarter in the domestic market, and we are confident of maintaining our market share, which, in our view, should enable us to deliver 10% to 15% growth in revenue, this fiscal despite the high base of financial year '26.

items.statement: Six turnkey projects worth INR9,000 crores yet to commence execution, expected to contribute from H2 FY27
items.quote: The total value of these 6 projects is approximately INR9,000 crores. These orders were won during the second half of financial year '26 and Q1 FY27. We expect these orders to start contributing more meaningfully during the second half of the fiscal year.

items.statement: Egypt 1,000 MW AC solar + 600 MWh BESS project (USD560M) NTP expected September, revenue contribution from Q4 FY27
items.quote: The NTP of this project, we are expecting in September. With this September NTP, we are expecting that the revenue contribution from this project will add to the last quarter of this financial year.

items.statement: EPC gross margin guided at 8-10% depending on turnkey vs BoS mix; O&M gross margin expected to stabilize at ~20%
items.quote: We expect the EPC gross margin to range between 8% to 10%, depending on the project mix of turnkey and BoS. On the O&M side, we expect gross margins to stabilize at around 20% level.

items.statement: O&M portfolio reached record 18.3 GWp; full contribution expected from Q3 FY27; FY27 O&M revenue guided at INR400-450 crores vs INR268 crores in FY26
items.quote: We have now achieved a record 18.3 gigawatt peak capacities under operations. We anticipate this full portfolio to start contributing fully from third quarter of this fiscal year.

items.statement: International projects de-risked via back-to-back supply chain pricing; no commodity price exposure on new international orders
items.quote: In all our international projects, we continue to judiciously evaluate the risk and rewards and are mindful of not being exposed to the commodity prices and equipment price increase risk.

items.statement: Order book growth guidance of 10-15% for FY27 maintained; UOV expected >INR10,000 crores by FY27 end
items.quote: We can say that the order book would be definitely more than INR10,000 crores in this financial year. To start with in the first quarter of next financial year at maybe slightly higher numbers than this financial years we had at the UOV.

items.statement: Domestic ordering activity expected to pick up from Q2 FY27; INR45,000-50,000 crores pipeline visible for H2 FY27 (25 GW utility + 35 GWh BESS)
items.quote: I can clearly see that the order worth of around INR45,000 crores to INR50,000 crores, right? So, let's say, around 25 gigawatt on the utility scale and around 35 gigawatt hour on the BESS side.

items.statement: Operating leverage expected to improve EBITDA margins as overheads grow slower than revenue; marginal EBITDA impact if gross margin at lower end of 8-10% range
items.quote: Our overheads in terms of absolute number will not increase. In terms of percentage, it should come down a little bit from the current number, because we are growing in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Net working capital at negative INR260 crores; expected to improve further with advances from new large projects
items.quote: Our net working capital was at negative INR260 crores compared to negative INR329 crores in previous quarter. As CKT mentioned earlier, with the improved collections from the new large projects, we anticipate the working capital cycle to continue to improve.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 top-line growth guidance of around 15% despite strong Q1.
items.quote: This year Sanjesh, I would still stick to our 15% kind of growth, something we had spoken about even in our last call, even though this this quarter has been a stronger quarter for us.

items.statement: Aims for steady-state consolidated EBITDA margin of at least 15% once recalibration materializes.
items.quote: Our aim is that once we recalibrate the whole business mix, the product mix, we should have a steady state, the EBITDA margins at around 15% at least once these steps that we are taking materialize.

items.statement: Expects current 11.6% EBITDA margin to be the base level going forward.
items.quote: Yes, so I think these level of margins you can expect to be the base level.

items.statement: Exiting B2C business expected to release 2-3% EBITDA margin improvement.
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA margins if you see it will release at least 2%-3% EBITDA.

items.statement: Pharma business expected to generate Rs. 30-50 crore revenue this year after compliance completion.
items.quote: Yes, and it could be a revenue potential of close to Rs. 30 crore - Rs. 50 crore.

items.statement: Pharma revenue targeted at Rs. 70-75 crore this year versus over Rs. 50 crore last year.
items.quote: The pharma, which is the higher value, I think we did more than Rs. 50 crore last year and this year we should do Rs. 70 – Rs. 75 crore in pharma this year.

items.statement: Slowed down all India capex; only calibrated spending on new R&D molecules.
items.quote: So, in in India currently we have slowed down on all the CAPEX spends because we are now doing very calibrated spend ing on new CAPEX.

items.statement: KSA project to take about 1.5 years from announcement to first production.
items.quote: It should take about 1.5 years for us to start the first kilo of production once we make the announcement.

items.statement: Took a Rs. 5 crore hit on phenol due to delayed China shipments and high spot purchases.
items.quote: We took a hit of around Rs. 5 crore in the last quarter on phenol alone because shipments from China were promised, and we had contracted them at a certain price.

items.statement: Able to pass on raw material price hikes; freight volatility causes some margin loss.
items.quote: To pass on the raw material pricing is no worry at all. Otherwise, you know, you see where the crude has gone from where and where our raw materials have gone.

items.statement: Volume grew about 10% YoY; rest of growth from higher pricing.
items.quote: The YoY growth in terms of volume v/s price, the volume has grown by about 10% and the rest of the growth has mostly come out of the higher pricing.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs. 248 crore in Q1 from Rs. 280 crore in March.
items.quote: On the debt profile, this quarter our net debt is about Rs. 248 crore. In March, this was about Rs. 280 crore.

items.statement: Finance cost run rate expected at Rs. 9-10 crore going forward.
items.quote: But I think now going forward the finance cost should be at close to this Rs. 9 crore to Rs. 10 crore kind of a run rate.

items.statement: Aims to more than double Rossari's scale over the next four years.
items.quote: We will not stop seeding these initiatives just to show a slightly higher EBITDA margin.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA growth target of 20-25% with revenue growth also above 20%
items.quote: If you see, we have been focusing more on the EBITDA numbers of more than 20%, 25% for FY27, number one.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 14-15% remains conservative given current 13-14% margins and high-value businesses yet to contribute
items.quote: Even at this scale, our long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of around 14% to 15% remain very conservative considering that we are already operating at close to 13% to 14% EBITDA margin with several high-value business yet to contribute.

items.statement: Incurred INR575 crores in Q1 FY27; balance INR9,580 crores of announced capex to be deployed over next 3-4 years funded primarily through internal accruals
items.quote: On the capital expenditure front, we incurred INR575 crores during this quarter towards our ongoing expansion project. Going forward, the balance approximately INR9,580 crores of our announced capex is expected to be deployed over the next 3 to 4 years across our planned project.

items.statement: Aluminium foil plant has order book of close to more than 10 months from existing facility
items.quote: We are already in the business. We have a lot of order booking. We have almost close to more than 10 months order bookings from our existing foil plant.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 14.9% YoY from 14.3% and QoQ from 14.4%; operating EBITDA margin at 14%
items.quote: Similarly, the EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR812 crores, which is a total EBITDA, which is reflecting a growth of 28.3% on a year-on-year basis and 7.4% on quarter-on-quarter. And as far as EBITDA margin expanded to 14.9% in comparison with the 14.3% in quarter 1 of the last financial year, and 14.4% in quarter 4

items.statement: Stainless steel product mix: two-thirds 200/400 series (nickel-free), 35-40% 300 series; flat steel focus
items.quote: See, we have been very conservative. I think we have shown around INR14,000 a ton, number 1. Number 2, our major product, two-third is going to be 200 and 400, which is almost a nickel-free steel, and close to 35%, 40% is going to be 300 series.

items.statement: Steel demand growing 7-8% annually; rebar contributes 50-55% of steel consumption; monsoon-related softness is seasonal and not a concern
items.quote: And if you see from the overall demand prospect, we all know that the country is doing very well. Still, there is a growth of 7% to 8% every year on steel. And rebar contributes the major consumption of steel in the country close to 50%, 55% of the overall steel production.

items.statement: No major iron ore mine acquisition planned due to high premiums; focusing on beneficiation of low-grade ore and downstream value addition instead
items.quote: We are doing a continuous due diligence on the iron ore assets and all. But most of the assets are at a very high premium. And we feel that it is not going to be wise on our scale of business to add lot of cost on the raw material.

items.statement: INR4,500 crores fundraising approval is only an enabling resolution; no immediate fundraise planned as internal accruals suffice for capex
items.quote: Enabling resolution. Just -- no, it's just enabling resolution. Nothing very serious on the table.

items.statement: Color coated plant commissioned in April 2026, increasing cold rolling capacity by 60% from 0.25 to 0.4 million tons
items.quote: We are pleased to share the successful commissioning of our color coated plant in April 2026, which increased our cold rolling capacity by 60% from 0.25 metric ton to 0.4 metric ton -- million ton.

items.statement: Aluminium flat roll product projects on track for commissioning in Q2 FY27; aluminium foil facility commissioned and ramping up
items.quote: The aluminium flat roll product projects remain on track for commissioning during the second quarter. All major projects across our portfolio continues to progress as planned and we expect to commission within the targeted timeline.

items.statement: Stainless steel business run rate currently INR130-140 crores; expected to reach INR600-700 crores at 70-80% capacity utilization of new plant
items.quote: Today, we are doing a run rate of close to around INR130 crores, INR140 crores in the stainless steel business. We expect that once we commission our new plant and it goes at 70%, 80% capacity, we should be able to do a run rate close to INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: Inventory levels maintained at 2-3 months; raw material procurement requires deposits with Coal India and government iron ore suppliers
items.quote: We will be maintaining our inventory level more on a 2- to 3-month inventory level, and we will continue with the inventory level.

items.statement: Acquired 26% stake in Emerge Green Power for renewable energy; shifting solar strategy from capex to opex/JV model
items.quote: During the quarter, Shyam Metalics acquired 26% equity stake in Emerge Green Power Private Limited, which is constantly becoming an associate company of the company.

name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd

items.statement: Yields expected to remain at Q1 levels, plus or minus a few basis points, barring telescoping pricing.
items.quote: So, we feel that, going forward, the yield should be in the similar range, barring one or two basis points here and there, plus the telescoping pricing.

items.statement: Employee cost to remain in similar range in coming quarters after ESOP cost of about Rs 10 crore per quarter.
items.quote: The impact of that is around 10 crores per quarter of the additional employees cost through the ESOP. And roughly, the employee cost, which is there in Q1, should continue in the same range for coming quarters.

items.statement: OPEX to remain within inflationary guidelines; no cost shocks expected.
items.quote: OPEX, I think, remain within the inflationary guidelines. Employee cost, as we discussed in the first call, should remain largely in the similar range as we have already factored in the ESOP cost, etc.

items.statement: Alternate business revenue contribution expected to remain in similar range in coming quarters.
items.quote: I think the revenue or contribution for Alternate should be in the similar range except 1% or 2% here and there, I think should be there.

items.statement: PMS long-only equity AUM targeted to reach Rs 20,000-21,000 crore over next three years.
items.quote: Definitely, we have a target to take it to anywhere between ₹20,000 crore, ₹21,000 crore over a period of next three years.

items.statement: Each Alternate vertical targeted to reach Rs 5,000-7,000 crore size to start with.
items.quote: I think each one of them will gun for about anywhere between ₹5,000 crores to ₹7,000 crore kind of size to start with.

items.statement: AMC committed to provide seed capital up to 10% of fund size for AIF performing credit funds.
items.quote: That is one of the reasons we also given a commitment from our AMC P&L in order to provide seed capital up to 10% of the fund size.

items.statement: Equity yield around 63-64 bps, debt 24-25 bps, liquid 12-13 bps, ETF around 8 bps.
items.quote: Yes. So, coming to the yield levels for equity, it is around 63 to 64 basis points. Debt should be around 24 to 25 basis points.

items.statement: PMS and AIF contributed around 7% of gross revenue and 4% of net revenue in the quarter.
items.quote: And PMS and AIF contribution, if you see contribution on total revenue on gross basis is around 7% for the quarter. And on net revenue basis, post payout of commission to distributors is around 4% on overall revenue.

items.statement: SIP cumulative contribution for the quarter around Rs 3,300 crore, in line with Q4.
items.quote: SIP cumulative contribution for the quarter was around ₹3,300 crore which is actually in line with Q4 numbers also.

items.statement: Flagship funds FlexiCap, Balanced Advantage, Multi-Asset, Small Cap expected to see maximum flows.
items.quote: First and foremost, FlexiCap fund. Second is Balance Advantage Fund. And third is the Multi -Asset Allocation Fund. And fourth is the Small Cap Fund.

items.statement: Fixed income volatility in May caused outflows in duration funds, impacting average AUM.
items.quote: We did lose some bit of money. In fact, all the money has come back in June end and July. At least for a month, I think it affected in the month of May, that's why it got impacted in the average asset.

items.statement: ESIC mandate adds very marginal revenue; EPFO mandate opened gate for privately managed EPFO flows.
items.quote: ESIC mandate, of course, in terms of the revenue, very marginal. We don’t earn any much on this.

items.statement: Continues outlook for 800 net new stores including franchisee stores in FY27.
items.quote: We continue with the outlook for adding 800 net new stores, including the franchisee stores in FY27.

items.statement: Private label sales were 20% of Q1 FY27 revenue; pharma 10.7%, non-pharma 9.3%.
items.quote: Private label sales for Q1 FY27 constitutes 20%, pharma being 10.7% and the non-pharma being 9.3% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Franchisee closures due to expectation mismatch; model still being tweaked to stabilize.
items.quote: there is an expectation mismatch both from the franchisees who are first-time entrepreneurs, they get into this. Their expectation is X, they'll end up getting Y. And very quickly, they are taking decisions, which we have to honor them.

items.statement: Promoter debt stands at approximately INR1,150 crores including interest.
items.quote: It's close to around INR1,150 crores.

items.statement: Book-to-bill ratio expected to remain at 1.5x for FY27
items.quote: So, book-to-bill ratio will be at the same thing where we are today at 1.5x. So, we will be at that number for the year too.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 10.5% in Q1 FY27, up 147 bps YoY; four consecutive quarters of double-digit margins
items.quote: Our normalized EBITDA margin stood at 10.5% in Q1 FY27, improving by 147 basis points year-on-year from 9% in Q1 FY26. Importantly, we now have consistently delivered double-digit EBITDA margins for four consecutive quarters.

items.statement: No significant incremental capex needed for AI data centre and robotics expansion; annual capex at 1.75-2x of revenue
items.quote: The capex, I think, as you said, whatever we have today, closely around 1.75 x to 2x of the revenue. So, we don't need any such additional capex apart from a regular annual capex.

items.statement: Strong order intake from both existing (70%) and new customers (30%); pipeline substantially higher than INR 4,000-5,000 crores
items.quote: If you look at that one, probably close to around 70% of that is -- where it is from our existing customers and the balance 30% is from the new customers whom we added in the last 4 equipment, at least from the last four to six quarters.

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing logistics delays and cost increases, but mitigated by inventory planning for Q1 and Q2
items.quote: What we are seeing even now today is there is -- there are some delays in the logistics in terms of shipments and we are also seeing some of the costs going up due to these West Asia crisis at this point of time.

items.statement: Semiconductor capital equipment revenue growth expected over next 6-12 months
items.quote: Over the next 6 to 12 months we will be seeing more of the revenue growth which probably in turn will also give us some leverage in terms of the margins there.

items.statement: Q2 and FY27 revenue momentum expected to continue in similar range; no hard revenue guidance given
items.quote: In terms of the Q2 and going forward, we will be seeing a similar momentum in the range, okay? So, we do not see any of the major concern on the momentum in terms of our revenues and order intakes.

items.statement: Build-to-specifications lab expanded from 6,000 to 15,000 sq ft, more than doubling footprint
items.quote: We completed the expansion of our build-to-specifications lab from 6,000 square feet to 15,000 square feet, more than doubling that footprint.

items.statement: Order book reached all-time high of INR 761 crores with 77% from private sector clients
items.quote: Our total order book has reached an all-time high of INR 761 crores, providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Largest ever order of INR 307 crores from Hindustan Zinc commenced execution in Rajasthan
items.quote: During the quarter, we commenced execution of our largest ever order, valued at 307 crores, received from Hindustan Zinc in the state of Rajasthan.

items.statement: Reliance Industries CBM contract extended for over INR 166 crores strengthening long-term revenue visibility
items.quote: We also secured an extension of our coal-backed methane contract from Reliance Industries Ltd., valued at over INR 166 crores, further strengthening our long-term revenue visibility.

items.statement: Expect significant growth in FY27 with H2 historically stronger due to favorable weather and higher project activity
items.quote: Historically, the second half has been our strongest period owing to favorable weather conditions and higher project activity and we expect this trend to continue in future as well.

items.statement: Reliance contract expected to contribute 35-40% of FY27 revenue (+/-5%)
items.quote: Yes, it should be on the same line, (+/-5%).

items.statement: Jharkhand coal block Phase-I requires ~INR 200 crores funded via internal accruals, bank debt, and off-take agreements
items.quote: As we have been saying that in the 1st Phase, we shall be requiring around approximately INR 200 crores to start the project.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 24.15%, management confident margins sustainable due to high entry barriers
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was around 24.15%.

items.statement: Order book split: ~25% oil & gas, remaining 75% across coal, mineral, seismic, aquifer mapping (each 15-30%)
items.quote: Oil and gas would be around 25% and the rest of it. Basically, all the verticals, I would say, they are ranging from 15% to 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Oman operations unaffected by Middle East tensions; located on outskirts of Strait of Hormuz
items.quote: Oman is, you know, it is outside the, I won't say outside the State of Hormuz, but it is on the outskirt of the State of Hormuz. So, the shipments have affected, but it has not affected that much that it's a matter of concern.

items.statement: Placed orders for additional drilling rigs and equipment to strengthen execution capabilities
items.quote: To support our growing business requirements, we have placed orders for additional drilling rigs and other equipment, further strengthening our execution capabilities.

items.statement: Jharkhand coal block targets production start by FY29 with 24.25% revenue sharing with government
items.quote: Subject to the necessary regulatory approvals, we will commence mine development activities including preparation of the mining plan with the objective of commencing coal production by the financial year 2028-2029.

items.statement: Resource utilization exceeded 100% in Q1 due to outsourcing and hired rigs; additional rigs on order
items.quote: More than 100%. The reason is that we have outsourced some of our work to other contractors as well. So, the resource utilization has been more than 100%.

name: Canara Robeco Asset Management Company Ltd

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target range 38-42%, comfortable below 40%.
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio for us -- we like it to be below 40. That's where we like it to be. We are well within that range. So between 38 to 42 is the range we like to play in.

items.statement: Yield target range 35-38 bps, comfortable with that range.
items.quote: We like our yields to be in the range of 35 to 38. That's why we would like -- we're comfortable with that range.

items.statement: New mutual fund product launch planned in next 2-3 months; passives and SIFs in short-to-medium term.
items.quote: Currently, we are focused on coming up with a new product which will be launched on the mutual fund space in the next two to three months and then in the short-to-medium term passives is certainly an option.

items.statement: Target about two NFOs per financial year, subject to board and SEBI approval.
items.quote: We generally target about two in the financial year, but they're subject to of course board and SEBI approval.

items.statement: Equity yields expected 36-40 bps, to rationalize over next quarter or two.
items.quote: But we do expect the yields to be in the region somewhere in the region of 36 bps to 40 bps in terms of the equity. So, in that region we expect it to be, but it obviously will rationalize out over the period of the next quarter or two.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 segment yields: equity 39-40 bps, fixed income 27-28 bps, liquid 2-3 bps, overall 37-38 bps.
items.value: equity 39-40 bps, fixed income 27-28 bps, liquid 2-3 bps, overall 37-38 bps
items.quote: Equity yields were in the range of 39 bps to 40 bps. Fixed income yields were somewhere in the range of 27 bps to 28 bps. Liquid and overnight yields were 2 bps to 3 bps. On an overall basis, we were in the range of 37 bps to 38 bps.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target 36-41%, range allows room for investments including AI.
items.quote: We've always maintained that we like to play around 36%, 37% to about 40%, 41%. That's the range we'd like to be in. It gives us room to make investments.

items.statement: SIP AUM grown to about INR41,000 crores; SIP is core strategy.
items.quote: The SIP AUM has actually grown in value and it's now INR41,000 crores in terms of contribution to our AUM.

items.statement: Equity-focused strategy continues; will invest in digital platforms, distributor engagement, product launches, and diversify beyond mutual funds.
items.quote: We will also focus on product launches and also diversify from the mutual fund into other spaces which are available for us.

items.statement: SIP initiatives take time to show results; investments behind strategy.
items.quote: The initiatives we've put in to focus more on SIPs take time to actually show results. So, we request your patience to see the results coming forward. But we're in the right direction, so we are putting investments behind that strategy.

items.statement: Distribution network expanded to over 56,890 empaneled partners; 24% AUM from B30 locations.
items.quote: Distribution network expanded to over 56,890 empaneled partners.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance maintained at 1-2% above industry growth for rest of FY27
items.quote: To sum up, our guidance for credit growth of 1% or 2% over the industry growth will continue for the rest of the quarters.

items.statement: Full year NIM guidance maintained at 3.7-3.8% despite Q1 NIM of 4.26%
items.quote: NIMs for the full year will be in the range of 3.7% to 3.8%.

items.statement: GNPA expected <1.5%, Net NPA <1%, slippages <1% of loan book for FY27
items.quote: Our GNPA is expected to be less than 1.5%. Net NPA will be less than 1% and slippages to be less than 1% of our loan book.

items.statement: Q1 NIM at 4.26% (4.34% including one-off interest recovery), up 1bp QoQ; expect 4%+ in Q2
items.quote: I am pleased to report that we could successfully navigate the quarter and maintain our net interest margin at 4.26. If we reckon one-off item, interest recovery of 8 basis points also will be there. With that, it would become 4.34.

items.statement: Cost of deposits up 4bps QoQ; expect 5-10bps increase next quarter
items.quote: The cost of deposits increased slightly by 4 basis points on a sequential basis as rates of deposits were increased during the quarter. We expect 5 to 10 basis points increase in next quarter.

items.statement: Fixed rate loan book increased to 34% from 29% QoQ; MCLR book down to 9% from 14%; EBLR stable at 55%
items.quote: The fixed rate loan book, which was 29% at the end of March '26, increased to 34% of the total book at the end of June '26. During the same period, the MCLR-linked book reduced from 14% to 9%, while the EBLR book linked remained at 55%.

items.statement: Provided INR163 cr upfront provision last quarter for geopolitical tensions; retained as situation unchanged
items.quote: To recall, we had made a provision of 163 crores towards sectors affected during the ongoing geopolitical tensions during last quarter, and we have retained the same as things still remain the same.

items.statement: ECL transition expected to have limited impact given 1.7% total provisions to advances and strong asset quality
items.quote: The total provisions to advances is at 1.7%, which should take care of the transition ideally.

items.statement: Plan to open 50 branches in H1 FY27; 2 opened in Q1, 25 more by end of Q2
items.quote: We opened two branches during the first quarter. So though we have planned for opening 50 branches during the first half of the year, so we will be completing 25 branches before the end of this quarter and the balance before the end.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio expected to stay within 45-50% range despite branch expansion
items.quote: So it will not have much issues as far as cost is concerned. But one more thing also you need to understand, 32% increase in the net interest income. If other side, the income is going up, our cost is concerned, it has not gone up by 32% even this year, this quarter also.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio yield estimated at 11-12% blended (agri + retail); agri gold loans 92% of agri portfolio
items.quote: Overall, if you can look at it, you can think of between 11% to 12%, we can think that can be the yield we can get in.

items.statement: North America business expected to continue sequential growth trajectory during the year.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect North America business to continue its sequential growth trajectory during the year supported by the upcoming product launches and continued commercial execution.

items.statement: Maintains $1 billion exit run rate for U.S. segment for FY27, dependent on new launches.
items.quote: So, yes, and that is the approval of these will give us a line of sight towards that $1 billion exit rate.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 remains 18.5% to 20%.
items.quote: Yes. So, broadly unchanged, Damayanti.

items.statement: Increased capex towards organic growth, R&D, biosimilars, and in-licensing.
items.quote: See, I think from what we had mentioned earlier in the last quarter, it remains the same where we've increased our capex, which is going towards organic growth.

items.statement: Four significant launches expected in remainder of year: three respiratory assets and one peptide.
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier, our pipe line for the remainder of the year includes 4 significant launches comprising 3 respiratory assets, including generic Advair and the key peptide opportunity as well.

items.statement: War-related cost impact estimated at 1-2% of revenue.
items.quote: But if you could assume about 1% to 2% of revenue in that kind of a range for the overall cost impact due to war.

items.statement: Yurpeak (tirzepatide) growing month-on-month, now second largest brand in anti-obesity category.
items.quote: So, we have reached number two in the whole category. So aft er Mounjaro, in IQVIA, Yurpeak is the second largest brand.

items.statement: Chronic mix strengthened to 60.4% Y-o-Y; targeting further increase over 2-3 years.
items.quote: Our overall chronic mix strengthened this quarter to 60.4% Y -o-Y.

items.statement: South Africa tender loss will continue to impact reported revenue in coming quarters.
items.quote: So, Yes, you will see continuing impact of tender in South Africa.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance at risk if new product launches are delayed.
items.quote: Of course, if there is a change in the plan due to any reason, then there can be risk to this margin guidance, including that of new launches, what you said.

items.statement: Ventolin ramp-up expected towards end of financial year.
items.quote: Yes. So that work is ongoing. We started supplying at the current scale, but I think that will go towards the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Lanreotide not included in Q4 projections; timing fluid due to regulatory approvals.
items.quote: But at this point, we're not including that as part of our Q4 projections.

items.statement: No significant manpower additions planned for India field force this year; focus on productivity.
items.quote: So, at this point, we have approximately 12,000 people in the field force. And for this year, particularly, we are not looking at any significant manpower additions, because we've added in the last two years.

items.statement: Expects double-digit year-on-year revenue growth in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: We expect double-digit revenue growth year-on-year in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Expects near breakeven EBITDA in Q2, positive margins in H2 FY27.
items.quote: On margins, we expect near breakeven at the EBITDA level in Q2, positioning us for positive margins in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Expects stronger revenue growth, improving margin and continued order intake momentum for FY27 vs FY26.
items.quote: We expect stronger revenue growth, improving margin and continued order intake momentum for FY27 as compared to FY26.

items.statement: Past peak capital investment in platform; capex expected to moderate.
items.quote: We are past the peak on capital investment in platform in the current investment cycle, and we expect capital expenditure to moderate from there.

items.statement: Q1 order intake was INR953 million.
items.quote: Order intake in Q1 was at INR953 million.

items.statement: AI programs grew to 9% of total revenue.
items.quote: AI is now embedded across a larger share of our portfolio and revenue from AI programs has grown to 9% of total revenue.

items.statement: Enterprise-to-consumer revenue mix shifted to 65-35 from 68-32 last year.
items.quote: The strong growth in the consumer business has led to a shift in the enterprise to consumer revenue mix from 68-32 in the same period last year to 65-35 in Q1 this year.

items.statement: AI-led training has higher realization but smaller batch sizes than traditional training.
items.quote: AI-led training does have a higher realization than traditional training. But batch sizes will tend to be smaller for AI-led training than the more traditional training

items.statement: BFSI onboarding demand showing early signs of recovery; large private bank L&D budgets remain constrained.
items.quote: In BFSI, the picture is too speed right now. Onboarding demand is showing early signs of recovery, while upskilling and L&D budgets at large private banks remain constrained.

items.statement: AI is a significant demand opportunity happening now, not in the future.
items.quote: AI represents one of the most significant demand opportunities in front of us, and it is happening now, not at some point in the future.

items.statement: Over half of current task content roles face displacement over next 36 months across GSIs.
items.quote: Across GSIs broadly, analysis suggests that more than half of current task content roles face displacement over the next 36 months in ways that have already begun.

items.statement: Activated four new solution lines across insurance, NBFC, wealth and Gen AI with 15+ clients.
items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, NIIT moved beyond its banking anchor to activate four new solution lines across insurance, NBFC, wealth and Gen AI.

items.statement: Operating expenses grew 7% while revenue grew 14%, improving EBITDA path.
items.quote: while our new top line grew by 14%, our operating expenses grew 7%, putting us back on the path to positive EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic opportunities that enhance capabilities, channels or IP with clear returns.
items.quote: we continue to follow a disciplined approach to evaluating inorganic opportunities that enhance capabilities, channels and/or intellectual property and which offer a clear path to returns and cash return.

items.statement: Agrochemicals expected to grow 6-8% in India; seeds mid-to-high single digits excluding cotton.
items.quote: For FY27, the cleaner consensus is that agrochemicals are expected to grow around 6 –8% in India, while seeds likely grow in the mid -to-high single digits but it will depend on the crop.

items.statement: Aims to deliver 15%+ EBITDA margin even in a bad year.
items.quote: So we want to be a consistent company, which delivers 15% plus EBITDA margin even in a bad year.

items.statement: On track to deliver 500 bps EBITDA margin improvement over 5 years.
items.quote: Two years ago, we said we want to deliver 500 basis points over a period of 5 years EBITDA margin, where I think we're on the track.

items.statement: Price increases already taken; mid-season hikes difficult; marginal positive price impact expected.
items.quote: I think price increase during the mid -season is generally very difficult. So whatever price increases have to happen have happened.

items.statement: Cotton business unlikely to grow; focus shifting to rice, maize, millet.
items.quote: Now seed, we have already factored in that this year, it is unlikely that cotton business will gro w.

items.statement: Chilli crop expected to recover this year, benefiting Q2 and Q3.
items.quote: This year, chilli planting intentions are positive, even commodity prices are high. So I think this year, Chilli should see recovery.

items.statement: Shift to post-emergent herbicides from pre-emergent due to delayed sowing.
items.quote: So this year, post -emergent herbicide demand is much more stronger than the pre -emergent.

items.statement: Working capital increased 15-20 days due to fertilizer cash crunch.
items.quote: So working capital, net to net, it has kind of increased by around 15 to 20 days.

items.statement: More cautious on sales return provisions this year due to uncertainty.
items.quote: This year, we would be more cautious in accounting for returns. Probably we'll be accounting more rather than less, right?

items.statement: Herbicide business grew 12% and is largest contributor this quarter.
items.quote: And our herbicide business has grown by 12%.

items.statement: Biologicals expected to perform significantly better than last year.
items.quote: I think overall, I would say biologicals should do better than -- significantly better than last year.

items.statement: Seed industry has surplus inventory this year, helping manage next season.
items.quote: In normal course, I would say, seed industry is sitting on the surplus this year, which should help us in better managing next season.

items.statement: Employee cost increase of ~12% YoY is normal inflation; INR24cr one-time reversal not to repeat.
items.quote: So the increase in the cost would be around 12%, which i s normal in inflation, which always happens year-on-year.

items.statement: Confident of double-digit revenue growth with sustained margins for the year ahead.
items.quote: Building on this strong foundation and sustained momentum, we remain confident of delivering double-digit growth in the year ahead.

items.statement: Q2 top-line performance expected similar or better than Q1.
items.quote: And definitely, the way Q2 has started, it makes us optimistic about doing similar or even better performance on the top line in this quarter.

items.statement: Management fee growth expected to sustain at high teens CAGR.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain confident of sustaining management fee growth at high teens CAGR, supported by a strong pipeline of hotel openings and incremental contributions from newly added hotels.

items.statement: Q2 RevPAR growth expected at least Q1 level, likely surpass.
items.quote: So we are reasonably confident of achieving at least what we have achieved in Q1. And if not, if things go business as usual and there is no big negative, we should at least surpass it comfortably.

items.statement: Frankfurt expected to swing from negative to positive, contributing to margin.
items.quote: I think as we commented earlier, Shaleen, the Frankfurt will swing from negative to positive. And then obviously, that's a contribution to margin that will start happening.

items.statement: TajSATS Q2 similar to Q1, rebound unlikely before Q3.
items.quote: I think Q2 will be similar or somewhat similar. We'll see how that goes. And then by September, October, we will be in a better position to tell you how the full year will look like. But Q2, we are not very hopeful that things will rebound quickly.

items.statement: Renovations translating into stronger pricing power and improved operating performance.
items.quote: These investments are now translating into stronger pricing power and improved operating performance across key markets.

items.statement: Domestic demand resilient, double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands despite macro headwinds.
items.quote: Despite these challenges, however, domestic demand remained resilient. We delivered double-digit RevPAR growth across all our brands, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our market positioning.

items.statement: Consolidated margin has hit 15%; standard range is 15% to 20%, expects further improvement.
items.quote: Our consolidated margin has hit 15%, and our standard range is between 15% and 20%, so we should see it improving only further.

items.statement: Aims to operate all businesses between 15% and 20% EBITDA, roughly 16-17% for the year.
items.quote: All our businesses, our aim is to operate between 15% and 20%, and this is something which we have seen is consistent with the performance.

items.statement: Total order book at end of Q1 stood at INR5,270 crores.
items.quote: At the end of Q1, the total order book stood at INR5,270 crores, providing healthy revenue visibility across both our international and domestic business.

items.statement: Product order book INR1,029 crores; project order book INR4,241 crores, split ~55% international, 45% domestic.
items.value: INR1,029 crores product; INR4,241 crores project
items.quote: No. I think we have given product order of -- the product business order is INR1,029 crores, and the project order is INR4,241 crores.

items.statement: Domestic project order book INR1,921 crores including about INR530 crores of O&M business.
items.quote: The domestic project order book stood at INR1,921 crores with about INR530 crores of O&M business.

items.statement: Expects domestic water sector improvement in second half of the year as sector issues resolve.
items.quote: We expect an improvement in the domestic water sector during the second half of the year as the sector issues are resolved.

items.statement: Believes water sector remains a priority, funds will be released, future outlook good or better.
items.quote: Yes. This is a good question, and I completely believe that the sector remains a priority and the funds will be released and future, there will be good traction in opportunity.

items.statement: MP government debarment: cannot bid new projects until old projects finish; targeting completion within next 1 year.
items.quote: They gave us a debarment basically saying that you cannot bid for new projects until you finish the old projects. And we are addressing those concerns, and hopefully, we can resolve the issue soon.

items.statement: JJM receivables pending roughly INR300-350 crores; expects majority inflow this quarter.
items.quote: Roughly, I think, INR300 crores to INR350 crores, and we should get a majority of that.

items.statement: Most JJM receivables from West Bengal government, less from MP government.
items.quote: So mostly from West Bengal government, less from MP government.

items.statement: South African PCI business is 3-4 year contracts; will further increase during this period.
items.quote: The consolidated margins have gone up to 15%, which was our target. And the South African business, as we have earlier mentioned, is 3- to 4-year contracts. So they are supposed to pick up.

items.statement: Intends to reduce minority shareholding in subsidiaries over medium 2-3 years; PCI buyout in 3 years to 100%.
items.quote: So again, it's a good point. And we -- our intention is to reduce the minority shareholding on all our subsidiaries over the, say, medium 2 to 3 years' time.

items.statement: Project work has price variation contracts covering longer-term raw material cost changes.
items.quote: Yes. Most of our project work has got price variation contracts, so therefore, that takes care of it, which are longer term. And otherwise, not much of a concern on margins.

items.statement: Full-year AUM growth guidance of 18% maintained, subject to revision after Q2.
items.quote: Our earlier guidance of 18% will hold good unless after second quarter, we revise it.

items.statement: Confident of growing more than 15% in the next quarter.
items.quote: But we are confident that we' ll be able to grow more than 15% at least for next quarter.

items.statement: Current NIM to hold for the immediate two quarters, then moderate to 8.5% medium term.
items.quote: See, immediate 2 quarters, I think the current NIM will hold good because we are utilizing the capital.

items.statement: Medium-term NIM guided at around 8.5% as new vehicle mix rises.
items.quote: So our long-term margins of 8.5%, we will be able to manage.

items.statement: Operational NIM to hold around 8.5%; surplus liquidity benefit to gradually subside.
items.quote: So what we were indicating earlier is that the operational NIM will hold at around 8.5%, and we continue to guide that.

items.statement: Incremental bank borrowing cost expected around 8%.
items.quote: But when we start borrowing, I think it would be in the range of around 8%.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds at 7.77%, lower than balance sheet cost of 8.56%.
items.quote: The incremental cost is at 7.77%.

items.statement: New vehicle disbursements at ~16% of total, to rise to 20-25% and book to 30%+ medium term.
items.quote: And it will keep increasing to around 20% to 25% over the period. So definitely, new vehicle book will be around 30% of our book, 30% plus in our book maybe in the medium term.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio expected to double to ~5% of book in 3 years.
items.quote: So we expect the portfolio to grow double in the next 3 years from around 2.5% of the overall book to around 5% because we feel that there's a very big opportunity for us to grow in the gold.

items.statement: MSME share of portfolio to rise from ~15% to ~20%.
items.quote: So from around 15% of the portfolio, the MSME will become around 20% of the book.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of around 2% to hold in near and medium term.
items.quote: Yes, I think it will hold good, but our -- see, our guidance has been around 2%. So it will remain around that in the near term or even in the medium term.

items.statement: Around 150 branches to be added in FY27.
items.quote: Tentatively around 150 branches.

items.statement: Construction equipment demand returning; book to start growing from next quarter.
items.quote: And we believe that there can be a demand coming back into construction equipment. So we should start growing that book from next quarter.

items.statement: Management expects to meet or beat last year's revenue growth for FY27, but gives no specific guidance due to global headwinds.
items.quote: we will be at par or better than what we did last year from the growth perspective.

items.statement: Management declines to give multi-year guidance due to geopolitical and AI-driven uncertainty, reiterating meet-or-beat FY26 growth.
items.quote: At this point, right, if somebody gives you a guidance saying that, you know, three years, this is the number, you know, that's going to be tough to ask at this point.

items.statement: Company has order book visibility for nine months, providing predictable revenue for that period.
items.quote: We have order books for nine months. So, there is a predictable revenue for the next nine months.

items.statement: Second FCCB round delayed due to global headwinds and weak IT sector sentiment; will happen in time.
items.quote: The second round is delayed because of the global headwinds that we are facing, you know, you understand all the global headwinds that are going on, and also today, you know, IT industry is not, or IT companies are not seeing a good limelight.

items.statement: Customers signing contracts but delaying project starts due to their own cashflow concerns in the US.
items.quote: people are signing contracts and are delaying the start because the companies themselves are worried about their cashflow.

items.statement: AI-led inquiries increasing; every project now includes an AI component, though pure AI projects are smaller.
items.quote: A lot of AI-led inquiries are coming in. Yes, some of them are smaller, AI-related projects, pure AI-related projects are small, but whatever we are doing from a translation perspective, yes, there is a component of AI in every project that we are doing now, unlike before.

items.statement: Phoenix.ai modernization accelerator delivers projects 80% faster at half the cost, driving new customer wins.
items.quote: Phoenix.ai is a product or an accelerator that we have launched which helps modernize enterprise legacy systems at almost 80% faster at half the cost.

items.statement: Internal KAI platform delivers 30% efficiency gains in testing, business development, and BA/analysis areas.
items.quote: we have seen 30%, you know, efficiencies coming in in certain areas. Not all of them, but, you know, certain examples are like, you know, testing-related ones, you know, the business development side, also the BA side of it, analysis side of it.

items.statement: JV with Action Energy targets 5% of the billion-dollar digital oil field market within three years, starting in Kuwait.
items.quote: the CEO of Action Energy has already stated that our target is to achieve 5% of the billion market, right, that is out there in this space, especially that transformation of the oil field and the digital oil field platform.

items.statement: Kumori acquisition was for ServiceNow capability, not revenue; contributed about 4 crores last quarter.
items.quote: the last quarter, this quarter's revenue or the last quarter's revenue was about 4 crores. It's not much. That's the reason why I said we acquired that company more for capability and not for revenue.

items.statement: DSO is above 100 days due to Fortune 100 customers with 90-day payment terms and long government invoice cycles.
items.quote: if you look at our DSO days, we are at 100 plus days where we are.

items.statement: Receivables high because company lacks negotiating power with large Fortune 100 customers; take-it-or-leave-it terms.
items.quote: We are a small company. We are not like the large companies that have the muscle power to negotiate. For us, it's like, take it or leave it.

items.statement: Optima digital oil field platform deployment for Oil India completed in under six months across 46 sites and 80 wells.
items.quote: that project has been successfully completed in less than six months. This is done in the Northeast in very difficult terrain across 46 sites of claims as they call them, covering about 80-odd wells.

items.statement: Snowflake partnership upgraded to select tier to strengthen data and AI capabilities and go-to-market.
items.quote: we just strengthened our partnership and moved up to the select tier partner during this quarter.

items.statement: Confident to achieve 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth for full year.
items.quote: We are confident to achieve the target of 10% volume growth in plywood and 25% to 30% volume growth in MDF segment for the full year

items.statement: Confident on 10% plywood margin guidance; expects to achieve once quarterly revenue reaches 600+ crores.
items.quote: I think we still are very confident on the 10% margin guidance that we've given.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin sustainable at 16-17%; may increase by 1% with new capacity operating leverage.
items.quote: So see, as per the capacity right now we have, the EBITDA margin will be around the 16% to 17% on a sustainable basis. Once the other line will come up, where we are doing around 70% extra capacity we are adding, so there will get some operating leverage on that time, the EBITDA margin may increase by 1% further.

items.statement: Total capex for FY27 approximately 500 crores across entities.
items.quote: So for the current financial year, I think in the parent standalone GIL we would have about 47 crores of total capex including loss funding for SAMET. In GSPL we would have at around 100 crores and in GSPPL we would have around 300 crores of capex. So approximately 500 crores of total capex for this financial year.

items.statement: Effective price increase of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood.
items.quote: Consequently, the effective price increase currently stands at approximately 7% to 9% in the MDF business and 3% to 5% in the Plywood business.

items.statement: Peak debt expected at 710-730 crores by March 2027, debt-equity 0.75x; then reducing.
items.quote: at the end of this fiscal year which is 31st March ‘27, we will hit peak debt around in absolute value anything between 710 to 725, 730 something like that. And if you talk about debt equity that day we'll be at 0.75x.

items.statement: New flooring line commercial production started 20 July 2026; potential peak revenue 75-80 crores.
items.quote: The potential peak revenue from this would be at about 75 crores, 80 crores, I think. Somewhere between 75 crores and 80 crores is a potential peak revenue.

items.statement: Plywood utilization target to max out at 98-100%; MDF practical max 80-82%.
items.quote: I think in plywood honestly, we've even gone up to 98, 99, or 100. So obviously the target will be to, you know, max out our, you know, available capacity. And in MDF I don't think it's practical to go above 80 %, 82%.

items.statement: May stop discounting in MDF or take small price increase in plywood if chemical prices continue rising.
items.quote: Maybe that maybe we stop discounting the way we are discounting in MDF, we pull back those schemes and in plywood if it continues this way maybe we take another small increase.

items.statement: Furniture JV targeting revenue of 120-150 crores for FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: I think we'll share that with you. I think should be around 120 crores to 150 crores, that range.

items.statement: New ContiRoll Tech in plywood to yield P&L gains from Q4 FY27.
items.quote: And quarter four onwards you should start seeing some gain on the P&L because of that as well.

items.statement: Furniture JV losses to become zero by mid next year.
items.quote: I think somewhere around next year mid is when we'll, you know, the losses will become zero and going forward from there I think it'll be positive.

items.statement: New laminate plant commercial production by early September; 30% capacity utilization in first year.
items.quote: Commercial production would be 1st of September, first week of September.

items.statement: Expects INR250-300 crore revenue from third plant in current financial year.
items.quote: I think based on the value of what you were saying, around INR250 crores to INR300 crores, it would be easily achieved from the third plant.

items.statement: Margins to remain similar at 19-20% plus even after new capex starts.
items.quote: I think the margins will remain the same, that is why even when the new capex will start end of August. So, we can expect the similar kind of margins 19%, 20% plus.

items.statement: New capex will be in products adjacent to laminates, focused on strengthening domestic market.
items.quote: In laminates there will be a saturation for every company. We do not actually want that. It would be product going along laminates.

items.statement: Domestic market restructuring to show results from Q3 FY27 onwards.
items.quote: And you will definitely see the results from Quarter 3. I won't even say Quarter 2, but you will see the results from Quarter 3 onwards.

items.statement: Phenol around USD1,400/ton; melamine USD1,000-1,100/ton; no further price hike currently planned.
items.value: USD1,400 per ton; USD1,000 to USD1,100
items.quote: Right now, the phenol prices are approximately around USD1,400 per ton. Melamine is around USD1,000 to USD1,100.

items.statement: US tariff remains at 10% as of now; situation uncertain.
items.quote: No, as of now it's 10%, but I think today morning it came a news that US is implementing because the 10% had to go 0% from 24th of July, which was today.

items.statement: Export growth to come from existing geographies plus new ones; Europe strong, APAC and Middle East next.
items.quote: We will generate growth on the existing geographies as well as adding more geographies to the point. And definitely Europe is our most Europe is doing good. Further ahead I think APAC region and Middle East.

items.statement: Logistics is a major challenge globally, including Middle East, but being managed.
items.quote: As of now, see, there are challenges in terms of logistics if we talk about right now for Middle East. In fact, for the entire world right now logistics is a very big problem, but that is a part of the business.

items.statement: Aica is a strategic partner; no daily involvement, only potential technology transfer.
items.quote: Secondly, no involvement from their side as they are themselves, they are a strategic partner. And as of now there is no discussions about export to them or anything of that sort.

items.statement: Domestic volume ramp-up slowly in Q2, significant ramp-up in Q3 FY27.
items.quote: So, you will slowly slowly see in Q2 also you in Q2 also you would see the ramp-up of the volume. Definitely Q3 you'll see a significant ramp-up.

items.statement: Management expects 22% growth trajectory to continue in FY27.
items.quote: Nishita, we are quite excited and positive that the growth will continue. It's -- yes, we are confident it will continue.

items.statement: Full-year capex guidance maintained at INR600 crores; INR89 crores already spent in Q1.
items.quote: So rest of the year, we have guided earlier INR600 crores. We still remain INR600 crores, INR89 crores is already spent.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stay in the 22-23% range.
items.quote: Yes, Nishita. We expect that to continue.

items.statement: Complex generics mix shift should continue to offset raw material cost pressures.
items.quote: But like you said, the mix is really helping us. Move towards more complex generics is helping us. And we have every reason to believe that it will continue.

items.statement: Pursuing calibrated pricing actions and cost pass-through with customers to mitigate cost inflation.
items.quote: We continue to closely monitor the situation and where appropriate, pursuing calibrated pricing actions and cost pass -through mechanism with customers to mitigate the impact of sustained cost inflation for the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Complex generics now 50% of finished dosages, up from 39% a year ago; growth sustainable.
items.quote: Complex generics, which were around 39% of our finished dosages a year ago are now 50%.

items.statement: Peptide CDMO targeting USD 50 million revenue with 30%+ EBITDA in about 3 years.
items.value: USD 50 million revenue with 30% plus EBITDA
items.quote: So that's very clear, USD 50 million revenue with 30% plus EBITDA, somewhere in the third year from now, mid of third year from now, should be our run rate.

items.statement: Peptide CDMO aims to be PAT positive on annual basis in FY27.
items.quote: As stated earlier, our focus for FY27 remains delivering a PAT positive performance on an annual basis, while recognizing the quarter -to-quarter variability inherent in a project -driven CDMO business.

items.statement: Peptide India investment: ~INR100 crores intermediate, INR200 crores API side initially.
items.value: INR100 crores intermediate; INR200 crores API
items.quote: our initial estimates suggest roughly about INR100 crores numbers on the intermediate side, and if you take it forward to the API side, we are starting with INR200 crores of investment plan.

items.statement: Expects about 9 US launches this year pending FDA approval; 18 approvals pending overall.
items.quote: This year, if -- pending the FDA approval, we are expecting about 9 launches. And overall, we have about 18 approvals that are still pending, 9 of which will be launched immediately after the FDA clear GGP and plus another 1 product from GPI and the remain ing are IP -based.

items.statement: Oncology first self-developed backward-integrated product to launch starting FY28-29; 9-13 products in development.
items.quote: Going forward, though, starting in FY28, '29, we launched our first self -developed product, which is fully backward integrated, and it will have geographical presence -- geographical expansions.

items.statement: R&D spend expected at 5.5% to 6% of sales going forward.
items.quote: This will be around 5.5% to 6% as we go ahead.

items.statement: Gagillapur remediation complete; 9 applications ready to launch pending FDA clearance.
items.quote: Our remediation work is essentially complete. We met the FDA in January, and we have submitted every response on time. To date, the agency has not raised a single concern on the adequacy or the pace of our corrective actions.

items.statement: Genome Valley facility scaling; utilization expected to cross 50% by year-end.
items.quote: And Yashika on the second question onGLS, currently, the utilization levels are very low. By the year-end, we are expecting it will cross 50%.

items.statement: Targets 16-18% AUM CAGR FY26-FY31, with mobility at 12% and new businesses at 30%+
items.quote: I did mention that we are looking at the franchise compound at a 16% to 18% growth, right?

items.statement: Maintains overall credit cost guidance band of 1.3% to 1.7%
items.quote: I would stand by my earlier guidance of 1.3% to 1.7% overall credit cost.

items.statement: Aims to progress ROA from 2% to 2.2% and eventually 2.5%; no fiscal year-end ROA guidance
items.quote: So we talked about hitting 2% climbing to 2.2% and then getting eventually to 2.5%.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds to stay in current range, around 10 bps plus/minus
items.quote: So I think overall, we should be in the ballpark in this kind of range, 10 bps plus/minus here and there.

items.statement: Continues to carry additional liquidity buffer of about INR 5,000 crores due to geopolitical caution
items.quote: So on a cautious side, we as of now continue to carry an additional liquidity buffer of close to INR 5,000 crores.

items.statement: Mobility business to grow at industry-plus rates across 3W, 4W, tractor, CV
items.quote: So structurally, the mobility business will definitely see industry and we are aiming for industry plus growth across the 3-wheeler, 4-wheeler, tractor, CV business.

items.statement: Non-wheels franchise growing 28-30%, wheels 11-12%, to maintain overall 16-18% growth
items.quote: the mobility -- the wheels franchise has compounded at 11% to 12% and the non-wheels franchise has started compounding at a 28% to 30%.

items.statement: Tightened underwriting for El Nino-vulnerable tractor customers via scorecards and LTVs
items.quote: our underwriting scorecards, as usual, assess what the agri output should be to repay the kind of the levels that they are borrowing

items.statement: Housing subsidiary boards to decide on mandate by Q2 this fiscal
items.quote: we had specifically mentioned that both the Boards will sit on judgment on this by Q2 of this fiscal.

items.statement: Went live with one bank for co-lending in PV business this quarter
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have gone live in the PV business with one bank in this quarter.

items.statement: Monitoring IRDAI regulations on insurance commissions; confident products are clean
items.quote: We know that something is coming regarding a very prescriptive manner in terms of what commissions are going to be, etc.

items.statement: AI agent Samur.AI coverage in CPC operations rose from 20% to 45%
items.quote: now covering from 20% where we gave the last update of our CPC operations which are agentic in nature, that's climbed very quickly to 45%

items.statement: AI vernacular bots coverage for collections up to 20%, expected to rise
items.quote: So our AI vernacular bots coverage has gone up to 20%, and you'll see a much higher clip going forward.

items.statement: Maintains medium-term through-cycle credit cost guidance of 1.3% to 1.7%, expects lower end if execution holds.
items.quote: I would still stay with that 1.3% to 1.7% for the business model from a medium term.

items.statement: Reiterates AUM CAGR guidance of 16% to 18% over five years, driven by non-wheels growth.
items.quote: I would stick to the 16% to 18% range because there is a very strong non-wheels assumption, not assumption, but a tuck-in ambition in that.

items.statement: Non-wheels businesses targeted to grow at 30% consolidated CAGR.
items.quote: So consol 4-year CAGR is the number that I talked about 30%.

items.statement: Wheels business expected to grow 11% to 12%.
items.quote: the wheels business should grow at 11% to 12% and the newer businesses should grow at 30%.

items.statement: Opex to average assets target band of 2.5% to 2.7%; below that risks credit cost compromise.
items.quote: I've always said being in the 2.5% to 2.7% clip is a business model requirement for us.

items.statement: No capital raise expected for at least 6 to 8 quarters; Tier 1 at 16.5%, well above regulatory requirement.
items.quote: I don't see us in the next at least 6 to 8 quarters requiring capital.

items.statement: Cost of funding rose 10 bps QoQ; no concern about steep increase going forward.
items.quote: we have seen a 10 basis points of increase in the CoF compared to last quarter.

items.statement: Loan income fell ~25 bps QoQ largely due to INR5,500 crore enhanced liquidity buffer; may reverse when conditions improve.
items.quote: it is the loan income, which has fallen by about 25 bps, right? Now there's a big contribution of that 25 bps completely to the liquidity buffer, enhanced liquidity buffer of INR5,500 crores that we are carrying

items.statement: Tractor Q1 strong due to delayed rains extending buying cycle; expects contracted Q2 as a result.
items.quote: anything which happens in Q1 will have a bearing in Q2, so you might see a contracted Q2 because of an accelerated Q1.

items.statement: Monsoon departure from normal higher in Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat; too early to assess, hopes for normalization.
items.quote: the departure from normal is higher in states like Rajasthan and MP and Gujarat for now. But too early, are still in its first stage, which we hope that things can normalize.

items.statement: No major shift seen in tractor mix between haulage and agri; playing out as usual.
items.quote: Your second question on whether the mix of haulage versus agri, I'm not seeing a big shift in that. It's playing out as usual for us.

items.statement: Housing subsidiary merger proposal to be taken to both Boards by Q2 of this fiscal.
items.quote: the proposal will be taken to both the Boards by Q2 of this fiscal. So hopefully, we'll give you an update next quarter.

items.statement: MIBL insurance broking PAT grew QoQ from 21% to 38%; expanding beyond motor into reinsurance and commercial lines.
items.quote: Q-o-Q, they have grown from PAT 21% to 38%.

items.statement: Credit cost could be at lower end of 1.3-1.7% range if execution holds; overlays created for monsoon risk.
items.quote: if we continue to execute well, we'll be in the lower end of that range. If too many curveballs come away, we will but definitely be within that range.

items.statement: India growth expected to continue at 12-15%, close to Q1/Q2 levels, with market slowdown expected in H2.
items.quote: Now moving forward, we are talking about a growth in the range of 12% to 15% is what has happened in these two quarters this year. I think going forward also, we are trying to maintain, as Ander was saying that we are proceeding in a measured way.

items.statement: Expects gradual slowing of growth over next few quarters as GST cuts taper and below-normal monsoon hits rural incomes.
items.quote: Market demand was robust in Q2 C26, though we expect a gradual slowing down of growth over the next few quarters as the effect of GST cuts tapers down and the negative impact of an expected below normal monsoon season starts impacting rural incomes.

items.statement: Cost inflation hit margins; countervailing measures to recover most of 80 bps drop over next two quarters.
items.quote: As far as margins are concerned, we have seen a drop of about 80 bps this quarter, largely because of the cost inflation. A large part of that will be recouped in the next two quarters.

items.statement: H2 CY26 capex expected significantly higher than H1; H1 capex was INR2.1 billion.
items.quote: The capex during H1 C26 was INR2.1 billion as compared to INR3.8 billion in full year CY25. The growth capex is mainly concentrated in India. The capex in H2 C26 is expected to be significantly higher than in the first half of the year.

items.statement: New order book of about INR5 billion per year won in H1 CY26, in line with internal targets.
items.quote: We have had a new order book around INR5 billion per year. That's the new order book that we have got till during the first half of the year. So we are in line with our internal targets.

items.statement: New US iron foundry program to add about INR2,000 million annual turnover; new line being built.
items.quote: we are now ramping up one big program for our American customers. So this will give us around INR2,000 million per year of new turnover that will fulfill our capacities in the country. So we need to expand our foundry, and we will build a new line

items.statement: European forgings market weak; expects 2-3% drop this year and similar next year.
items.quote: the forgings, the market in Europe is weak as we highlighted, I mean, in the next years, the market will continue this weak, let's say, evolution. There will be a drop of around 2%, 3% this year. Next year will be similar.

items.statement: Restructuring aluminum portfolio by exiting loss-making products; rebalancing toward four-wheeler aluminum.
items.quote: the restructuring of our business portfolio at our aluminum vertical, wherein we have let go of some loss-making products.

items.statement: Gears grew 18%, composites 17%, stamping 16% in the quarter.
items.quote: In Gears, we grew in this quarter we grew 18%, for example, okay? In Composite 17%, Stamping 16%.

items.statement: Chinese OEMs gaining share in Europe; European suppliers disadvantaged for next 2 years until Chinese localize supply chain.
items.quote: as we see it for the next 2 years, the more market share Chinese gain, European automotive suppliers, auto component suppliers are at a disadvantage.

items.statement: Net financial debt negative INR14.2 billion; actively evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities.
items.quote: The consolidated net financial debt at the end of H1 C26 was negative INR14.2 billion, which means we have healthy liquid cash available, and we are actively evaluating organic and inorganic growth opportunities.

items.statement: Iron castings export dispatches started; revenue recognition from next quarter due to long supply chain.
items.quote: Dispatches have happened. I think revenue recognition will happen from the next quarter. Because the supply chain is long.

items.statement: Targets at least 30% presales growth for FY27, possibly better if launches happen on time.
items.quote: The last quarter, I mean, like end of the financial year, so we have guided for at least 30% growth in the presales. That I think we should be able to continue to achieve.

items.statement: Plans to complete 6-6.5 million sq ft in FY27 versus 5.4 million sq ft last year.
items.quote: We plan to complete about 6 to 6.5 million square feet for FY ’27 as against last year’s completion of about 5.4 million square feet, which can be about 20% higher.

items.statement: Confident of launching 9 projects totaling ~8.2 million sq ft in remaining FY27, GDV ~INR12,000 crores.
items.quote: Of this, we are confident of launching 9 projects, aggregating approximately 8.2 million square feet during the remaining period of FY ’27.
