One of the things we had mentioned was that we will premiumize the product and the combination of price actions as well as the mix has moved the average unit realization by 73% to INR14.4 lakhs during the quarter.

items.statement: Over 40% of Keystone sales from 10-year Ivory product, the middle segment
items.quote: If I look at the mix, I think that is also evolving positively. A majority, about more than 40% of our sales are now coming from the 10-year product, which is the Ivory as we call it, and that is the middle segment.

items.statement: Occupancy improved to 86.7% during the quarter, reflecting sustained demand across the network
items.quote: If I look at the occupancy metric, it improved to 86.7% duri ng the quarter, reflecting sustained demand across the network.

items.statement: Expect to add ~1,000 keys gross in FY27 across Jodhpur, Ganpatipule, Darjeeling, Jawai, Dalhousie, Goa and other destinations
items.quote: If I look at the FY27 number, we expect to add about 1,000 keys at the gross level. And this is across multiple destinations.

items.statement: Exit 300-400 more keys over next 3 quarters; total 600-700 keys exit planned for FY27
items.quote: During the course of the year, we actually expect to exit another 300 to 400 keys over the course of the next 3 quarters, in line with that.

items.statement: Standalone profit down INR22 cr YoY; 30% from 400 keys under renovation, 20% from new resorts stabilizing, 25% from capability/branding investment, 10-15% regulatory (GST, solar)
items.quote: If I look at the journey and the delta of about INR22 crores, about 30% is coming because, as I mentioned, there are about 400 keys, which are generating no revenues today. And there is some cost already in the system.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 stronger as renovated keys return, new inventory adds, new resorts turn profitable; Q2 is seasonally weakest quarter
items.quote: One is the 400 keys, renovated keys will come back into the system that should really help in terms of more availability and improved performance for us. The second thing, as I mentioned, is inventory will start coming as we go forward. And I think we are also approaching the 2 best quarters, which will be Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: HCRO (Holiday Club Finland) loss increased ~INR20 cr YoY; strategic review ongoing, expect conclusion during FY27; all options open including partnership or exit
items.quote: I think the European business, if I look at it, I think there was an increased loss of about, give or take, INR20 crores compared to Q1 of last year. This is our Holiday Club Finland business. As I mentioned in the past, I think it is going through a bad phase in terms of the demand cycle. And we have mentioned before

items.statement: Theog signature resort delayed 3-4 quarters to Q3/Q4 FY28; cost overrun estimated 5-10%; civil structure nearly complete
items.quote: As of now, I think this will be probably in the second half of F '28, somewhere in probably the fourth quarter is what we are targeting. which was originally supposed to be. So it's about -- my sense is about 3 or 4 quarters behind where we thought it would be.

items.statement: Two more signature resorts in pipeline: second in mid-design stage, third in early design; plan to break ground on second in FY27; construction typically 2.5-3 years
items.quote: Another resort, and I won't tell you the destination right now, but another resort is in late stages of design in terms of the layout, etcetera, which is going to be a second resort. And hopefully, that we should be able to break ground on that in this financial year if everything goes according to plan.

items.statement: Deferred revenue INR5,825 cr; cash balance INR1,420 cr; provides significant financial leverage for transformation and expansion
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong. Deferred revenue stands at INR5,825 crores, and the cash balance stands at INR1,420 crores. This provides us significant financial leverage to fund our ongoing transformation and expansion road map.

items.statement: Dividend unlikely in FY27; earliest consideration FY28 due to Ind AS 115 transition difference of INR1,509 cr
items.quote: So I think in F '26 -- sorry, F '27, we will be in a position of not being able to pay a dividend. I think the earliest we can probably consider a dividend is going to be F '28 at this point in time.

items.statement: Non-member (FIT) business grew 30% YoY in Q1; realization up ~10% YoY; rates comparable to member rates but best yielding days reserved for members
items.quote: If I look at the realization compared to last year, it has jumped about 10% and that's another focus that we'll keep moving up yield even in that business.

items.statement: Reaffirmed USD 100 million revenue guidance for FY27 and USD 200 million for FY28 for CrudeChem (CCTL) business
items.quote: you gave a guidance last quarter that of USD 100 million in FY27 and USD 200 million in FY28 from this segment

items.statement: Commissioned major capacity expansion at Texas facility, increasing total manufacturing capacity to ~148,000 MTPA from 80,000 MTPA
items.quote: During this quarter, we commissioned a major expansion -- capacity expansion at our Texas manufacturing facility, increasing the total manufacturing capacity to approximately 148,000 metric tons per year

items.statement: Successfully passed on increased raw material costs to customers despite geopolitical volatility, preserving blended margins
items.quote: During the quarter, despite the volatility in the global raw material prices arising from geopolitical developments in the Middle East, we successfully passed on the increased input cost to customers, thereby preserving healthy blended margins.

items.statement: Healthy balance sheet with high cash reserves; disciplined capital allocation for organic growth and selective M&A; no immediate fund raise indicated
items.quote: We continue to remain and maintain a healthy balance sheet and providing us the flexibility to pursue growth organic expansions and selective inorganic expansions and opportunities going forward.

items.statement: CrudeChem EBITDA margin estimated at minimum 13-14% on standalone basis; significant margin expansion post-acquisition due to synergies, technology transfer, cost reduction
items.quote: the margins have to be minimum 13% there, 13% to 14%, which is very good in terms of these volumes and the value revenue

items.statement: Targets healthy double-digit blended revenue growth for FY27, aiming to outpace industry digital growth by a couple of percentage points.
items.quote: We are intending to outdo that by at least a couple of percentage points overall. So, blended growth, I think, should we should be at, the aim is to be at more than, I mean, at a healthy double-digit kind of a growth rate.

items.statement: Aims for full-year FY27 EBITDA positivity and bottom-line profitability in FY28.
items.quote: The aim will be for the year to be EBITDA positive at least. And yes, I think we are very confident that next year we will be bottom-line positive also.

items.statement: Aspires to achieve upwards of 20% EBITDA margin over a 2-3 year horizon on a reported basis.
items.quote: I think if I see a 2-3 year perspective, I think definitely upwards of 20% EBITDA is something that we should aim for.

items.statement: New initiatives investment to be reduced by over 50% in FY27 vs FY26, primarily by scaling back traditional media content creation.
items.quote: On the new initiatives, I think we have guided that we will use it by more than 50% in FY27 compared to FY26. And I assume a large part of that will come because the traditional media side, we will kind of contain our turn.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 2 crore; excluding INR 20 crore new initiatives spend, existing operations EBITDA would be INR 18 crore.
items.quote: Adjusting for these investments, the EBITDA for existing operations for the quarter would have been around INR 18 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty caused deferral of select B2B syndication deals, contributing to 17% YoY digital revenue decline in Q1.
items.quote: Digital revenue for the quarter declined by 17% year-on-year, as select B2B syndication deals were deferred on account of geopolitical uncertainty, coupled with the inherently lumpy nature of this B2B side of the business.

items.statement: FAST channel ecosystem globally degrowing for 12-18 months; Shemaroo reduced channels to two, keeping it experimental.
items.quote: In terms of the FAST ecosystem globally, it has actually been degrowing in the last, I would say about almost 18 to 12 to 18 months, it has been degrowing. So there was a point when there was a huge number of FAST channels up there and that number has shrunk significantly now globally.

items.statement: Traditional media revenue expected flat in FY27 (not de-growing), digital double-digit growth, leading to overall double-digit top-line growth.
items.quote: Digital we are anticipating or we are looking forward to a double-digit growth rate. And traditional should probably be flat to, yes, I would imagine it would be flattish, not a degrowth.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex was close to INR 3,500 crores; focus on deploying logged-in opportunities and completing projects
items.quote: One significant thing is that we delivered a quarterly capex of about -- close to INR3,500 crores of capex. And that is what we are focusing and we will continue to focus that we continue to deploy all those logged-in opportunity on the ground and complete these projects one by one.

items.statement: Smart meter installation reached 1.34 crore (13.4 million) cumulatively against order book of 2.46 crore (24.6 million); IntelliSmart acquisition will expand portfolio to ~4.7 crore (47 million) meters with natural growth provisions
items.quote: We have also now completed the smart meter installation of 1.34 crore s or 13.4 million meters cumulatively on the order book of 2.46 crores or 24.6 million. In addition, you must have seen the news that we are acquiring IntelliSmart. And combined IntelliSmart and AESL, we'll have a portfolio of about 4.7 crores or 47

items.statement: Transmission capex target of INR 20,000-25,000 crores annually, maintaining ~25% market share; STU pipeline expected at INR 20,000-25,000 crores annually; HVDC projects KPS-1 by Dec FY29, Bhadla-Fatehpur by early FY29
items.quote: See, Aditya, we have been doing a market share of about 25%. And we will at least continue that part from our side. So roughly about INR20,000 crores, INR25,000 crores of capex addition every year.

items.statement: Energy Solutions platform now full-scale: 5,000 MW supply tied up (4,000 MW from AGEL, 1,000 MW third-party), 3,500 MWh battery storage contracted; 350 MW C&I customers secured, targeting 7.5 GW market opportunity by 2031
items.quote: Now the energy solutions platform, which we are talking since last couple of quarters, has now transitioned to a full -scale business, we were incubating that. So we tied up about 5,000 megawatts of capacity on a supply side. And these are mainly green energy supply.

items.statement: Energy Solutions Q1 EBIT INR 590 crores: INR 570 crores from long-term contracted capacity (3,325 MUs), balance from services/trading (9,800 MUs); service margin ~Paisa 0.3/unit; long-term spreads contract-to-contract
items.quote: So the breakup is about 570 crores is from the volume that where we have taken a position, where we have a long -term contract. The balance revenue is from power trading and power solution services activity.

items.statement: Data center demand pipeline robust: 1 GW IT load requires 1.5 GW consumption load, 3.5-4x renewable capacity plus storage; all data centers grid-connected; C&I market 50+ GW by 2030-31
items.quote: So from the overall demand side, we are looking at a very robust pipeline, where for every gigawatt of IT loads, you are talking about 1.5x of the consumption load. And say, for 1.5 gigawatt of consumption load, we are talking about on -- if we want to supply from renewables, 3.5x to 4x of renewable capacity required a

items.statement: Renewable supply contracts market-linked, not tender-based; bilateral sale prices range INR 3-15/unit depending on product (bundled, storage-shaped); battery storage contracted on fixed hire basis
items.quote: It is essentially a market -linked. So, we evaluate when we buy as to what are the options available with us in terms of quantum and pricing, and we decide based on that.

items.statement: Energy Solutions currently has timing mismatch: 3,325 MUs sold, only 400-500 MUs under long-term contracts; rest sold on exchange/bilateral (1-13 month tenors); aim to close positions back-to-back to reduce volatility
items.quote: Currently, out of the 3,300 -odd million units, about 400 or 500 would be on a contract basis, which is with 350 megawatts of C&I customers. But you will see most of the volume getting absorbed in the long-term sale contract very soon.

items.statement: Parallel license matter in Maharashtra pending with commission; state government advised waiting for central tariff policy amendment before proceeding
items.quote: So that matter is still pending with commission. There is no movement. And we believe that state -- Maharashtra government has given a policy advice to commission to wait till the amendment in tariff policy, which the central government is planning to do.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 started on a softer note; historically weaker quarter
items.quote: While Q2 is historically a weaker quarter and it has begun on a softer note.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 20% in Q1 FY27 from 1.9% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded to 20 % compared to 1.9% in Q1 FY26, reflecting the benefits of structural cost optimization, disciplined expense management and improved operating leverage.

items.statement: Management believes cost base is at optimal level; no further significant savings expected
items.quote: So I think we have done most of the cost savings, and this should be an optimum level of cost per quarter that you are looking at.

items.statement: Creative business (Radio Plus) rebounded to INR9.8 cr; advertiser spend mix shifting toward solutions
items.quote: The pure radio advertising is subdued. And the created business, which is the Radio Plus business is where we are seeing traction. So that mix of spend of the advertiser is slightly shifting.

items.statement: Government ad spend unpredictable; treated as independent vertical to maximize share
items.quote: So the government continues to be a very important contributor to the radio business. And however, it's difficult to predict government spends because it depends on elections and it depends on all the other factors.

items.statement: Seasonality: H1 contributes ~45% of annual revenue, H2 ~55%
items.quote: Like quarter 1 vis-a-vis the -- like H1 typically contributes about 45% of your business and H2 goes to 55% of the business.

items.statement: Digital revenue is 4% of total revenue
items.quote: And the second question on the digital share, it is 4% of the revenue as of now.

items.statement: 80% of advertisers are recurring; 20% new business each quarter
items.quote: Typically, we -- every quarter, we get about 20% of new business. Which are new businesses are businesses who haven't advertised with us in the last 1 year, but 80% seems to be recurring advertisers.

items.statement: No new ventures or horizontal/vertical expansion in pipeline
items.quote: Currently, nothing is on pipeline.

items.statement: No buyback plans; holding INR270 cr net cash as of June 2026
items.quote: Currently, no plans are there.

items.statement: No further impairment expected if share price and performance sustain; share price still below net book value
items.quote: Going forward, if this continues, we don't see any further impairment, but that will be, again, will be checked at the year-end when the year-end performances are done.

items.statement: Manpower at optimal level; focus now on efficiency and revenue growth
items.quote: We believe we're at optimal level right now. Now all energies are focused on improving efficiencies and increasing revenues.

items.statement: Priorities: accelerate revenue growth, enhance monetization, expand client relationships, unlock digital/adjacent opportunities
items.quote: As we move forward, our priorities remain centered on accelerating revenue growth, enhancing monetization across platforms, expanding client relationships and unlocking new opportunities across digital and adjacent businesses.

items.statement: Technology expenditure is close to INR 1,000 crores, around 12%-13% of total opex.
items.quote: It's close to INR1,000 crores. Around 12%-13%.

items.statement: Gold loan business grew 130% YoY and 15% QoQ to INR 4,500 crores; distribution expanded to over 1,300 branches.
items.quote: Gold loan business grew by 130% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter to reach INR4,500 crores. We initiated gold loan product across 400-plus existing branches during the quarter, taking total gold loan distributions to over 1,300 branches.

items.statement: MFI portfolio capped at up to 10% of total book to meet PSL and small farmer obligations; 96% covered under CGFMU guarantee.
items.quote: Overall, as a component, we have publicly announced that it could go up to as high as 10%. Because you know our requirement of SMAs is also now 10% and we don't have any other Agri book as such.

items.statement: ECL framework implementation impact expected to be neutral given low historical LGDs; better visibility by end of Q3 FY27.
items.quote: historical trend of our LGDs and PDs, especially LGDs on our asset classes are very, very low. So that gives us enough comfort to say that the impact would be neutral, right? We don't expect much to in terms of any additional hit on the balance sheet. However, I think, closer to maybe end of Q3 or something, we would b

items.statement: Cost of funds stable at 6.48%; SA deposit cost ~5.05%, TD cost ~7.25%; FCNR rates increased to ~7.5% to attract flows.
items.quote: Cost of funds remained broadly stable at 6.48%. Increased cost on savings accounts and wholesale funding was offset by residual repricing of retail term deposits.

items.statement: CD ratio ex-refinance at ~80%; management comfortable with current level for balance sheet optimization.
items.quote: CD ratio ex-refinance is ~80%. So we don't look this number to optimize anything, right. It is just the number for our sustenance, right? How much we should raise deposits and how much we can do the loan.

items.statement: Expect cost-to-assets ratio to improve on full-year basis; operating leverage to play out.
items.quote: Operating leverage continues to play out on underlying basis and we expect cost to assets ratio to improve on a full-year basis.

items.statement: Additional one-time provision of INR 23 crores taken for alignment of unsecured product provisioning norms.
items.quote: PAT for the quarter included an additional one-time provision of INR23 crores from further strengthening of NPA provisioning norms in selected products.

items.statement: Personal loan book 100% sourced from existing bank customers (99% liability customers); credit card and PL businesses still scaling.
items.quote: This is, this book is 100% as of now is towards our existing bank customer. And majority of them would be liability customer, some of them would be asset customers.

items.statement: NSFR typically ranges 105-115%; LCR ranges 115-120%; management operates within these bands.
items.quote: LCR range is around 115 to 120 and our NSFR typically is about 105 to 115. That's where we range.

items.statement: Professional lighting sees healthy project inquiry pipeline; street lighting and facade projects executing
items.quote: Professional Lighting continues to gain traction, aided by execution of key street lighting and facade projects, and we continue to see healthy project inquiry pipeline

items.statement: Commodity volatility (copper, aluminum), minimum wage hikes, fuel costs, import delays, geopolitical uncertainty driving broad-based cost increases; war ongoing, inflation unpredictable
items.quote: Persistent commodity inflation, particularly copper and aluminum, increase in minimum wages, inflating labor cost and their availability, alongside rising fuel cost, import delays and broader geopolitical uncertainty

items.statement: Management expects margins to improve to previous levels or better once Middle East crisis ends and US/Qatar supply increases
items.quote: once this crisis in Middle East is over, we see a lot of supply coming in from U.S. and the Qatar region. So that will help us to get better rates in the coming years -- in the coming months. So once this happens and the Middle East crisis is over, we'll see the margins improving to the last level or better than that.

items.statement: Spot purchases currently 15% of consumption after curtailment; mid-term procurement being pursued to reduce spot exposure
items.quote: Spot volumes are around 15% of the total consumption after the curtailment.

items.statement: Gas sourcing mix: 40% domestic APM+NWG, 48% long-term contracts, pooled gas mechanism withdrawn by government
items.quote: If you look at the domestic APM and NWG allocation, that is around 40%. And on the longer-term contracts, we have 48%. And if you look at the current -- during the pooled mechanism, volumes were available from the allocation and which has been withdrawn after the peace deal

items.statement: NWG price at 12% of Indian crude basket, significantly above $5/MMBTU last quarter; Brent above $107/bbl drove up NWG and imported RLNG costs
items.quote: It is 12% of the Indian crude basket. And it is significantly more than $5 per MMBTU level during the last quarter.

items.statement: CNG volume grew 18% YoY; double-digit growth across passenger vehicles, light commercial vehicles, taxi aggregators; OEM CNG vehicle sales growing ~30%
items.quote: If you see entire CNG segment, whether it is light commercial vehicles or passenger vehicles or taxi aggregators, I mean growth is in double digits, entire value chain in terms of the infrastructure, which is being planned all across country in terms of CNG stations added, it is in double digit.

items.statement: Slightly higher capex budget vs last year; dedicated task force for domestic PNG connections; monitoring gas scenarios and high-growth areas
items.quote: Yes, we have slightly higher budget compared to last year, but we are monitoring the situation in end-to-end basis, in terms of the gas of the scenarios, in terms of the areas where the growth is very evident

items.statement: Steel pipeline network expanded to 15,987 inch-km; added 38,000 household connections (total 11.41 lakh), 5 CNG stations (total 707), 392 commercial and 56 industrial customers
items.quote: steel pipeline expanded to 15,987-inch kilometres further strengthening our distribution network to support future growth. During the quarter, we added 38,000 new households' connection, taking our total customer base to 11.41 lakh households in domestic segment.

items.statement: EV charging network expanded to 5,306 points (58 MW); sold 3.3 million kWh, 100% YoY growth; target 10,000 charging points
items.quote: Our EV charging network expanded to 5,306 charging points within installation capacity of 58 megawatts. We sold 3.3 million electrons during the quarter and delivered robust growth of 100% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Industry representations made to restore pooled gas mechanism; government may reinstate it if Middle East tensions persist
items.quote: Probably there is some development also, probably government is looking at a bringing impact again because it definitely has an impact on the CGD industry as a whole and directly impacting the consumer also.

items.statement: PNG connections to maintain current run-rate; exploring reticulated/LPG conversion models to accelerate; per capita domestic consumption ~0.38-0.4 SCMD
items.quote: We would at least maintain the same rate at which we are right now doing it. So that is how our aim is, while we're also exploring multiple options or the business models, which will help us to accelerate these numbers

items.statement: Volume growth momentum to continue; no major issues seen as CNG/PNG/industrial infrastructure keeps expanding
items.quote: if you see our volume growth, that will continue to grow in a similar manner. And right now, the challenge is only to build the gap above the spot volumes. That is where we are working towards ensuring that we continually -- we maintain the momentum.

items.statement: Cement demand expected to grow at healthy 7% in FY27
items.quote: I believe the cement demand will also grow at a healthy rate of 7% in this financial year.

items.statement: Industry cement demand grew 7-8% YoY in Q1 FY27
items.quote: As per analyst estimates, cement demand for the industry grew by about 7% to 8% Y-o-Y in quarter 1.

items.statement: Organic volume growth targeted in line with industry at 7-8%
items.quote: I think for our organic numbers, we should be in line with the industry. We are chasing more, but at least in line with the industry.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance maintained at INR3,200-3,400 crores excluding acquisition cost
items.quote: Our capex commitment for FY27 is expected to remain at around INR3,200 crores to INR3,400 crores, in line with our earlier guidance.

items.statement: Jaypee Cement assets acquired adding 5.2 mt cement and 3.3 mt clinker capacity in Central India
items.quote: This acquisition brings 5.2 million tons of cement capacity, supported by 3.3 million tons of clinker capacity in the strategically important Central India region.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton improved 3% QoQ to INR1,055 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA per ton improved 3% Q-o-Q to INR1,055 during the quarter.

items.statement: Price increases of INR10-15 in South and INR15-20 in East markets passed on cost inflation
items.quote: Healthy price increases of about INR10 to INR15 in South and INR15 to INR20 in East markets enabled us to pass on a significant portion of the input cost inflation.

items.statement: Cost savings of over INR150 per ton achieved through procurement and operational initiatives
items.quote: Collectively, these initiatives generated savings of more than INR150 per ton during the quarter.

items.statement: Q1 volume growth of 9% YoY despite state elections in key markets
items.quote: Despite these market-specific challenges, we have delivered a robust volume growth of 9% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Premium product share reached 25% of portfolio; Weather365 premium-plus offering launched
items.quote: More importantly, this growth was accompanied by a marked improvement in the quality of our sales, and the share of premium products in our portfolio has moved to a healthy number of 25%.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in West Asia creating cost uncertainty; monsoon progress and El Nino being monitored
items.quote: This quarter was largely impacted by cost escalations stemming from West Asia conflict. While input costs have moderated from their peak levels, the recent resurgence in hostilities will remain a key factor influencing cost trends in the near term.

items.statement: Total cement capacity to reach ~67 mt by Q3 FY28 with Belgaum, Kadapa, Pune and Jaypee projects
items.quote: With this acquisition, along with our ongoing expansion projects at Belgaum, Kadapa and Pune, our cement capacity will reach about 67 million tons by quarter 3 of financial year '28.

items.statement: Revised FY27 credit cost guidance to 0.9%-1% of average total assets, down from prior guidance
items.quote: Accordingly, we are revising our FY '27 credit-cost guidance to 0.9% to 1% of average total assets.

items.statement: Raised FY27 ROA guidance to 1.8%-2% from previous guidance
items.quote: we are confident in raising our FY '27 ROA guidance to 1.8% to 2%.

items.statement: FY27 opex to average assets guidance revised to ~6.4% from earlier plan
items.quote: full year opex to be lower than earlier planned and now would be around 6.4% of average assets.

items.statement: Planned capacity building spend of INR250 cr for FY27 on branches, branding, tech and analytics
items.quote: We already had informed you that we are planning to spend around INR250 crores.

items.statement: Plan to activate gold loans in 250 branches during FY27, targeting presence in nearly all branches
items.quote: This year also, we'll be activating gold loan in about 250 branches. And we are witnessing that branches where we start operations, within 1 year, the productivity of our loan officers reaches a level of INR25 lakhs to INR30 lakhs

items.statement: Cost of funds at 6.86% in Q1 FY27, expected to remain stable with marginal increase
items.quote: Cost of funds continued the downward trajectory and stood at 6.86% for the quarter.

items.statement: NIM stable at 8.5% in Q1 FY27, expected to hold at guided levels for FY27
items.quote: Net interest margin remained stable at 8.5%.

items.statement: Microfinance demand increasing across almost all states except Kerala; branch expansion focused on UP, Rajasthan, Bihar
items.quote: we are witnessing increase in demand in almost all states. Kerala is one state where we strategically don't want to grow that much. But apart from that, from all the states, we are seeing good demand

items.statement: Secured loan book at 50.4% as of June 2026, targeting 56% by March 2027
items.quote: Ashlesh, we maintain the same guidance of 56%. 56% of secured by exit March '27.

items.statement: Micro mortgage disbursement capacity to reach INR140-150 cr/month by March 2027 from INR100 cr currently
items.quote: on the micro mortgage side, you will see INR100 crores a month kind of a disbursement number, which exit March will probably reach in the range of INR140 crores, INR150 crores.

items.statement: MFI bucket X collection efficiency at 99.68% in Q1 FY27; slippages annualized at 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4
items.quote: On an annualized basis, the slippages is about 1.72%, which was 2.68% in Q4, again, on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Micro mortgage PAR at ~1.5% and GNPA at ~0.55%; bucket X collection efficiency 99.7%-99.75% for 24 months
items.quote: Currently, we see about 95% on-time repayment and about 99.7% to 99.75% bucket X collection efficiency month-on-month consistently for the last 24 months

items.statement: Opened 38 branches in Q1 FY27, total 814 branches; plan 144 new branches for full FY27
items.quote: As part of plan for FY '27, bank has operationalized 38 new branches, taking total count to 814 as of June '26.

items.statement: Employee cost guidance for FY27: Rs 95 crore per quarter standalone, Rs 130 crore per quarter consolidated
items.quote: So, the guidance on the employee cost that we gave earlier was Rs 95 crores for the standalone entity and close to around Rs 130 crores per quarter for a consolidated entity. That is the run rate that we are looking at.

items.statement: Other expenses guidance for FY27: 8-10% increase over FY26 base
items.quote: Some things may work out on the AI side. That's why the in the April month we gave a target that 8% to 10% increase on the FY25-26 number will be the target run rate number for this particular financial year.

items.statement: TER changes fully passed to intermediaries; no margin dilution
items.quote: Mohit, as you can see from our yield number, there are no dilution as far as the margins are concerned. So basically, whatever the impact of the TER changes has been there, we have passed on the impact to all our intermediaries, and there's no impact on our margin number as such.

items.statement: SIP registrations for age 18-25 grew 18.6% QoQ to 98,127 in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So, if you look at some of the data that we have, we can clearly see in our data that in the first quarter of FY27, we saw about 18.6% increase on a quarter-on-quarter basis on the SIP registrations which happened between the age group of 18 to 25. They have now jumped up to, in this first quarter itself, to 98,127.

items.statement: Equity assets at 70% of mutual fund AUM vs industry 62%; passive pipeline expanding with Nifty 500 ETF, BSE Sector Leaders ETF approved
items.quote: We remain particularly encouraged by the improving quality of our asset mix, with equity assets across both active and passive strategies accounting for 70% of our average mutual fund AUM, compared to the industry's equity-to-non-equity mix of 62:38 ratio.

items.statement: SDOF IV secured ~Rs 900 crore commitments as of June 30, 2026; MOF II launched; alternatives AUM Rs 3,843 crore
items.quote: We also launched our second multi-opportunities fund, MOF II, and continue to see strong investor interest in Structured Debt Opportunities Fund 4, which is the fund we launched earlier this year. This has secured commitments of approximately Rs 900 crores as of 30th June 2026.

items.statement: International business flows negative for ~2 years due to weak India sentiment and fund underperformance; viewed as cyclical
items.quote: What you are seeing in terms of the flows over the last, I would say, actually, almost 2 years, combination of both the lack of appetite for India, I should actually say negative sentiment towards India and the fact that our own scheme has struggled in terms of performance over the last two years.

items.statement: No buyback proposal currently; maintaining cash for potential bolt-on M&A in alternatives or international
items.quote: No, there's no proposal that we are considering at this point of time. It's not on the table.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio ~95% of profit; expected to continue
items.quote: I think we have been maintaining a very healthy pay-out ratio of the profit in excess of 95%. I think hopefully that will continue.

items.statement: Flexi cap facing redemption pressure but SIP inflows encouraging; large & mid-cap seeing strong net inflows
items.quote: There have been some redemption pressure under our flexi cap category, but large and mid-cap, we have been receiving quite a positive inflow, and in fact, in flexi cap fund as well, the SIP inflows have been encouraging.

items.statement: SIF and GIFT City outbound funds in pipeline for H2 FY27; balanced hybrid and sectoral debt funds planned
items.quote: Apart from that, SIF and GIFT City outbound funds are also in the pipeline in the H2 of this particular financial year.

items.statement: Sales team restructuring complete: supervisory-to-feet ratio at 4-4.5x; Gen Z now 39% of workforce, Gen Z+Y 80% of sales team
items.quote: We sort of clustered some of the branches. So effectively, that allowed us to address that. So, I say we're pretty much there in terms of that 4, 4.5 number.

items.statement: Investment performance not where management wants it; working on process readjustments and talent
items.quote: Investment performance is where, we are not where we would like to be, in my opening remarks I made the call investment excellence, and we've not managed to execute well on that.

items.statement: Guided 25% revenue growth for FY27 with stable margins similar to FY26
items.quote: I remain confident of delivering 25% revenue growth for the full year with stable margins.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin for FY27 to be similar to full year FY26 levels
items.quote: For current financial year, for the full year, as we guided during the commentary also, we are expecting a similar kind of margin as we had for full year FY '26.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR50 cr for electrolyte additives pilot plant and INR40-45 cr maintenance; R&D center and land acquisition capex to be announced later
items.quote: For FY '27, capex is largely the spillover capex of electrolyte additives as well as the pilot plant capex, which is around INR50 crores and around INR40 to INR45 crores of maintenance capex, that is what the already planned capex for this year.

items.statement: Indichem plant capex expected to complete by end of Q2 FY27; revenue from FY28 onwards
items.quote: this is getting constructed even before the schedules and expected to get -- capex is expected to get completed by end of this quarter. And maybe from next financial year onwards, we will have the revenue coming up from that plant.

items.statement: Electrolyte additives Phase 2 (third product) capex completion by end of Q2 FY27; trial runs soon
items.quote: Phase 2, which is for the third product of our Electrolyte Additives segment, which is going on schedule. And as we mentioned earlier also by end of Q2 FY '27, we would be completing our capex.

items.statement: Battery chemicals: commercial supply started; multiple customers in North America and Korea; 4,000 MT capacity (2,000 MT VC + 2,000 MT FEC); expect full utilization in 3 years
items.quote: we have a capacity of 2,000 metric tons for VC and 2,000 metric tons for FEC. So it's a total 4,000 metric ton capacity and for which we are more than confident that we will be able to hit the full capacity utilization by end of 3 years.

items.statement: Battery chemicals demand unprecedented, driven by tight global supply; expect rapid ramp-up over coming quarters
items.quote: Demand here is unprecedented, driven by tight global supply and we, therefore, expect a rapid ramp-up over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Gulf persist; team secured raw material availability and supply continuity
items.quote: We began the financial year on a turbulent note, driven by geopolitical tensions in the Gulf. While these tensions persist, our team has done a commendable work in securing raw material availability and ensuring supply continuity.

items.statement: Employee cost guided at ~INR150 cr for FY27 including annual increments and one-time performance bonus
items.quote: We should typically look at around INR150 crores of employee cost for the current year.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to remain at current levels (~16%) for most of FY27, with gross margin spreads around INR 28,145/KL sustained for next 1-2 quarters.
items.quote: We are hopeful of the margins remaining at this level or around this level. The current quarter looks good. And we are hopeful of it carrying forward at these levels for the whole year.

items.statement: Volume growth target for FY27 is 8-11% YoY, consistent with historical range.
items.quote: Historically, we've always been doing volume growth in the range of 8% to 10% to even 11%. So, we see ourselves getting that much of volume growth during this year also.

items.statement: Export revenue contribution expected to remain at current elevated levels (~51% of revenue) for coming quarters.
items.quote: We anticipate the export revenue and the export sales will be in the same level for the quarters to come.

items.statement: Price increases implemented across all segments (PHPO, PIO, lubricants) except automotive lubricants where hikes were delayed; higher realizations driven by supply chain disruptions and agile sourcing.
items.quote: The price increase has been across the segment, except a bit for the lubric -- automotive lubricant category, where it is more of a dealer distributor network. The price increase has been taken even in that category but obviously got with a little delayed manner.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions (Middle East, Strait of Hormuz) causing supply chain disruptions, elevated freight/insurance costs, and raw material availability issues; managed via agile sourcing and inventory management.
items.quote: The operating environment remained challenging, shaped by heightened geopolitical tension in the Middle East, concerns surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, volatility in the crude oil and the base oil pricing and intermittent disruptions across the global supply chains.

items.statement: Texol subsidiary (Sharjah) temporarily impacted by regional supply constraints but maintained business continuity; logistics normalizing, throughput improving.
items.quote: During this period -- during the period of quarter 1, operations were temporarily impacted by regional supply constraints and disruption in vessel movements arising from the geopolitical situation. However, leveraging our regional sourcing capabilities and operational agility, we ensured uninterrupted supply to custome

items.statement: South Africa entry strategy under development; clarity expected in 1-2 quarters. New customer qualifications ongoing under NDA; pipeline includes domestic and international prospects.
items.quote: The strategy for the South African arm is being worked out. There will be much more clarity being emerging in the next 1 or 2-odd quarters.

items.statement: Trade payables increased to INR 430 cr but 90% within 90 days; INR 600 cr not yet due. Increase driven by revenue growth, not payment delays.
items.quote: Out of that INR900-odd the trade payables, there is INR600 crores, which is not yet due. On a basic -- historical basis, even currently, 90% of it is within 90 days.

items.statement: Targeting ~10% volume growth for FY27 and FY28; value growth depends on gold prices
items.quote: Broadly, we are targeting around 10% volume growth going forward. Internally, our primary focus remains on volume growth, and we believe that achieving around 10% growth in volumes is a reasonable target.

items.statement: Two new showrooms finalized: Dahod, Gujarat (~3,200 sq ft, COCO) and Jabalpur, MP (~3,750 sq ft, FOCO); fit-out underway
items.quote: We have successfully finalized the locations for new showrooms in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, and Dahod, Gujarat. All key agreements, approvals, and necessary formalities have been completed. Fit-out and showroom development activities are underway at both locations, and the stores will be operational soon.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 11.01% (+80 bps YoY); PAT margin 7.55% (+82 bps YoY) driven by scale, operating leverage, cost discipline, favourable mix
items.quote: At operating level, EBITDA increased by 70% year-on-year to INR93.99 crores in Q1 '27 as compared to INR55 crores in Q1 '26. EBITDA margin expanded by 80 basis points year-on-year to 11.01% as compared to 10.21% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Gold inventory carried at ~INR1,20,000 vs market ~INR1,51,000-1,52,000 (~20% gap); new procurement at INR1,45,000-1,50,000; profitability driven by making charges, not gold price
items.quote: As of today, if we look at the prevailing gold price, it is trading at around INR1,51,000 - INR1,52,000 whereas the inventory value reflected in our books is approximately INR1,20,000. This creates a sizeable gap of nearly 20% between the carrying value of inventory and the current market price.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volume growth ~1-2% YoY; revenue growth 58% driven by gold prices; demand recovering after price correction to INR1,45,000-1,50,000 range
items.quote: When we compare Q1 FY27 with Q1 FY26, we have delivered volume growth of approximately 1% to 2%. The balance growth has largely been driven by higher gold prices.

items.statement: Gold 80% of jewellery inventory (22K), 18K ~15%, 14K/other balance; studded (diamond) 6-7% of sales, target 12-15% by Mar'28; silver revenue +150% YoY to INR40 cr
items.quote: As of now our business is doing like between 6% to 7% of the studded mix. And we have targeted by March '28, we would like to increase up to 12% to 15% on an overall basis.

items.statement: Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15% in May 2026 creates near-term cost and demand sensitivity; long-term fundamentals intact
items.quote: While the recent government announcement and increase in gold import duty from 6% to 15% in May 2026 has introduced near-term cost and demand sensitivity, the long-term fundamentals of the sector remain intact.

items.statement: Inventory turnover 4.7-5.0x annually; 95-98% assets in inventory; operating cash flow negative due to working capital nature, expected to improve with scale
items.quote: Our business currently operates with an inventory turnover ratio of around 4.7x to 5.0x annually, which, in our view, is among the best in the industry.

items.statement: Hedging: real-time replenishment (3-4x daily), old gold exchange (natural hedge), Gold Metal Loans (100% for incremental inventory), MCX positions per research
items.quote: The company continues to leverage exchange led procurement of gold, gold metal loan, and hedging mechanisms on the commodity exchange platform to mitigate gold price volatility, support margin stability, and improve working capital efficiency.

items.statement: Targeting 20% volume growth for remainder of FY27 with EBITDA also growing at least 20%
items.quote: So, looking ahead, we are still working towards achieving a growth of 20% for the rest of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg back to INR 7-8 range from mid-May, supporting full-year margin recovery
items.quote: From almost May 15th, we are already back to INR 7-INR 8 per kg margin.

items.statement: Annual capex capped at INR 200-250 crore to support 20-25% volume growth
items.quote: We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year. So, this year also will be INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore in total.

items.statement: Q1 blended EBITDA margin hit INR 2/kg due to absorbing gas cost spike on committed orders; new orders at INR 7-8/kg
items.quote: We took a hit from INR 7 a kg blended and we came down to INR 2 a kg, wherein we absorbed all that cost.

items.statement: Cost-plus model with 30-40 day order book hedge; sudden gas cost spike absorbed on committed orders, new orders repriced immediately
items.quote: We operate at a cost-plus model wherein any increase and decrease that we take in our raw material or even consumable is passed on to the customer.

items.statement: B2C contributed ~10% of sales in Q1; target 25% of total sales from B2C (50% of low-carbon volume) with 20-30% higher EBITDA/kg vs B2B
items.quote: Customer response has been encouraging with these products contributing approximately 10% of our sales already during the last quarter.

items.statement: IHT/OHT combined capacity 9,000t (rising to 15,000t with OHT commissioning); targeting 50% IHT utilization next month, 60-80% by year-end; EBITDA INR 10-20/kg at optimum utilization
items.quote: IHT and OHT combined, right now we have 9,000 tonnes of capacity, which will reach to 15,000 tonnes with OHT commissioning.

items.statement: Gas costs remain elevated (1.5x average increase) but fully passed through in new orders; no inventory loss risk due to 70-80% order hedge
items.quote: Even today, our gas prices are escalated. We do not see any decrease in our gas prices today. All of that is still there. Our costs are still escalated but the only change is that all of that has been passed on.

items.statement: Operating capacity 680,000 tonnes; running at ~85-90% utilization sweet spot; 60,000t additional capacity available on demand; backward integrated equipment manufacturing enables 6-month capex lead time
items.quote: Our operating capacity as of today stands at around 680,000 tonnes, and we are pleased to say that we are back to the normal level of operations with steady and comfortable margins.

items.statement: Minimum wage revisions in Karnataka and Telangana estimated to impact FY27 adjusted EBITDA by ~120 bps; full quarterly impact from Q2
items.quote: Based on the current notification, we estimate an impact of approximately 120 basis points for FY 2027 on adjusted EBITDA.

items.statement: Q1 free cash flow INR 2,416 million after fixed asset additions of INR 745 million
items.quote: We generated INR 3,161 million of operating cash flow during the quarter, and our free cash flow was INR 2,416 million after fixed asset additions of INR 745 million.

items.statement: Signed $35.3 million steady-state ACV in Q1 across 18 existing clients and 1 new logo
items.quote: our commercial momentum remained healthy with $35.3 million of steady state ACV signed during the quarter across 18 existing clients and 1 new logo.

items.statement: Demand favors partners with deep healthcare domain expertise, operational scale, technology, analytics, AI and measurable outcomes; traction in managed service deals and Sagility Synchrony platform
items.quote: demand continues to favour partners that combine deep healthcare domain expertise with operational scale, technology, analytics, AI and a demonstrated ability to deliver measurable outcomes.

items.statement: Minimum wage hikes in Karnataka (effective May 23) and Telangana impact ~65-70% of headcount; cascading pay parity effects; mitigation via geographic expansion and operational efficiency over 12-18 months
items.quote: The increase in minimum wages in Karnataka was pretty significant, and so absorbing this reflects the strength and flexibility of our operating model.

items.statement: CareSeed acquisition closed June 2026: $5.1M CY25 revenue, 95% recurring, 31.4% EBITDA margin, 30 clients (26 new), adds HEDIS quality capabilities and Forecast/Harvest platforms
items.quote: CareSeed delivers on HEDIS reporting and has two platforms, Forecast which provides HEDIS reporting and quality analytics, and Harvest which delivers cloud -based medical record review and chart abstraction. So you see the numbers, $5.1 million was CY 2025 revenue with a 95% recurring revenue and a 31.4% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Seasonal open enrolment revenue proportion ~6% of total (similar to FY26); Q4 FY26 had $24.8M seasonal revenue; visibility on FY27 seasonal volumes by September, update in Q2 call
items.quote: the proportion of seasonal revenue to total revenue, we believe will continue in the same way that we had last year, right? With the addition of BroadPath, you're right, our seasonal percentages have gone up. And those percentages will most likely hold for FY 2027 as well.

items.statement: On track to fully repay outstanding debt during FY27; net debt INR 1,110M, net debt/EBITDA 0.06x; cash INR 9,674M
items.quote: We remain on track to fully repay our outstanding debt during FY 2027. This will further strengthen our balance sheet and reduce finance costs.

items.statement: AI-led deflation historically 100-150 bps, could increase to 200 bps; driven by onshore-to-offshore migration, automation, and AI; not tracked quarterly
items.quote: all of this put together is what I historically said, even before we had 100 to 150 bps and that could increase to 200 bps over the near future and maybe even go higher in the future.

items.statement: Expect inflation impact to taper down in subsequent quarters of FY27
items.quote: With elevated inflation weighing on demand environment in quarter 1, we expect the impact to taper down in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: No further price increases planned at current inflation levels
items.quote: At this moment, we do not feel the need to take any further price increases beyond what we have already done.

items.statement: Plan to accelerate small format store openings, see opportunity for ~3,000 small stores
items.quote: We can see an opportunity of almost 3,000 small format stores in the country. And as we progress forward, you will see increased momentum on the small format.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 28.7% from 28.4% YoY due to lower promotional spend
items.quote: On the gross margin, the improvement that you've seen this quarter from 28.4% to 28.7% is largely because of the fact that our promotional expenditure has been lower than the previous year.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved to 10.4% from 10.3% YoY
items.quote: Operating EBITDA was INR 387 crores, which was a growth of 19.3% over last year, and our operating margin (Operating EBITDA margin) improved from 10.3% last year to 10.4% this year.

items.statement: Private brands to maintain or widen price discount vs market leaders in FMCG
items.quote: Our firm view is that our price discount to the market leaders has to be almost in every case, actually slightly higher than earlier or at the very least, the same.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth of 10% driven by 8% new customer acquisition and 3% existing customer volume growth
items.quote: Our total number of customer acquisitions in the quarter has gone up by 8%. So we have served 8% new customers in our store. And our existing customers have bought 3% more approximately in this quarter, and that's how we have achieved approximately 10% same-store sales growth.

items.statement: Private brands contribute 75.2% of revenue; 100% in apparel, 75% in GM, 60% in FMCG by volume
items.quote: Our private brands continue to see strong customer traction, contributing 75.2% to revenue growth or rather our revenue in quarter 1 FY27.

items.statement: RFID rollout across network to take slightly over 1 year; currently rolling out in Delhi NCR
items.quote: But I think the entire rollout will slightly exceed 1-year time frame.

items.statement: Employee cost per sq ft up 13% YoY due to minimum wage hikes across multiple states; structural change
items.quote: This quarter, we have seen a significant increase in minimum wages across multiple states like Haryana, UP, Telangana, Karnataka and so on and so forth. Obviously, the base has gone up, but we will continue to look for opportunities and try and optimize as much as possible. But obviously, this is a structural change.

items.statement: Closing inventory at INR 1,900 crores as of Q1 FY27 end
items.quote: So our closing inventory for quarter 1 is INR 1,900 crores.

items.statement: Guides 20% CAGR store/distribution growth over next four years
items.quote: So, I think we've guided to about 20% CAGR over the next four years in terms of distribution growth.

items.statement: Expects marketing spend as % of revenue to decline from 6.6% to 4.5-4.6% over next five years
items.quote: So, we believe that over the next five years, this 6.6% will go down to around 4.5%, 4.6% odd percent.

items.statement: Contribution margin stable; operating leverage to drive EBITDA margin from 7.5% to ~15% over next four years
items.quote: So, there is massive headroom to expand the operating EBITDA margin from 7.5% to the 15% handle.

items.statement: Demand softened in May after customs duty hike but normalized in June and continued into July
items.quote: Essentially, last quarter had been kind of mixed. Akshaya Tritiya period was great, then there was import duty hike which softened the demand, and then I think as June progressed, a lot of that demand kind of kept on coming back. And we continue to see that the same trend continuing into July also.

items.statement: Stable gold prices are most conducive for consumer demand and business targets
items.quote: I wish gold prices remain stable and then we continue to operate the way we operated for last six years. And I think we feel lot more comfortable in that environment. We believe that is the most conducive environment for us to be able to deliver the targets that we have set off for ourselves.

items.statement: Experimented with 14 karat in lower price points; redesigning entry products using less gold
items.quote: We have seen, we have done some experimentation with 14 karatage. So, what we have generally seen is in lower price point, it helps plug that gap that got created. However, just lowering the karatage is not the only strategy we have. We have done a lot of redesigning also in entry price points.

items.statement: Hedging policy unchanged at 50% of gold inventory; not designed to predict gold prices
items.quote: So, we are consistent with our policy, there is no change.

items.statement: New stores larger (~4,500 sq ft) in Tier-2/3 for frontage and capacity; unit economics stable
items.quote: Now, all of this is not operational square feet. So, this is basically the incremental capacity that we are building for the kind of store productivity we are able to see in our older cohorts. Second, from a rental perspective on the absolute level, when we look at it on an absolute cost per store, rent per store, reve

items.statement: 95% of products manufactured in-house; 300-400 bps margin delta vs peers but strategic for design control
items.quote: Broadly all of it is in-house, about 95% of the products that we sell is manufactured in-house.

items.statement: Long-term NMV growth guidance of 25% CAGR over next five years, higher in initial years and lower later
items.quote: So, I think we have a long -term growth guidance that we have kind of mentioned of the next five years of 25% CAGR, which is kind of obviously higher in the initial years and maybe lower in kind of the later years.

items.statement: Contribution margin to improve from restoring logistics pricing and growing ad revenue; logistics efficiency gains passed to customers
items.quote: Initially or during the course of last year, some of our margin in relation to what we charge for our logistics services versus our cost had sort of come down, which we are now in the process of restoring. And beyond a certain kind of stage, we would largely kind of keep it constant and pass on any efficiencies that we

items.statement: Logistics cost per delivered order fell ~INR1 QoQ in Q1 FY27 despite fuel and wage hikes; expect continued efficiency gains
items.quote: you would be able to see that our cost per delivered order actually came down even during this quar ter by about a rupee versus kind of the previous quarter.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA budget cap for new initiatives (Horizon 2) is ~INR200 crore
items.quote: roughly about INR200 crores is kind of the annual budget cap that we have around new initiatives in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: Valmo handles ~50% of logistics volumes, stable QoQ; no specific share target, allocation based on lowest cost per lane
items.quote: In terms of quantification, I think again last quarter was about 50%, similar to kind of the previous quarter before that.

items.statement: Annual order frequency grew 9% YoY with 29% ADU growth; both older and newer cohorts showing positive frequency trends
items.quote: if you look at overall the annual frequency with a 29% ADU growth still continued to go up by about 9% year -on-year.

items.statement: Meesho Mall growing much faster than overall platform; substantial part of business and expected to be large growth driver for 3-5+ years
items.quote: Overall, if you see, Meesho Mall continues to grow at much faster pace as compared to the overall platform. It's substantial part of our business, so it's not insignificant, and we anticipate that this should be a large part of our growth story over the next three, five, maybe even longer years.

items.statement: Kirana Club acquisition at early product-market fit; P&L contribution long-term; strategic fit with low-cost logistics and B2B expansion
items.quote: contribution to P&L will happen over the long term. The business is really, really small. I think I would say like early product-market fit. So, we have to do a lot before it starts to contribute to the P&L of the company.

items.statement: Low-cost local logistics network for perishables/grocery (sub-INR20-30 items) in experimentation stage; pre-product-market fit, separate from national Valmo network
items.quote: We are still in the experimentation stage, but we believe it's again quite important for the long run. If we make that supply chain work, we should be able to extend our value proposition to ma ny more price points and categories in the long run.

items.statement: ~2/3 of GMV-contributing sellers advertise on platform; ad adoption increasing QoQ; ROAS stable
items.quote: I think close to about two -thirds of our GMV contributing sellers do ads. I think there is scope for increasing this even further.

items.statement: For >50% of GMV-contributing sellers, Meesho is a primary source of income
items.quote: So more than for more than 50% of our sellers, let's say, we would be a primary source of income.

items.statement: GST/GTA restructuring for Valmo (VTPL) follows industry precedent; legal/accounting opinions obtained; no regulatory queries received
items.quote: We had of course taken reasonable number of opinions, legal as well as accounting opinions from leading law firms as well as accounting firms. Just to clarify, there has been no question asked by any regulatory authority or tax authority to us on this matter.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 growth impacted by Diwali shifting to November (sale moves to Q3); Q2+Q3 combined trajectory unchanged
items.quote: This year Diwali being pushed forward into November, our annual sale will kind of start during the month of October. And that is a significant GMV generating event for us and hence you would see some variations in terms of growth rate Y-o-Y in Q2 versus kind of the trajectory that we are on. But on a Q2 and Q3 combined

items.statement: Management does not provide MRR guidance; advises looking at past quarterly exit MRR trends instead
items.quote: See, we don't provide guidance on MRR. We always, advise everyone to look at what we have done in the past rather than, predict the future.

items.statement: Expecting next lot of 1,024 B200 GPUs in next couple of months; plans to expand into non-flagship Blackwell and Vera Rubin architectures
items.quote: We obviously plan to deploy the B200 as soon as a new lot becomes available to us. And we are expecting that to happen soon over the next couple of months. And apart from that, we obviously plan to build more capacity in terms of more Blackwell including non-flagship Blackwell as well. And also, we have plans to expand

items.statement: B200 cluster at maximal utilization; customers increasingly seeking 1-3 year contracts for capacity lock-in
items.quote: Yes, it's quite a maximal utilization of capacity that we have.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 75.2% (+1,450 bps QoQ); management believes current margin level is sustainable over medium to long term
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR1,179 million with margins expanding up to 75.2%. EBITDA margin expanded by 1,450 basis points compared to Q4 2026.

items.statement: Price hikes announced in July for both GPU and CPU; CPU price increase driven by higher memory costs; customers offered option to lock current prices via longer-term contracts
items.quote: So, to accommodate that, we had to, in fact, increase the price of both the GPUs and CPUs. And it's not just about the higher demand scenario that's associated with the price increase. So it was also that some of these inputs cost actually increased for us.

items.statement: Strong demand across training and inference workloads running in parallel on same infrastructure; international revenue ~37%, India AI mission ~20-21%, rest domestic
items.quote: With regards to capacity building, we have already said that we intend to be more judicious as well as aggressive. Now from a revenue composition in the previous quarter, I think India AI revenue was about 20%, 21%. And international was closer to 37% or so. And rest is like all domestic revenue.

items.statement: Sovereign AI platform gaining traction with open-source models approaching frontier capabilities; TIR and Jarvis Labs software layers enabling agentic workflows
items.quote: Now with open source coming very, very close to how the frontier models are working, we are very close to achieving AI Sovereignty for our customers, where all four components interoperate with each other using the software that we provide to our customers.

items.statement: Management views AI as still in 'day zero' of a decadal adoption cycle; not concerned about AI bubble or commoditization risks from specific news events
items.quote: We believe that some of those things which are equally important are completely lower. So it is still day zero of AI. We are still in the midst of largest build-outs in the history of IT itself where the whole world is building the AI super cycle.

items.statement: Current debt ~INR 450 crores for first B200 lot; will increase with next GPU deliveries; no quantification of peak debt; future equity raises will be communicated if/when they happen
items.quote: So, the loan, which stands as of now is broadly INR 450 crores, which with the other lot coming in picture, it would be increasing across in the near term.

items.statement: Live GPU capacity at 5,100 (excludes 1,024 B200s coming soon); 1,024 Blackwell GPUs went live in Q1 and were put on revenue
items.quote: Nearly 5,100 is the current capacity, which is live on our platform today. That's the number of GPUs which are live today. So that does not include another 1,024 B200 we are expecting soon.

items.statement: Expect revenue and earnings growth driven by consumer preference and new destinations
items.quote: We expect a year of revenue and earnings growth driven by consumer preference for our cruise brand and expanding our new destinations.

items.statement: Average ticket price increased 4.3% YoY in Q1
items.quote: we report a load factor of 105% for Q1 with an increase of 4.3% of average ticket price versus Q1 2025.

items.statement: Q1 net profit Rs.22.77 Cr, net margin ~12%; EBITDA hit by Rs.14 Cr higher fuel cost
items.quote: With the higher fuel costs, we report a net profit of Rs.22.77 Crores on a consolidated basis and a net profit margin of around 12% for the quarter ended June 2026.

items.statement: Fuel cost impact ~Rs.14 Cr in Q1; VLSFO price spiked to $1,228/tonne, now ~$800/tonne; recovery via surcharges from Q2/Q3
items.quote: the major increase is in the fuel, which is around Rs.14 odd Crores, so if it would have not been there your EBITDA would have gone up by Rs.14 odd Crores that is a major impact.

items.statement: Cordelia Sky handover Sep 25, 2026; maiden voyage Oct 23, 2026; Cordelia Sun to follow
items.quote: The handover of the vessel will be on September 25, 2026. Thereafter, the rebranding will be happening and implementing our entertainment programs, our guest offerings for India. The ship name will change to Cordelia Sky and will be arriving in Mumbai on October 15, 2026 and our first maiden voyage will be October 23,

items.statement: Advance bookings for new ships Rs.65 Cr, implying Rs.110-115 Cr revenue for shorter sailings
items.quote: Right now, I can share with you Rs.65 Crores in advance booking, which is resulting to approximately Rs.110 Crores to Rs.115 Crores revenue for the shorter sailings.

items.statement: New ships offer 245 suites vs 69 on Empress; 9 restaurants vs 3; ~100% revenue potential increase per ship
