items.statement: Retail revenue up 85% YoY; 76% stores profitable vs 61% last year; network expanded to 1,200+ outlets with 22 new stores
items.quote: Revenue of retail business increased by 85% year-on-year, reflecting improved scale, operating leverage and profitability across the network. 76% of the stores were profitable during the quarter compared to 61% in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Nano DAP sales volume grew 2% with ~60% market share; exports initiated; growth moderated by bans in UP and Maharashtra
items.quote: The Nano business delivered stable performance with sales volume growing 2% year-on-year, supported by sustained demand for Nano DAP and a market leadership position with nearly 60% of market share.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth to track market growth of 4-5% and does not expect 23% revenue growth to continue every quarter
items.quote: I think bottom line, if I can grow same as the market, that would be a happy place for me.

items.statement: Markets remain robust and growing at 4-5% range; festival season expected to support near-term demand
items.quote: The markets that we operate in remain robust, and there are challenges still remaining with the political crisis, et cetera, and the raw material, but we are quite confident that the market will be growing in near future, especially with the festival season coming in the next few months.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through varies by contract (monthly/quarterly indexing); most Q2 impact passed on; transparent inventory sharing with customers
items.quote: In terms of passing of RM costs, again, it depends on our contract. Sometimes with our customers, we have quarterly price change -- index change contract. In some cases, we are able to change that pretty frequently.

items.statement: Growth driven 1/3 each by price, volume, mix; home care and liquid categories growing faster; blueloop adoption below 30% but asset utilization >70%
items.quote: The growth was driven by price, volume and product mix, almost 1/3 each of that. And roughly, when you're talking about 23% growth overall in net sales, it's pretty robust.

items.statement: Investing in modernization and productivity improvements to support organic growth; solar captive plant at Khopoli coming online in Q3 supplying ~50% power
items.quote: We are channeling some of that money into modernization and capex expenditure, et cetera, that we do internally for organic growth.

items.statement: Middle East crisis causing supply chain disruption and raw material volatility; inventory built up consciously to avoid stock-outs; geopolitical situation makes procurement hard but manageable
items.quote: We actually kind of covered ourselves a bit higher versus the previous periods because of the fact that we were seeing a lot of volatility in the markets from a commodity standpoint and the Middle East Asia situation.

items.statement: Export and domestic growth balanced at ~23% each; exports 30% of sales volume to SE Asia, Africa, Europe, Americas; duty stability improving
items.quote: Actually, 30% of our sales volume comes from exports. So we are already supplying to Southeast Asia, Africa, Europe as well as Americas.

items.statement: Volume growth high single-digit (~9%); no specific revenue run-rate guidance; land monetization not disclosed; no inorganic acquisition plans currently
items.quote: I can't give you exact volume number. But I can tell you it's a high single digit. So if I compare last year with this year, Hitesh, so just short of, let's say, double digit.

items.statement: Conductor division pending order book at INR10,190 crores with 56.8% export proportion; new orders received INR5,245 crores in Q1 FY27, 65.8% exports
items.quote: The pending order book stands at around INR10,190 crores with an export proportion of 56.8%. New orders received by the conductor division were INR5,245 crores in the quarter, of which exports contributed to 65.8%.

items.statement: Cable division pending order book at INR1,925 crores, up from INR1,653 crores a year ago
items.quote: The pending order today stands at INR1,925 crores. So it largely covers the plan or the requirement for the current -- for the coming quarter compared to INR1,653 crores from a year ago.

items.statement: Conductor EBITDA per ton INR53,418 vs INR43,688 YoY; Oil EBITDA per kL INR25,482 vs INR7,004 YoY; Cable EBITDA margin 10.6% up 60 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA growth is attributable to a higher share of the premium mix due to which despite a slightly lower volume of conventional conductors, the absolute EBITDA has grown, which came in at INR53,418 per ton compared to INR43,688 per ton a year earlier.

items.statement: Oil division volumes down 13.7% YoY (UAE facility restricted by Hamriyah port closure); India volumes down only 4.4%; auto oil +6.6%, industrial lubricants +12.1%
items.quote: Volume for the quarter stands at 129,085 kL, down 13.7% compared to a year ago and down -- yes, the volumes were affected really because of our facility in the UAE, which because of this crisis and the resulting closure of the Hamriyah port was restricted to only making local deliveries.

items.statement: Oil division provision of INR94 crores taken due to sharp crude/gas oil price rise then fall; inventory reduced to limit reversal impact
items.quote: the company has followed the requirements of accounting standards and has provided for approximately INR94 crores for the oil division in the quarter.

items.statement: MJP premiums on aluminum cannot be hedged; APAR locks in premiums via supplier contracts; premiums have risen quarter-to-quarter
items.quote: Yes, we are, and there is no way to hedge it. The only thing is we do make contracts with suppliers. So we kind of effectively hedge ourselves to the extent we lock in the premium with the suppliers through a mutually agreed contract.

items.statement: U.S. conductor market 70% reserved for domestic production; APAR competes in 30% import quota; Section 232 tariffs 50% on aluminum conductors
items.quote: All bare products are covered under 232 with a 50% duty. So aluminum is 50%, rods are at 50% and conductors are also at 50%.

items.statement: Cable division approved for data center supplies to Meta, Microsoft, Google in U.S.; now participating in copper cable RFQs (LV/MV, PVC/XLPE/rubber)
items.quote: Today, APAR is approved in the U.S. for cables being supplied to data centers of Meta, Microsoft and Google by various major electrical contractors.

items.statement: Wires portfolio: B2C retail sales +46% YoY; active towns +17%, distributors +25%, retail accounts +51%; B2B channel sales +92% YoY
items.quote: Specifically, if you take, in this quarter, sales for wires grew 46%, and our focus has been on increasing distributor and retailer presence.

items.statement: Company issued notice for shareholder approval for securities issuance; restricted from discussing guidance, projections, or funding requirements
items.quote: the company has issued a notice to its shareholders seeking the approval under applicable law for the issuance of securities. So under these guidelines, to comply with them, we have specifically restrictions around publicity.

items.statement: FY27 sales volume guidance maintained at 10.5-11 million tons despite Q1 shutdown
items.quote: Yes, yes, you're right. We will maintain the run rate, rather we will increase the run rate because we had taken a shutdown in the quarter 1.

items.statement: FY27 capex plan of ~INR 8,500 crores; INR 2,000 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: Against our FY27 capex plan of approximately INR 8,500 crores. We invested roughly INR 2,000 crores during Q1.

items.statement: Long-term capex framework of INR 7,000-10,000 crores per year focused on value-added products only
items.quote: We want to grow not at the rate of tons, but at the spending rate of about INR 7,000 crores to INR 8,000 crores or maybe INR 10,000 crores per year.

items.statement: Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 crores; EBITDA/ton INR 11,937 (+INR 1,843 QoQ)
items.quote: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA per ton increased by INR 1,843 per ton, taking it to INR 11,937 per ton.

items.statement: Target to reduce net debt/EBITDA below 1.5x by Q2FY27 from 1.71x currently
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving the ratio below our stated threshold of 1.5x during Q2FY27.

items.statement: Coking coal consumption cost rose $23/ton QoQ in Q1; guidance of $20-25/ton increase for the quarter
items.quote: This improvement was driven by increase in ASP, partly offset by a $23 per ton increase in coking coal consumption cost, which is in line with our guidance of $20 to $25 per ton of coal.

items.statement: Expect further coking coal cost increase of $12-15/ton in Q2, but blending optimization to mitigate impact
items.quote: Today we are seeing that maybe $15 will be the total increase, about INR 1,500 in coking coal. But it also depends upon the Chinese factor.

items.statement: Slurry pipeline commissioning expected H1 August to save ~INR 700/ton on logistics
items.quote: One of the key cost saving will come from the slurry pipeline, which I think we have already told in the market about INR 700 per ton benefit that as Mr. Sharma has said is coming from the Q2.

items.statement: Value-added product share rose from 61% in Q4FY26 to 66% in Q1FY27; target 50% high-EBITDA products
items.quote: The share of value-added product has increased from 61% in Q4FY26 to 66% in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand seasonally weak in monsoon; expect recovery from end-August with construction boom
items.quote: We are very much confident that in times to come, say from end of August onwards when the monsoon is receding, the country will come back again with construction boom.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Russia-Ukraine, Middle East) creating global steel surplus; China capacity cuts of 50-60Mt vs demand drop of 100Mt
items.quote: Today we are seeing that in China, the capacity reduction is about 50 to 60 million tons, whereas the demand has gone down by 100 million tons.

items.statement: Internal cost reduction target of ~INR 1,000/ton through yield, energy, and consumable optimization
items.quote: I think there is a chance of, roughly figures, I am not committing something, but roughly because I have to talk to my colleagues also, at least INR 1,000 per ton reduction is possible in terms of cost.

items.statement: Captive iron ore mix at 28% currently, targeting 40% by FY27 exit via Utkal B1 ramp-up and B2 commissioning
items.quote: Last quarter we were around 16%, with this currently we are around 28% in this quarter and the full year basis we should be around 40% on an exit basis.

items.statement: Asset Management and Private Wealth share of operating PAT expected to continue rising due to growing annuity businesses and low market share providing headroom
items.quote: We have guided that the share of Asset and Private Wealth businesses will continue to rise because of growing share of annuity businesses and the low market share that we have in these businesses allowing a lot of headroom for us to grow.

items.statement: AMC AUM growth supported by ₹16,000 crore annualized SIP run rate, NFO collections, funds crossing 3-year vintage, current AUM 15% above FY26 average, potential MTM gains, and GIFT City entry
items.quote: We believe our AUM growth will be supported by the following factors: o Annualized SIP run rate of around ₹16,000 crores o Collections from proposed NFOs besides discretionary flows o More products crossing the 3-year vintage o Current AUM of nearly ₹1.9 lakh crores is over 15% higher than the FY26 average AUM of ₹1.57

items.statement: Alternate Asset Management to be key growth and ARR driver on larger fund sizes, new categories, and more funds entering carry income recognition
items.quote: Alternate Asset Management business will be a nother key growth driver and also an ARR driver of the Motilal Oswal Group on the back of o Larger fund size that we have raised in every subsequent series o Entry into newer categories o More funds entering the carry income recognition threshold, which will boost our carry

items.statement: Private Wealth ARR AUM currently ~₹52,000 crores, focus on growing ARR-led revenue mix to improve earnings quality and predictability
items.quote: Focus is now on growing ARR AUM, which is current ly at around ₹52,000 crores through various initiatives, including advisory solutions, strengthening leverage solutions as a value add for family offices and exclusive co -investment leveraging group synergies.

items.statement: Housing Finance expected to witness strong growth in next 2-3 years with strong capital adequacy and low leverage, no further capital infusion needed
items.quote: We expect housing finance business to continue to witness strong growth in the next 2 to 3 years. Business has a strong capital adequacy ratio, very low leverage, giving us enough growth levers without any need for further capital infusion.

items.statement: HFC borrowing cost expected to rationalize by 15-20 bps over next 12-18 months post CRISIL AA+ rating upgrade
items.quote: Hence, with the recent upgrade from CRISIL we further expect cost to rationalize by 15 to 20 b ps over the course of next 12 to 18 months, considering our AA+ rating improvement.

items.statement: Capital Markets FY27 YoY growth expected but QoQ volatile depending on market windows; strong signed mandate pipeline
items.quote: Hence, FY27 as a whole, we'll witness growth. However, on a QoQ basis, it really depends on market.

items.statement: Unlisted alternates carry income run rate ~₹66 crores/quarter expected for next 3 quarters and next year, with only 70% of fair value recognized conservatively
items.quote: On unlisted equities - the number is ₹66 crores accrued as variable additional return for this quarter and will continue to recur around a similar level for the next 3 quarters as well as for the next year because there's a whole pipeline of products which will keep advancing and coming closer to maturity.

items.statement: AMC to launch 4-5 new active mutual fund offers over next 12 months, more passive offerings; key growth from existing funds crossing 3-year vintage (small cap, large cap, multi-cap)
items.quote: On the active side, there would be fewer, but still over the next 12 months, there can be 4 to 5 new offers from our side. The big thing to focus on the AMC is that over the December'26 - Jan'27, we have 2 large funds, the small and the large cap funds, which will complete 3 years.

items.statement: Private Wealth RM hiring in FY27: fewer additions but higher cost, targeted at family offices; headcount increase lower than FY26
items.quote: This year, the composition of RM additions will be fewer in numbers, but much higher in cost, targeted at the family offices. Thus, the cost increase will continue to be there, but headcount increase will be lesser in FY27 compared to FY26.

items.statement: Continued calibrated investment in senior leadership and relationship managers for Private Wealth; opportunistic strengthening of fund manager and research teams for AMC
items.quote: We continue to make sizable investments in senior leadership as well as relationship managers and we'll continue to do so in a calibrated manner going forward.

items.statement: Group PBT margins historically 50-52%, Q1FY27 at ~52%; expected to sustain in FY27 supported by high variable cost structure (70% variable in Wealth Management)
items.quote: If we look at historically and our last few years , our margins have been around the range of 50% to 52%. Q1 of this year is also around 52%. We expect, historically the margins that we had to sustain over the course of current financial year.

items.statement: AMC net flows market share 4.2% vs AUM share 2.9%; SIP flows ₹4,064 crores (+16% YoY), SIP AUM ₹38,643 crores; digital net flows market share improved from ~6% to ~7% YoY
items.quote: Our flow market share continues to be well above our AUM market share, which is 2.9%. In Q1FY27, our SIP flows were strong at ₹4,064 crores, up by 16% YoY with a market share of 4.3%, resulting in an SIP AUM of ₹38,643 crores.

items.statement: Regulatory headwinds for Wealth Management (prop trading changes from July 1) but minimal impact on business model; only minor impact on intraday funding from banks
items.quote: There is no much impact because that is mainly impacting the brokers who are heavy on prop trading. From a liquidity perspective, it's very early to assess the impact because of the volatility in the markets. There is no impact for us on the overall business model, except some change on the intraday funding from the ba

items.statement: Full-year FY27 NIM guidance upgraded to ~5.8% from previous 5.75%
items.quote: But now for the year, our expectation is that we could hit margin closer to 5.8%. So in that sense, we now feel that margin could improve from 5.75% to 5.8%.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 credit cost guidance lowered to 150-160 bps from previous 170-180 bps
items.quote: But on the credit cost guidance also, while we said 170 to 180 basis points in the previous earnings call, we feel now we could land up more with 150 to 160 basis points on credit cost.

items.statement: Targeting full-year FY27 ROA of ~1%
items.quote: That's what we sort of answered on the previous call, that we are gunning for reaching an ROA of about 1% for the year.

items.statement: Opex growth guidance maintained at 13-14% for FY27 with focus on maintaining 500 bps operating jaw
items.quote: Our endeavor would be to maintain that opex leverage, right, which is that 500 basis points delta which we were able to achieve in Q1.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted NIM improved 5 bps QoQ to 5.90% driven by cost of funds reduction
items.quote: If I exclude these two line items from the individual quarters, then the NIM has shown an improvement of 5 basis points and the adjusted numbers would look like 5.85% going up to 5.90%.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 4 bps QoQ to 5.96% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: This improvement was largely contributed by reduction in cost of fund, which further came down from 6% to 5.96%.

items.statement: Loan book grew 20.6% YoY to INR3.05 lakh crore in Q1 FY27 driven by mortgage, vehicle, corporate and consumer loans
items.quote: Individually, if I now talk about loan book, there also we registered a strong growth of 20.6% on a Y-o-Y basis and that book has now crossed INR3 lakh crores to reach about INR3.05 lakh crores.

items.statement: Customer deposits grew 16.6% YoY and 5.3% QoQ to nearly INR3 lakh crore; CASA ratio improved 1% QoQ to 50.8%
items.quote: If I see total deposits, which is customer deposits plus certificate of deposit, then the growth was about 17.7% on a Y-o-Y basis and 5.9% on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: MFI book at INR6,700 crore with 93% CGFMU coverage; targeting 15% YoY MFI book growth in FY27
items.quote: We feel that we could end up or target a book increase of 15% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: NRI deposits at INR25,000 crore (1.7% market share); targeting 2.5% share of FCNR(B) inflows via SBLC structure
items.quote: With respect to FCNR, we feel that through a combination of leverage and the SBLC structure, we are hopeful of garnering a share of about 2.5% or so.

items.statement: Created voluntary contingency provision of INR515 crore for macro/geopolitical/monsoon uncertainties despite healthy asset quality
items.quote: Another point to call with respect to provisions is that we have created a contingency provision of INR515 crores. This is purely I would say voluntary and on a prudent basis considering the evolving macroeconomic and the geopolitical uncertainties and the monsoon related factor.

items.statement: ECL transition impact on capital expected to be neutral; steady-state impact manageable due to EIR benefits
items.quote: In a combination of both, we feel that the impact on capital could be quite neutral at the time of transition. So, that is our current sense as far as ECL is concerned.

items.statement: Technology investment focus on architecture quality over quantum; IT spend at ~9% of opex with modern stack enabling scalable growth
items.quote: It's not about how much you invest; it's about where you invest them. So, I agree we are like 9% there. The thing is that we've built a really good architecture and a good stack and modern stack.

items.statement: PSLC purchase cost ~INR250 crore in FY26; still short on PSL requirements but building organic franchise (INR1-1.2 lakh crore PSL book)
items.quote: Last year we lost about Rs. 250 odd crore. Probably I mean, it depends on how the rates will be for this year, we'll take the numbers as it comes. But we're going to be short, we're going to buy.

items.statement: FY27 disbursement target of INR 65,000 crore and borrowing plan of INR 70,000 crore approved by Board
items.quote: for '27, FY '27, we are planning to have a disbursement of around INR65,000 crores. Last year, we had achieved around INR5,000 crores. On the basis of the INR65,000 crores, Board has approved the borrowing plan also. So, it is around INR70,000 crores.

items.statement: Loan book target of INR 3 lakh crore by 2030 with mid-course review in FY28
items.quote: 2030, we have planned a loan book of INR3 lakh crores, and I'm very sure that we will be achieving that INR 3 lakh crores loan book. But at the same time, in mid of FY '28, we will be reviewing on the basis of the achievements of FY '27.

items.statement: Spread compression due to accelerated growth; expected to vest at 2% by Q3 as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 disbursements capitalize
items.quote: The compression is only account of the accelerated growth within the company. So, we will be vesting at around 2%. Maybe in the third quarter, you will see that all these disbursements, which we had done in Q4 of last FY and the Q1 of this FY, they will be capitalizing and creating that kind of spreads for us.

items.statement: Total sanctioned pipeline outstanding at INR 2.5 lakh crore; INR 60,000 crore sanctioned in Q1 FY27 and INR 1.64 lakh crore in FY26
items.quote: The total sanction outstanding, if you see, it is around INR2.5 lakh crores, which is already there in last quarter only, we had sanctioned more than INR 60,000 crores. Last year, we have sanctioned on INR1.64 lakh crores.

items.statement: Signed MOUs with Gujarat (INR 1 lakh crore+) and Bihar (INR 1 lakh crore+) for urban infra, metro, satellite towns, roads, tourism; Gujarat projects to start sanctioning this quarter
items.quote: we had signed this MOU, which is bagged by a lot of projects which are identified, which includes the infrastructure for the Olympics finally and the metro systems, RRTS also since Gandhinagar, Ahmedabad and the Sabarmati has to join and that kind of infrastructure has to come on.

items.statement: Private sector sanctions of 2 projects worth INR 6,000-7,000 crore in Q1 FY27; no fixed target but focus on bankable PPP projects under Urban Challenge Fund with 50% CGF
items.quote: we have started with the private sector. One project -- two projects rather, we had already sanctioned in Q1 and Q2 -- the part of Q2, I think in Q1, Q1, we have sanctioned 2 projects and amounting to around INR 6,000 crores or so, INR7,000 crores.

items.statement: Gross NPA INR 1,600 crore, Net NPA INR 82 crore; INR 1,100 crore in NCLT (pre-2013) expected to resolve this FY; strategy shifted to mutual resolution with promoters
items.quote: our gross NPA is slightly more than INR 1,600 crores and our net NPA is around INR 82 crores. So out of the INR 1,600 crores, around INR 1,100 crores are at different stages of the NCLT where we are funding these projects way back previous to 2013, and I'm very sure that we will be resolving these assets by -- during t

items.statement: Urban population to double to 80 crore (50% of total) in 20 years; massive urban infra need driven by new cities, metros, industrial corridors, Urban Challenge Fund (INR 1 lakh crore VGF)
items.quote: presently, if it is 40 crores of the urban population, it will be doubled in the next 20 years. So, it will to the extent of 80 crores. So, it is 50% of the total population, which is projected. So, the kind of urban capital, which is required for the country, it is giving a lot of potential.

items.statement: Repayment pipeline of INR 20,000 crore for FY27 (INR 4,000 crore received in Q1, INR 15,000-16,000 crore remaining)
items.quote: total repayment for the year will be approx. 20,000 in the current financial year. Out of that, already INR4,000 plus we have received for the current quarter. So, for coming of the quarters in the current financial year, we will be receiving around INR15,000 crores to INR16,000 crores.

items.statement: Effective tax rate reduced to 20.61% from Board decision to stop creating DTL on special reserves to align with peers
items.quote: tax rate is like 20.61%. Because now earlier we used to create a deferred tax liability on special reserve, which we used to create, which we are required to create for sustaining the long-term financing but to align ourselves in line with the other government sector and private sector, NBFCs, now we have -- the Board

items.statement: No FCNR maturities in FY27/FY28; only USD 200 million maturing in 2028 with higher protection; rest long-term ECBs covered under RBI forex window with full hedging
items.quote: We have a very small portion of FCNR, $200 million, which we -- they are going to mature in 2028. So, we do not foresee any foreign currency losses in the current financial year. And that $200 million, which is going to mature in 2028 is also adequately secured, we have taken higher protections, and we do not foresee a

items.statement: Yield on loans at 8.78% in Q1; strategy to maintain 2% spread by passing borrowing cost changes to borrowers while cutting cost of funds via RBI window, bond retirement, asset monetization
items.quote: yield is around 8.7%. At the same time, our cost of fund is also reducing, and we are continually trying to cut down our cost of funds. So, beyond yield, I can make any statement that we will maintain our spreads and the repeatedly, I am advising that our spreads will be 2%.

items.statement: Management confident of delivering around 20% growth in FY27 subject to market conditions
items.quote: Subject to overall market condition, we remain confident of delivering around 20% growth during the current financial year.

items.statement: PMS AUM at Rs 150 crore end Q1 FY27, targeting Rs 250 crore by FY27 end; AIF launch expected Q3 FY27
items.quote: We launched our PMS in Q1 and at the end of Q1 our PMS AUM and the direct PMS and advisory stands at Rs. 150 crores. That's a very decent number as the PMS was launched in Q1 only and our target by end of financial year anywhere around Rs. 250 odd crores.

items.statement: Initiated CP program with Crisil A1+ rating; progressing with NCD issuance to diversify funding and counter RBI top-desk restrictions
items.quote: To further strengthen our funding profile, we have initiated a commercial paper program backed by the highest short-term rating of Crisil A1+. In addition, we are progressing with the issuance of Non-Convertible Debenture program which will diversify our borrowing sources, optimize funding costs and support growth of o

items.statement: Regulatory headwinds from SEBI derivative rules and RBI top-desk funding norms largely behind; smaller peers face capital challenges
items.quote: We believe major challenges are over now and future seems to be very good for Share India. Every team is very motivated, extremely pulled up.

items.statement: Share India Cred (debt trading) launched Q1 FY27 with Rs 74 crore sales, Rs 1.08 crore EBITDA, Rs 40 lakh PAT
items.quote: Share India Cred was a debt trading company. So, now this company is mainly into dealing debt market products especially NCDs and all. So, the great part is it started operations in Q1 only and it is led by Mr. Keshav Goyal. So, 1st Quarter they have done the sales of around Rs. 74 crores. They have underwritten Rs. 74

items.statement: GIFT City international desk turned positive with ~Rs 2 crore profit in Q1 FY27 after prior losses
items.quote: GIFT City numbers in Q1 were positive. So, around Rs. 2 odd crores. So, that's also a big encouragement for us wherever we were making some small losses and it turned out to be a very good quarter in GIFT City also.

items.statement: Merchant banking completed first main board IPO raising Rs 167 crore at 12x subscription; SME IPO of ~Rs 200 crore in Q1
items.quote: And today when we are speaking, we have just finished our first main board IPO and we raised on Rs. 167 crores. And the overall subscription till now is more than 12 x into this challenging market.

items.statement: Acquired Enshrine (Silverleaf) for up to Rs 45 crore primarily for 18,000 sq ft Mumbai office property valued ~Rs 42 crore
items.quote: See, the basic idea of acquiring this property was to get a new office in Mumbai. And this is located in interface 11, which is the prime area. And the value of property itself is more than Rs. 42 crores.

items.statement: Forecasts 5-5.5% electricity demand growth for next 7-8 years, similar to CEA projections
items.quote: If not 11%, but 5 to 5.5% is what we are forecasting similar to what CEA has forecasted for next 7-8 years

items.statement: Q1 FY27 electricity volume grew 16% YoY to 37.5 billion units
items.quote: For the first quarter of this year, we achieved electricity volume of 37.5 billion units, registering a growth of 16%.

items.statement: Peak demand hit ~271 GW in May and July 2025, up ~12% YoY; energy consumption up 8-9%
items.quote: peak demand was almost about 271 gigawatt in the month of May and even in the month of July it almost touched about 271 gigawatt with about 12% increase in peak demand and 8% to 9% increase in energy consumption

items.statement: India added 58 GW capacity in FY26 (thermal + renewable), total installed capacity 533 GW (275 GW renewable)
items.quote: last year capacity addition of 58 gigawatt across thermal and renewable capacity was done taking India's total installed capacity to 533 gigawatt, out of which 275 gigawatt was the renewable capacity

items.statement: Market coupling in DAM may impact 20-40% of DAM volumes, but DAM is only ~40% of total mix; limited overall business impact expected
items.quote: even if there is an impact, it may be about 20, 30, 40% (in DAM) . So, as far as business is concerned, I do not think it is going to be significant.

items.statement: Carbon credit trading expected to start by Oct 1, 2026 per BEE; final GHG notification issued for 7 sectors
items.quote: BEE has said that they want to start it by 1st of October 2026.

items.statement: Indian Coal Exchange incorporated; rules mandate all coal trade via exchange within 6 months of operations; ~120 MT currently on e-auction platforms
items.quote: today we find that almost about 120 million tonnes of coal is being traded through the e-auction platforms and other marketplaces

items.statement: CEA projects 950 GW installed capacity by 2030 (66% renewable); per capita consumption target 2,000 units by 2030, 4,000 by 2047
items.quote: CEA projects installed capacity of almost about 950 gigawatt by 2030 and out of that almost 66% is going to be renewable

items.statement: Filed applications with CERC for Green RTM, Peak Power Contracts (DAM/RTM), and extending TAM contracts from 3 to 11 months
items.quote: We have already filed an application with the CERC for approval of Green RTM Market, Peak Power Contracts for DAM and RTM, and also for enhancing the Term Ahead Market contracts from 3 months to 11 months.

items.statement: Expects 50 GW of demand shifting potential by FY35 as states move agriculture load to daytime
items.quote: By certain estimate there is 50 gigawatt of additional potential there where shifting can happen and this can be done not in a year, it will take some time by FY’35, we expect this shifting can be done.

items.statement: 80 GW thermal capacity addition in pipeline with 41 GW under construction, 20 GW awarded, 16 GW planning
items.quote: On the thermal side also 80 gigawatt of capacity addition is in the pipeline and 41 gigawatt is already under construction where PPAs have been signed. There is another 20 gigawatt where the contract has been awarded to the suppliers and 16 gigawatt is under various stage of planning.

items.statement: BESS arbitrage remains strong with 545 cycles in FY26 at Rs 4.81/unit average despite outlier year
items.quote: Even after that you can see there are 545 cycles which were possible in the last year . So one cycle 365 days and second cycle also quite a quite a few days so about one and a half times . We can operate one and a half cycle on an average and what sort of arbitrage was available? For every cycle, arbitrage available in

items.statement: Merchant BESS capacity growing: ACME 3,200 MWh, Juniper 500 MWh, Adani 3,400 MWh all standalone merchant
items.quote: ACME has started commission ing 3,200 M wH which is standalone merchant basis, Juniper has done 500 MwH again on a standalone merchant bases and Adani has done 3,400 MwH which are again on a merchant basis.

items.statement: 11-month Long Duration DEEP contract petition filed to capture seasonal demand (Durga Puja, Diwali, Winter)
items.quote: A third contract which is in the pipeline is 11 months (Long Duration) DEEP. Currently it is up to 3 months, but we know that in India there is short-term seasonal requirement which is there.

items.statement: IGX filed DRHP this month, expects listing soon after 40% CAGR to 76.8 MMBtu and Rs 42 Cr profit
items.quote: It reached with CAGR growth of over 40% a volume of 76.8 million MMBtu and reported profit of 42 crores. All entities which are dealing in gas in India or abroad are mainly all around the platform. And the good part is that they filed the DRHP in this month and hopefully (would be) getting listed soon.

items.statement: Carbon trading expected to start in FY27
items.quote: Carbon trading is something which is again in the pipeline and we expect that in FY’27 itself we should start trading in it.

items.statement: Built hot standby for Real-Time market to handle 5-minute bidding window and ensure high availability
items.quote: We have also built a hot standby solution for the Real-Time market which is something that would ensure that we are able to have a much higher availability and reliable solutions that even in a five minute bidding scenario, even if there is a technical outage in one of the channels, the other channel will be able to pr

items.statement: Exchange share of total generation could reach ~25% in next 5-6 years from current ~14-15%
items.quote: We did some estimation on this and what we feel is that almost about 25 percent of the total generation that is the market size, opportunity size, maybe in the next five, six years, it can be that kind of opportunity.

items.statement: BESS price arbitrage opportunity expected to last 3-5 years
items.quote: So, you can do a reasonably good forecasting for 4-5 years. About that, yes, we are reasonably sure but in future also I am sure it will be there.

items.statement: Power demand boom driven by electrification, data centers, EVs, ACs; per capita consumption expected 1.5x by 2032
items.quote: We are banking on the (power) demand boom in the country, electrification is happening, data centers, EV, air conditioners are going to drive the demand. If it is (per capita electricity consumption) going to be 1.5X by 2032, we will have our play here.

items.statement: Coal exchange fees will be higher than current MSTC/M-junction fixed auction fees due to added clearing & settlement value
items.quote: The fees in case of exchanges will be definitely higher than what MSTC and Mjunction are charging.

items.statement: Market coupling cost will be passed to consumers; fee structure and market share impact uncertain pending final regulations
items.quote: There is nothing free. All costs are passed on to the consumer. Directly or indirectly.

items.statement: Top 10 buyers contribute 50-60% of volumes, top 10 sellers ~40%; concentration stable over years with daily 800-900 participants
items.quote: I think the volume contribution is almost about 50-60 percent and top 10 sellers, I think the concentration is less on the sell side. It could be about 40 percent but we have every day almost about eight to nine hundred participants who participate in this market.

items.statement: Targeting INR6,000-6,500 crores disbursement for FY27
items.quote: So, we are looking at anywhere between INR6,000 crores to INR6,500 crores.

items.statement: Maintaining credit cost guidance of 2.5-3% for FY27; net credit cost expected closer to 2%
items.quote: Very much. We are at, as I said, 2.1% for Q1 and the efforts are on to retain that.

items.statement: Opex target ~INR675 crores for FY27 (down from INR760 crores FY26); ~10% increase in FY28
items.quote: So against the last year full opex of about INR760-odd crores. I think we should be more around INR675 crores or so for the full year this year. And next year should be just a 10% increase on that.

items.statement: INR545 crores sanctioned under CGS scheme; INR200 crores utilized; more sanctions in pipeline
items.quote: We managed to garner around INR545 crores of sanction under the credit guarantee scheme, and sanctions are still coming, and there are quite a few sanctions in the pipeline as well.

items.statement: NIM improved to 12.5% from 9.9% QoQ; yield at 24.6% (target 25.25%); marginal cost of borrowing down to 11.3% from 12%
items.quote: With the improving trend in the yield and declining borrowing cost, our NIM improved to 12.5% compared to 9.9% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: CGS borrowing priced at ~10% or slightly above; overall cost of borrowing down to 12.8% from 13.2%
items.quote: Pricing is just about at 10% or a little over 10% because there are sub-10%, there are marginally over 10% as well.

items.statement: Balance rights issue INR200 crores (INR100 cr promoter, INR100 cr others) expected this quarter
items.quote: The balance rights issue money of INR200 crores, INR100 crores from the promoter and the balance INR100 crores from others who participated is expected this quarter, before the end of this quarter.

items.statement: NBFC AUM long-term CAGR target of 20-25% after 1-2 year transition
items.quote: So, our aim is to increase at an CAGR of about 20-25%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target Rs 6,000-8,000 crores in 5 years at 20% CAGR
items.quote: So, if we grow 20%, we will have revenue in five years' time around Rs. 6,000 to Rs. 8,000 crores.

items.statement: NBFC secured book now 75% of AUM, up 5% YoY; yields rising with mix shift
items.quote: So, as you will see, even at the end of quarter-end the secured book constitutes 75% of the AUM, which is slightly higher than the last quarter-ended and even year-on-year, the secured book has grown by 5%.

items.statement: NBFC borrowing cost down 25 bps in Q1; NIM expected to grow gradually
items.quote: So, regarding the interest rate, so basically in the current quarter, we had a reduction in our weighted cost of fund by around 25 basis points.

items.statement: Insurance gross premium Rs 759 crores in Q1, 90% from non-life segment
items.quote: The major segment is our non-life insurance, which contributes approximately 90% of the total premium.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM grew 11.5% to Rs 4,787 crores; 92,129 active SIPs
items.quote: Our mutual fund AUM grew from 4,294 crores as on March '26 to Rs. 4,787 crores as on 30th June, representing a growth of approximately 11.5%.

items.statement: Insurance EBIT moderated due to manpower and distribution investments for reinsurance opportunity
items.quote: The moderated EBIT growth versus revenue reflects investments in distribution capacity and technology infrastructure to support the upcoming reinsurance opportunity following our composite broker upgrade.

items.statement: Stoxkart revenue quadrupled YoY to Rs 20 crores; added 26,000 subscription clients
items.quote: If you compare Q1 2025 to Q1 2026, it contributed around 20 crores. In Q1 2026, we contributed 20 crores in terms of revenue. And as number of clients, we opened around 26,000 clients in the quarter.

items.statement: Gift City business expanding; major player with good prospects
items.quote: Moreover, we are very optimistic about our Gift City businesses. This is expanding. So, in years to come, Gift City is having good prospects. And we are a major player in Gift City.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 26.2% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On a standalone basis, Q1 FY27 operational income stood at Rs. 273.4 crores, up 11.1% YoY, with an EBITDA of Rs. 71.5 crores, at a margin of 26.2%, an expansion of 100 basis points YoY.

items.statement: Expects employee cost growth of 22-24% for full year FY27 including ESOP expenses
items.quote: However, if you look at on a full year basis, including ESOP expenses, we expect that on a full year basis, employee cost growth can be in the range of 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Current quarter commission cost as % of revenue (56.2% standalone) is a steady-state number for projections
items.quote: Broadly, you can because it might depend on the composition between insurance and the mutual fund. But however, I think on a margin basis, probably you can consider this as a good number for your projection purpose.

items.statement: Monthly SIP book increased to INR1,240 crores in July from INR1,203 crores in June; SIP collections stable at INR1,147 crores in June
items.quote: Our monthly SIP book has further increased to around INR1,240 crores when I'm talking to you. This gives us confidence that SIP accretion remains on a healthy trajectory.

items.statement: Net sales resilient at INR3,790 crores in Q1 FY27, up 50% YoY; gaining market share vs industry
items.quote: At the same time, our net sales remained resilient at INR3,790 crores. This represents a healthy 50% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: PMS AUM grew 37% YoY to ~INR1,900 crores; bond distribution income more than doubled YoY; SIF AUM crossed INR500 crores with 1,323 certified distributors
items.quote: Average PMS AUM grew by 37% year-on-year, and now it stands at roughly about INR1,900 crores. And our income from bond distribution business has more than doubled compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Plans to add ~30 new branches in FY27; >12 already operationalized in Q1
items.quote: We plan to add around 30 new branches during the year, of which almost more than 12 branches have already been operationalized during the quarter.

items.statement: Added ~600 distribution partners/month in Q1 FY27 vs 430/month in FY26; driven by existing distributors moving to platform post regulatory changes
items.quote: During the first quarter of current year, which is FY27, we added around 600 partners per month compared to monthly run rate of 430 in FY26.

items.statement: Direct-indirect AUM split roughly 10-90; 10% includes Indus, Karvy, old B2C and iFAST
items.quote: Direct AUM roughly about -- and the direct-indirect split would be roughly about you can say 90-10 kind of a thing. 90% of the AUM is serviced by partners and 10% includes the Indus, Karvy, Prudent's old B2C and iFAST.

items.statement: Positive on SEBI's mutual fund-only PMS at INR25 lakh ticket; evaluating acquisition or own license; no board decision yet
items.quote: But after looking to this INR25 lakh of ticket size and mutual fund only PMS, I think we are also finding it very, very important thing in our system because it might be very, very helpful for us to provide this kind of services to our retail.

items.statement: Treasury book of ~INR650 crores; evaluating value-accretive acquisition opportunities to strengthen distribution platform
items.quote: Finally, with a treasury book of around INR650 crores, we continue to evaluate value-accretive acquisition opportunities that can further strengthen our distribution platform.

items.statement: Current mutual fund yield (~88 bps gross, ~31 bps net) expected to hold for FY27; may decline 1-2 bps over medium term on new business
items.quote: Currently, whatever is the yield on our assets, we believe that this kind of margins would continue in the near future. Of course, over time, with the size of down the commercial will come down, but that is mainly on a new business.

items.statement: Reaffirmed 20% AUM growth guidance for FY27, expecting INR 6,500-6,800 crore disbursements for the year
items.quote: We will be somewhere around INR 6,500 crores to INR 6,800 crores, which will enable us to achieve our growth guidance of 20% very comfortably.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY27 maintained at 1.7%-1.9%, trending toward 1.7%
items.quote: The guidance what we have given for the credit cost for this financial year, the credit cost will be in somewhere between 1.7% to 1.9%. But already the trend is lower than what we have said in the higher side. So you see the trend goes towards 1.7% more likely in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance to fall below 3% in FY27
items.quote: We have also clearly guided you on the gross NPAs, which will fall to sub 3%.

items.statement: Write-offs guided at INR 225-250 crore for FY27, running at ~INR 60 crore per quarter
items.quote: We should be seeing write-offs for the full year at somewhere around INR225 crores to INR 250 crores, which is largely the run rate that we did in the first quarter. We did about INR 60 crores of write-offs in the first quarter.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing expected around 8.5%, with 10-15 bps further compression possible this year assuming no repo hikes
items.quote: My sense is, I think our incremental cost of borrowing should be somewhere around the 8.5% level, which means we still have another 20-30 basis points of compression that can come in the borrowings over the period.

items.statement: Spreads expected to remain flat at current levels for next few quarters assuming no policy rate changes
items.quote: Spread should largely remain flat to current levels for the next few quarters, assuming no policy actions.

items.statement: Target ticket-size mix: 25% at ~INR 3 lakh, 50% at ~INR 5 lakh, 25% at ~INR 10 lakh; average disbursement ticket ~INR 5 lakh
items.quote: We definitely want to operate at 25-50-20, which will be 25% at around INR3 lakh ticket size and 50% around the INR5 lakh ticket size and the other 25% closer to the INR10 lakh ticket size.

items.statement: Energy cost increases and regulatory liquidity decisions flagged as key external risks to monitor
items.quote: One is on the energy cost, which has gone up, which may even go up. Second is on the liquidity front, what the regulator is going to take a call on the price hike.

items.statement: Adequate borrowing lines available; holding INR 1,850 crore liquidity; ADB ECB tranche pending with hedging cost impact
items.quote: We are still holding close to INR 1,850 crores on the balance sheet. So it's still a sizable number. But the focus of the company will clearly be to ensure appropriate cost of funds. But at the same time, we will not compromise on the growth.

items.statement: Guidance for 25 bps opex reduction for FY27 maintained
items.quote: Cost of operations have been calibrated in a downward sloping curve and we continue our guidance of a 25-basis point reduction this year over the 150-basis point reduction we've delivered since listing.

items.statement: Spreads improved 39 bps Q-o-Q to 9.4%; NIMs at 10.6%
items.quote: Spreads, which improved by 39 bps at 9.4% driven by both a lower cost of borrowing and better pricing on the asset side. NIMs moved up by a similar basis point as spreads and stood at 10.6%.

items.statement: Co-origination mix reset to 10% from ~20% due to new RBI norms; expected to return to usual run rate from Q2
items.quote: Following the revised guidelines, the co-origination mix reset to 10%. This has since stabilized and we expect a return to the usual run rate from this quarter onwards.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to remain range-bound at 1.4%-1.5% for next two quarters
items.quote: We are penciling in that it will be range-bound in this current range. So, 1.4% or 1.5%, this is the range that we are looking at for at least next two quarters.

items.statement: Guidance for coming quarter unchanged on all fronts; ROE at 14.7%
items.quote: Our guidance for the coming quarter remains unchanged on all fronts. No surprises there, birds on the badminton court notwithstanding.

items.statement: No new products planned; focus on deepening existing geographies and improving execution in MSME and gold loans
items.quote: We don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new. We will continue doing what we are doing. Hopefully we will do it better than what we have done so far.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at mid-teens for FY27; EBITDA margin expected broadly in line with FY26
items.quote: Overall, we expect the top line to grow in line with the stated guidance of mid -teens. We will continue to invest behind our core brands, super-premium to luxury portfolio and organizational capabilities while maintaining FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY 26.

items.statement: Management indicates potential upside to high-teens revenue growth and 18% EBITDA margin over 2 years
items.quote: I would rather want to step it up from mid -teens, it may go even higher to high teens and an EBITDA margin of 18%.

items.statement: India-UK FTA expected to improve margins by 70-80 bps in FY27 and 130-140 bps in FY28
items.quote: We expect the benefit to flow in second half of the year and would lead to about 70 to 80 basis points improvement in current financial year. For FY28 on a full year basis, it would help us in improving margins by 130 to 140 basis points.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%; like-to-like gross margin 48.4% (up 522 bps) excluding supply chain impact
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 277 basis points to 46%, supported by a favorable input cost environment and early benefits from backward integration despite the temporary impact of global supply chain disruptions.

items.statement: ICONiQ White volume grew 33.8% YoY to 3.1M cases in Q1 FY27; targeting ~15M cases in FY27 vs 10.7M in FY26
items.quote: ICONiQ White is now operating at a meaningful scale supported by domestic market penetration, the defense channel, and an expanding international presence.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment contribution increased to 48.2% of volume and 59.3% of value in Q1 FY27 vs 46.2% and 55.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, the Prestige & Above segment contributed 48.2% of volumes and 59.3% of value compared to 46.2% and 55.8% respectively in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: ABD Maestro luxury portfolio FY26 revenue ~₹40 crore; targeting 2x growth to ~₹80 crore in FY27
items.quote: The turnover that we clocked in FY 26 was top line of ~₹40 crores, which we expect to double in FY27.

items.statement: Global supply chain disruption impacted Q1 FY27 by ₹24 crore; management expects pressure only up to Q2 FY27 with recovery in H2
items.quote: I am extremely optimistic by saying that maximum that we would face pressure up to Q2. Q3 and Q4, we will all bounce back as an industry.

items.statement: Telangana government overdues ~₹400 crore; recent supplies paid on time, legacy overdues being cleared
items.quote: Overdue from Telangana government is approximate ₹400 crores. So right now, what's happening is Telangana is paying us well within agreed timeline for all recent supplies.

items.statement: Price increase dialogue ongoing with Telangana and 1-2 other states; management optimistic on materialization
items.quote: I personally feel that considering the first 2 quarters margin pressure, representations to most state governments that we have given, some state may also consider giving us price increases.

items.statement: Capex program to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within defined framework
items.quote: Our capex program is planned to be funded through internal accruals and debt while maintaining leverage within our defined framework through the investment cycle.

items.statement: Reiterated FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue and 40% EBITDA margins
items.quote: we really remain confident and are happy to reiterate our FY28 outlook of $400 million organic revenue as well as, EBITDA margins of 40%.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin improved significantly due to favorable mix from drug device combination business and H2-heavy base business
items.quote: it's basically the mix which is driving this. You know, the as you see there's a significant improvement in margins which primarily coming from higher contribution from the drug device combination business

items.statement: Demand for semaglutide generics significantly outpaces supply in Canada and India; customer forecasts remain robust
items.quote: The constraint in this market has been supply, not demand. In fact, the demand has been significantly outpacing supply both in the markets where the brand was present or was launching.

items.statement: Line 1 at ~225 sterile days/year at full revenue contribution in Q1; profitability not yet optimal due to upfronted opex for new lines
items.quote: we look at one line at about roughly 225 odd days, sterile days available. And based upon the per day realization for us, I would say that quarter one we had, reached fairly the full contribution which is there per line.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 8-12% YoY for FY27
items.quote: we foresee a growth of about 8% to 12% on a year on year basis on the revenue compared to last year from a growth perspective

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth target of 8-12%
items.quote: These strengths support our medium-term target of delivering revenue growth of 8% to 12%.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 140-160 crores for FY27
items.quote: we will probably maintain the range we have said earlier, about INR 140 crores to INR 160 crores per year of capital expenditure, even in this financial year

items.statement: Bengaluru metal card facility expected operational by end of calendar year 2026
items.quote: We expect the Bengaluru facility to be operational by the end of the calendar year after the necessary regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Won two multi-year PSU bank tenders worth INR 73 crores over tender period
items.quote: In this quarter, we won two multi-year tenders from leading PSU banks, which represent approximately INR 73 crores in revenue over the tender period.

items.statement: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 due to higher material costs
items.quote: Gross margin moderated to 41.7% in Q1 FY27 from 44.5% in Q1 FY26 as cost of materials consumed increased faster than revenue.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 135 bps YoY to 25.1% in Q1 FY27 despite gross margin pressure
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter came in at INR 94 crores with an EBITDA margin of 25.1%, an increase of 135 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: 40-45% of gross margin impact from currency, rest from war-driven commodity/logistics costs
items.quote: maybe 40% to 45% of impact is directly attributable to currency, and the remaining probably is due to the direct impact of the war on the input costs.

items.statement: Actively working with customers on price revisions to protect margins
items.quote: we are actively working with customers on price revisions and taking steps to protect margins and maintain healthy profitability.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 stronger driven by seasonal BFSI pickup and steady communication/IoT momentum
items.quote: given the nature of our business, we expect H2 FY27 to be stronger driven by seasonal pickup in BFSI demand, and steady momentum in the communication and fulfillment businesses, and continued growth in the IoT segment.

items.statement: IoT solutions grew 145% YoY to 18% of revenue; payment solutions 5% YoY at 42%; communication & fulfillment 13% YoY at 40%
items.quote: IoT solutions contributed 18% to total revenue in Q1 FY27 and witnessed a growth of 145% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: IoT business expected to grow ~45% in FY27 and 35-40% in FY28; payment solutions 10-12% CAGR; communication & fulfillment flat
items.quote: So, this year also, we expect it to grow at a similar nature. Probably in the following year, with the base being higher, we haven't really given a visibility on the growth for the following year. So, I think that should be again in the range of 35% to 40% in the following year.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and cost pressures creating near-term headwinds
items.quote: As of now, we operate in a challenging environment impacted by geopolitical uncertainties, currency fluctuations, and cost pressures.

items.statement: SIM card capacity utilization at ~40%; overall capacity utilization 65-70% average, peaks at 85-90%
items.quote: For the SIM card business, Pratik, we were close to around 40% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 357.63 crore as of March 31, 2026, providing visibility beyond 24 months due to 3-5 year contract life cycles.
items.quote: As on 31st March 2026, our order books stood at Rs. 357.63 crores. Since our contracts are 3-5 years in life cycle, these order books provide visibility beyond 24 months.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin improved to 10.5% from 7% in FY25; Q4 FY26 PAT margin improved to 15.1% from 8.7% in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Profit after tax for the year stood at Rs. 24 crores, representing a robust 70% year-on-year growth, while PAT margin improved to 10.5% compared with 7% in previous financial year.

items.statement: See massive opportunities in mining GovTech globally due to critical minerals focus, modernization of legacy systems, and ease-of-doing-business initiatives by state governments and private miners like JSW and Adani.
items.quote: We see massive opportunities coming from the state governments and the ministries across the few countries and we also see tremendous amount of spend being done by the private companies or the public sectors like Steel Authority of India or the Gujarat Mining Development Corporation or Odisha Mining Corporation to that

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs 0.5 per equity share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.5 per equity share for Financial Year 26, subject to shareholders' approval at the forthcoming Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Strategy prioritizes continued investment in technology infrastructure, proprietary platforms, AI/ML capabilities, and skilled workforce for complex digital transformation programs.
items.quote: Looking ahead, our strategy remains focused on four key priorities: 1. Continue investing in strengthening our technology infrastructure and proprietary products and platforms. 2. Further enhance our capability in artificial intelligence and machine learning and other emerging technologies.

items.statement: Mining remains largest vertical; implementing systems across Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Rajasthan, and Kenya; expanding into critical minerals and mineral evacuation globally.
items.quote: Mining remains as one of the largest contributors to us. We develop software for mining for the governments we call it systems like i3MS in Jharkhand, Odisha we have i3MS, we have the similar system implemented in Jharkhand, state of Chhattisgarh, we have done it in state of Bihar in the past, we are doing it right now

items.statement: Revenue seasonality: Q3 and Q4 typically higher due to government spending cycles; Q4 FY26 revenue moderated to Rs 60 crore from Rs 64 crore in Q3 FY26 after exceptional Q2 FY26 order booking.
items.quote: Typically, historically you know because the government processes are such that in the last two quarters only, we have higher revenues. Last year was an exceptional year where in the quarter of Q2 there was an exceptional order booking. This is again coming from some pending things that are there. However, you will see

items.statement: One-time exceptional charge of Rs 2.7 crore recognized in FY26 for statutory impact of new Labor Codes.
items.quote: During the year, the company recognized a one-time exceptional charge of Rs. 2.7 crores towards the statutory impact of new Labor Codes. Excluding this one-time item, our profitability remained robust.
